
## 55. P6-A1 Effect Pipeline and Mana Transaction V0 Product Design Authority

### 55.1 Status and scope

This section is the approved, product-design authority amendment for P6 V0. It closes
the twelve P6-RO1 product-decision groups, freezes the P6 V0 resource bounds, freezes
the P5-to-P6 handoff and P5/P6/P9 ownership boundary, fixes the P6-S1-through-P6-S4
split and P6-G01-through-P6-G09 Definition of Done, and authorizes P6-S1 after this
amendment's remote closure.

For this amendment:

- WORK LAYER = PRODUCT DESIGN;
- PRODUCT-BLOCKING = NO;
- repository delta is this architecture document only;
- the delta is a strict EOF append;
- production source, tests, scripts, Gradle, workflows, resources, codex-spec files,
  ADRs, P5 runtime behavior, and public API remain unchanged;
- P6 implementation, P7+, real Minecraft damage, GameTest, dedicated-server
  qualification, and P6-specific JAR qualification remain not started;
- product authority, not evidence topology or verification recursion, is the only
  subject of this section.

Within the P6 V0 product semantics expressly stated here, this approved scoped
amendment resolves older ambiguity. It does not supersede frozen requirements outside
that scope. It becomes complete only upon this commit's unique exact-SHA, attempt-1,
six-job remote Build Gate success.

### 55.2 P5 completion preservation

P5 remains complete. This amendment neither reopens P5 nor imports its optional
post-completion terminal-auditor work into P6.

The exact P5 deltas in this amendment are:

- P5 admission changed = 0;
- P5 scheduler and order changed = 0;
- P5 budget and breaker changed = 0;
- P5 lease and pin changed = 0;
- P5 reference resolution changed = 0;
- P5 child-publication ownership changed = 0;
- P5 persistence changed = 0;
- P5 public API changed = 0.

P5 terminal QA hardening remains OPTIONAL / NON-BLOCKING. No P6 implementation unit
may own, duplicate, bypass, or redefine a P5 responsibility merely because the
existing package-private handoff is consumed.

### 55.3 P6 formal identity

The formal phase name is:

~~~text
Effect Pipeline and Mana Transaction V0
~~~

P6 requires every gameplay modification within its scope to pass through a typed
request, pure resolution, bounded fixed plan, ordered commit, and explicit result.
Every mana mutation passes through the sole ManaTransactionService.

The canonical P6 flow is:

~~~text
ActionExecutor
-> EffectRequest
-> EffectResolver
-> EffectCommitPlan
-> EffectCommitter
-> EventEmitter / bounded child intent
-> P5 publication
~~~

P6 must not:

- create a second scheduler or queue;
- bypass P5 admission, budget, deadline, cancellation, breaker, or lifecycle gates;
- repin or query the latest skill revision;
- own a P5 queue, slot, lease, child reservation, event ID, or attribution record;
- publish child work directly or recursively execute it;
- create pending work outside P5 ownership;
- implicitly load a chunk or force an entity load;
- create a background worker or cross-thread execution model.

### 55.4 P5 / P6 / P9 responsibility boundary

The responsibility boundary is fixed as follows:

| Owner | V0 responsibilities | Explicit exclusions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P5 | admission, immutable event identity, exact-revision pin and projection, deterministic scheduler order, loaded-only generic reference resolution, execution and pending budgets, cancellation, deadline, breaker, bounded child reservation and sole publication, lifecycle, fault cleanup | effect-specific product semantics, mana truth, mana mutation, concrete P6 result semantics |
| P6 | EffectRequest and DamageEffectRequest semantics, pure effect-specific validation and resolution, bounded fixed EffectCommitPlan, ordered commit state machine, test-double DamageEffectCommitPort, target revalidation contract, rich result/failure/partial/compensation vocabulary, mana truth and ManaTransactionService | P5 state ownership, network, presentation, and real Minecraft damage integration |
| P9 | real Minecraft damage adapter, LivingEntity.hurt or equivalent call, DamageSource and DamageType integration, armor, invulnerability and vanilla/NeoForge damage-event behavior, playable projectile and hit pipeline | redefining P5 admission or P6 transaction semantics |

Before P9, P6 production composition uses UNAVAILABLE_DAMAGE_COMMIT_PORT. Its only
closed expected outcome is COMMIT_PORT_UNAVAILABLE. It must not pretend that damage
occurred, modify the world, or fall back implicitly to a vanilla damage API.

The concrete world-facing integration is therefore:

~~~text
P9 REAL-DAMAGE VERTICAL SLICE
~~~

### 55.5 P5-to-P6 handoff

The sole composition entry remains the existing synchronous, package-private
RuntimeExecutionPort:

~~~java
RuntimeExecutionBatch execute(
    RuntimeEvent event,
    RuntimeExecutionContext context);
~~~

P6-S4 adds one opaque, package-private, call-scoped RuntimeExecutionGuard component
to RuntimeExecutionContext. P5 owns that guard and its cancellation/deadline truth.
Its read-only check returns exactly ALLOWED, CANCELLED, or DEADLINE_EXCEEDED from the
current P5 event/slot state and P5 tick coordinate. P6 may invoke it only at the ten
safe points fixed below; it cannot cancel, reschedule, mutate, or otherwise observe a
P5 slot. The guard is synchronous, is not a background callback, and must not be
retained after the port call. This package-private handoff addition changes no P5
public API, admission, order, budget, or lifecycle semantics.

P6-S4 supplies one package-private final adapter in the root
com.yo1no.gramarye package. The adapter:

1. receives the already-admitted RuntimeEvent and call-scoped context;
2. consumes P5's exact immutable validated definition, node, and typed action;
3. invokes the typed ActionExecutor;
4. invokes the P6 effect and mana pipeline;
5. maps the rich P6 result to the existing P5 transport outcome;
6. maps children from successful steps into one bounded RuntimeChildPlan;
7. returns, after which P5 alone validates and publishes child work.

P6 does not re-resolve the definition, query latest, repin, allocate an event ID,
mutate the child reservation, or reach a P5 queue or slot.

The adapter and all P6 operations have cross-call retention zero. They must not retain
RuntimeExecutionContext, MinecraftServer, ServerLevel, Entity, Player, a revision
lease, child reservation, transaction receipt, commit plan, trace, or any other
operation object after return.

### 55.6 Typed ActionExecutor authority

P6 V0 uses a package-private typed ActionExecutor abstraction. Its input is the
validated typed action representation already selected by the exact P5 node. Its
output contains at most one EffectRequest.

For a supported action, an absent or null request is REJECTED / INVALID_REQUEST with
zero mana and world mutation. A normal accepted ActionExecutor result therefore
contains exactly one request while preserving the absolute maximum of one.

ActionExecutor must not:

- use generic Object, raw types, reflection, or service-loader discovery;
- modify world or mana;
- enqueue, schedule, publish, or recursively execute child work;
- look up a latest revision or retain a call-scoped P5 value.

Dispatch uses the ResourceLocation registry key of the current ActionType<?> obtained
from the formal action registry. It never uses a Java class name, descriptor-object
identity, payload shape, or reflection as the dispatch identity. Choosing the Java
member name that reads the committed registry key does not reopen product design. The
executor registry is immutable after server composition, duplicate registration
fails fast, and a missing executor returns UNSUPPORTED_ACTION. Runtime-reloadable
executor registration is unsupported in V0.

P6 V0 public/protected Action execution API delta is zero. Third-party integration is
deferred beyond P6 V0.

### 55.7 EffectRequest vocabulary

EffectRequest is an immutable, typed, package-private product value. One P6 execution
accepts at most one request. A request carries only bounded typed or stable-reference
data required by its effect; it carries no Entity, Level, MinecraftServer,
Attachment instance, mutable collection, arbitrary map, free-form payload, raw type,
or generic Object.

ActionExecutor is the only Action-layer producer of an EffectRequest. Request
construction validates nullability, type, stable identity, target cardinality,
effect-specific scalar bounds, and compensation policy before resolution. An invalid
request returns REJECTED / INVALID_REQUEST with zero mana and world mutation.

The resolver consumes a request plus the exact call-scoped P5 view. It performs no
world or mana mutation and creates no pending work.

### 55.8 DamageEffectRequest V0

DamageEffectRequest is the first P6 request. It is immutable, non-null, has exactly
one target, and contains at least:

- request identity and source-event identity;
- one typed stable target reference;
- effect magnitude;
- mana cost;
- CompensationPolicy.

Effect magnitude uses long abstract effect units with the inclusive range:

~~~text
1 <= magnitude <= 1_000_000
~~~

The bound is MAX_EFFECT_MAGNITUDE = 1_000_000L. The magnitude is not Minecraft HP or
heart units. P9 owns conversion to concrete damage, rounding, DamageSource and
DamageType selection, and vanilla/NeoForge damage-event interaction.

Mana cost uses long and the inclusive request range zero through
MAX_MANA_OPERATION_AMOUNT. Zero means no mana transaction; a positive cost is a
single DEBIT request and must satisfy the mutation-amount bound.

DamageEffectRequest contains no Entity, Level, arbitrary tag, map, object payload, or
unbounded collection.

### 55.9 Pure resolver and bounded commit plan

EffectResolver is pure and non-mutating. It validates request shape, source and target
semantics, dimension, effect-specific validity, compensation policy, all P6 structural
bounds, and the supplied P5 child capacity before mana debit or world mutation.
Generic loaded-only lookup remains P5-owned; P6 performs the effect-specific
revalidation defined in Section 55.16.

An accepted resolution yields an immutable EffectCommitPlan with declared list order,
contiguous zero-based step indexes, at most eight commit steps, and no hidden,
deferred, or dynamically appended step. An accepted DamageEffectRequest plan contains
at least one primary step; an empty plan is REJECTED / INVALID_REQUEST before debit.

The plan declares a nonnegative integer maximum child-intent and
primary-world-mutation contribution for every step. Construction uses exact checked
addition and rejects the aggregate before debit if it could exceed either the supplied
P5 child capacity or the P6 world-mutation bound. Actual contributions are
nonnegative, cannot exceed the corresponding declaration, and successful-step child
intents form an ordered subset of the prevalidated potential. Consequently the
return-time child check confirms a prevalidated bound rather than discovering new
product work after mutation.

The plan and its collections use immutable copies. It contains no live Minecraft
object, callback, future, lambda that captures a live object, queue handle, or
cross-call state.

Exactly one injected commit seam exists in P6 V0: DamageEffectCommitPort. There is no
parallel generic commit-port registry or second commit seam. Production uses the
unavailable implementation until P9.

### 55.10 EffectStepOutcome

EffectStepOutcome is the closed three-case vocabulary:

- APPLIED: the planned primary mutation succeeded, successful-step count increases
  by one, the outcome reports a positive actual primary-mutation contribution no
  greater than the declared maximum, and primary mutation count increases by that
  actual contribution;
- NOT_APPLIED: the step guarantees that it performed no world mutation and returns a
  closed expected failure; its actual primary-mutation contribution is zero;
- APPLIED_WITH_FAILURE: at least one planned non-rollback mutation occurred, so the
  execution has primary mutation and terminates as partial/failure without refund.
  Its actual mutation contribution is positive and no greater than the step's
  declared checked maximum.

The committer executes in declared order. It does not skip, reorder, retry, or
continue after the first non-APPLIED outcome. It never rolls back a successful world
step and never automatically resubmits the plan.

### 55.11 Result and failure vocabulary

EffectExecutionResult is a closed sealed terminal vocabulary with exactly:

- SUCCEEDED;
- REJECTED;
- FAILED;
- PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED;
- COMPENSATED;
- COMPENSATION_FAILED.

SUCCEEDED means every executed primary step returned APPLIED. Any successful mana
debit remains committed, and child intents come only from successful steps.

REJECTED occurs before primary commit and guarantees mana mutation zero and world
mutation zero. Its closed V0 reasons are:

- UNSUPPORTED_ACTION;
- INVALID_REQUEST;
- INVALID_TARGET;
- TARGET_UNAVAILABLE;
- INSUFFICIENT_MANA;
- MANA_STATE_UNAVAILABLE;
- BOUND_EXCEEDED;
- CANCELLED;
- DEADLINE_EXCEEDED;
- COMMIT_PORT_UNAVAILABLE.

WRONG_THREAD is not a gameplay rejection. It is the typed invariant rejection of a
mutable-service entry and guarantees zero read, write, receipt, trace, and world
access at that entry.

FAILED means primary mutation count zero and either no mana debit occurred or no
refund is required. It represents a closed expected commit failure.

PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED means primary mutation count is greater than zero and a later
step has a closed expected non-success. Successful mutation remains, later steps do
not run, no rollback or refund occurs, and children come only from successful steps.

COMPENSATED means a debit succeeded, primary mutation count is zero, a closed
expected primary failure occurred, and the one permitted refund succeeded.

COMPENSATION_FAILED means a debit succeeded, primary mutation count is zero, a
closed expected primary failure occurred, and the one permitted refund returned a
closed expected failure. It is not retried or reported as success.

EffectFailureReason is a closed V0 category vocabulary:

- PRIMARY_STEP_NOT_APPLIED;
- PRIMARY_STEP_APPLIED_WITH_FAILURE;
- EXECUTION_CANCELLED;
- EXECUTION_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED;
- COMPENSATION_REFUND_FAILED.

These five categories are the complete failure-reason surface; there is no nested or
extensible originating-reason vocabulary. NOT_APPLIED maps to
PRIMARY_STEP_NOT_APPLIED, APPLIED_WITH_FAILURE maps to
PRIMARY_STEP_APPLIED_WITH_FAILURE, guard cancellation/deadline map to their matching
categories, and a closed refund failure maps to COMPENSATION_REFUND_FAILED. A reason
carries only the step index or NOT_APPLICABLE. It is never a free-form message,
Throwable, generic Object, or mutable payload.

### 55.12 P5 transport mapping

The P6-to-P5 transport mapping is fixed:

| P6 terminal | P5 RuntimePortOutcome | RuntimeChildPlan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SUCCEEDED | Completed | children from successful steps only |
| PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED | Completed | children from successful steps only |
| REJECTED | Completed | empty |
| FAILED | Completed | empty |
| COMPENSATED | Completed | empty |
| COMPENSATION_FAILED | no returned batch | no publication |

COMPENSATION_FAILED makes the root adapter throw the package-private
P6ExecutionInvariantException. That exception contains only closed reason and receipt
identities; it contains no live object, Throwable field, free-form payload, or
operation graph. P5 then applies its existing runtime-fault and cleanup policy.

An unexpected RuntimeException or Error is never caught and translated into a
gameplay result, P5 reject reason, or new exception. The identical object propagates
to P5. The adapter does not retry, replace, suppress, or wrap it.

Existing P5 RuntimePortOutcome rejection reasons and P5 kernel semantics remain
unchanged. P6's ordinary closed product outcomes are handled completion results, not
new P5 scheduler rejection families.

### 55.13 Compensation policy and ordered state machine

CompensationPolicy has exactly one P6 V0 value:

~~~text
REFUND_IF_NO_PRIMARY_MUTATION
~~~

One execution follows this order:

1. invoke the P5-owned RuntimeExecutionGuard at execution entry;
2. validate the request;
3. validate every structural, child-demand, mutation-demand, trace, magnitude, and
   mana bound;
4. resolve the target only from P5's loaded call-scoped view;
5. revalidate target existence, loaded state, dimension, validity, and commit-port
   acceptance;
6. invoke the guard immediately before the
   debit/primary boundary;
7. if mana cost is greater than zero, execute DEBIT;
8. before each primary step, invoke the guard and then execute in declared order;
9. stop after the first non-APPLIED step;
10. derive the provisional primary outcome and refund eligibility from debit state,
    primary mutation count, guard state, and the closed step outcome;
11. if and only if the refund predicate holds, attempt exactly one REFUND;
12. after the refund attempt, construct and return the final immutable terminal
    result, bounded trace, and bounded successful-step child intent; P5 alone then
    decides publication.

The refund predicate is:

~~~text
debit succeeded
AND primary mutation count = 0
AND terminal failure is a closed expected outcome
~~~

There is no refund after any primary mutation, partial success,
APPLIED_WITH_FAILURE, unexpected RuntimeException, unexpected Error, or uncertain
mutation state. No world step is rolled back. Neither the plan nor compensation is
automatically retried.

A cancellation/deadline result before debit is REJECTED. If debit has occurred but
no primary mutation has occurred, a later closed cancellation/deadline failure uses
the compensation policy. If primary mutation count is greater than zero, the same
pre-step failure produces PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED and no refund.

### 55.14 Mana truth and player Attachment

The sole persistent player mana truth is the dedicated Attachment:

~~~text
ResourceLocation = gramarye:player_mana
schema_version = 0
fields = exactly schema_version, balance
~~~

The V0 serialized root is a compound. schema_version is a signed 32-bit integer field
whose only accepted V0 value is zero; balance is a signed 64-bit long field. The
current schema accepts exactly those two logical and physical fields. A missing field,
unknown field, wrong scalar type, unsupported schema version, invalid root, or
out-of-range balance returns MANA_STATE_UNAVAILABLE. It does not silently reset,
partially decode, or perform mana mutation.

Mana is represented by long integer mana units with the inclusive absolute range:

~~~text
0 <= balance <= 1_000_000_000
MAX_MANA_VALUE = 1_000_000_000L
~~~

The default new-player balance is zero. Mana regeneration and per-player gameplay
capacity/progression are outside P6 V0; the absolute cap is only the representation,
overflow-safety, corruption-rejection, and transaction bound.

Lifecycle is fixed:

- login/load reads the dedicated Attachment;
- logout/save uses the Attachment lifecycle;
- death clone copies balance exactly;
- non-death clone copies balance exactly;
- dimension travel does not create another truth;
- invalid schema, type, or range makes mana state unavailable without mutation.

Mana must not be stored in player_skills, P5 runtime or event state, the definition
store, a diagnostics collection, or a transaction journal. The Attachment persists
no reservation, pending debit, refund token, receipt list, journal, trace, Throwable,
or live Minecraft object.

### 55.15 ManaTransaction V0

ManaTransactionService is the only mana mutation authority. V0 supports exactly
DEBIT, CREDIT, and REFUND, with one account per operation.

The closed executable V0 ManaReason vocabulary is:

| ManaReason | Permitted operation |
| --- | --- |
| SKILL_COST | DEBIT |
| ITEM_RECOVERY | CREDIT |
| ADMIN_ADJUSTMENT | DEBIT or CREDIT |
| COMPENSATION_REFUND | REFUND |

Natural regeneration is outside P6 V0. Share-out/share-in reasons and operations are
deferred with multi-account transfer. A reason/operation mismatch returns
INVALID_TRANSACTION_STATE before mutation.

V0 does not support transfer, multi-account atomic transaction, reservation, hold,
escrow, cross-tick transaction, persistent journal, automatic retry, or batch account
mutation.

Amount uses long and the inclusive mutation range:

~~~text
1 <= amount <= 1_000_000_000
MAX_MANA_OPERATION_AMOUNT = 1_000_000_000L
~~~

Zero mana cost does not call ManaTransactionService, mutate mana, or create a
zero-amount receipt. Arithmetic is exact and checked. Negative balances, a result
above MAX_MANA_VALUE, and arithmetic overflow are forbidden.

The closed expected transaction rejection vocabulary is:

- INSUFFICIENT_MANA;
- BALANCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED;
- INVALID_AMOUNT;
- MANA_STATE_UNAVAILABLE;
- WRONG_THREAD;
- ALREADY_REFUNDED;
- RECEIPT_ACCOUNT_MISMATCH;
- INVALID_TRANSACTION_STATE.

A mutation receipt is package-private, call-scoped, and bound to one stable account
identity. It records operation kind, ManaReason, amount, before, and after. It retains
no Player, Entity, Attachment owner, or mutable collection. A debit receipt may be
refunded at most once, only to the same account, and only for exactly the original
debit amount. A second refund returns ALREADY_REFUNDED; mismatched account returns
RECEIPT_ACCOUNT_MISMATCH. A receipt never crosses a P6 invocation.

Each P6 effect execution performs at most two mana mutations. The only legal
effect-execution sequences are DEBIT or DEBIT followed by REFUND. Direct CREDIT is a
standalone service operation and cannot be mixed with a DEBIT in the same effect
execution.

### 55.16 Threading and world access

Every P6 V0 product execution is synchronous and server-logic-thread-only. No worker
Thread, Executor, ExecutorService, CompletableFuture, Future, ForkJoin facility,
parallel stream, ThreadLocal, background callback, off-thread world preparation, or
cross-thread receipt handoff is permitted.

Pure P6-S1 values and functions have no thread dependency, Minecraft import, or
NeoForge import. The actual P6 execution entry and every account read or mutation are
server-thread confined.

Before any account read or write, mutable ManaTransactionService validates thread
authority. WRONG_THREAD yields:

~~~text
account reads = 0
account writes = 0
receipt creation = 0
trace mutation = 0
world access = 0
~~~

P6 uses only P5's loaded-only call-scoped reference view. It never queries latest,
loads a chunk, forces an entity load, or retains an Entity or Level. Immediately
before a commit attempt it revalidates that the target exists, remains loaded, is in
the expected dimension, remains valid, and is accepted by the damage commit port.

A lost, unloaded, moved, invalid, or no-longer-accepted target produces
NOT_APPLIED / TARGET_UNAVAILABLE. If no other primary mutation occurred, the
compensation predicate governs an already-completed debit.

### 55.17 Determinism and ordering

P6 inherits P5 event execution order and creates no new global ordering system.
Within one execution:

- request count is one;
- target count is one;
- the plan executes in declared list order;
- step indexes start at zero and are contiguous;
- execution stops at the first non-APPLIED outcome;
- unordered Set or Map iteration cannot affect a result;
- trace sequence follows execution and step order;
- child intents follow successful-step order;
- mana debit precedes the first primary step;
- refund precedes final terminal-result construction and return;
- P5 publishes children only after P6 returns;
- gameplay randomness count is zero.

Simultaneous interactions observe the deterministic server-thread order supplied by
P5 and revalidate current live state. P6 does not create a competing same-target
arbiter.

### 55.18 Trace contract

EffectTrace is immutable, result-owned, call-scoped, and in fixed execution order. It
uses List.copyOf or equivalent immutable copying, has at most 32 entries, and is not
stored in an Attachment or retained across events.

Each trace entry contains only bounded scalar or typed data:

- sequence;
- stage enum;
- step index or NOT_APPLICABLE;
- result-code enum;
- stable request or target reference, if already available;
- mana amount before/after or NOT_APPLICABLE;
- child count;
- closed reason enum.

Trace must not contain an arbitrary message, stack trace, Throwable, Entity, Level,
MinecraftServer, Attachment instance, mutable collection, or generic Object payload.

The closed V0 trace-stage vocabulary is exactly:

- REQUEST_VALIDATED;
- TARGET_RESOLVED;
- MANA_DEBITED;
- STEP_APPLIED;
- STEP_NOT_APPLIED;
- STEP_APPLIED_WITH_FAILURE;
- REFUND_APPLIED;
- REFUND_FAILED;
- TERMINAL_REJECTED;
- TERMINAL_SUCCEEDED;
- TERMINAL_FAILED;
- TERMINAL_PARTIAL;
- TERMINAL_COMPENSATED;
- TERMINAL_COMPENSATION_FAILED.

Every append validates remaining trace capacity first. All potential trace demand is
bounded by plan construction before debit, so BOUND_EXCEEDED remains a pre-mutation
product rejection.

### 55.19 Exact numeric bounds

P6 V0 freezes these product bounds:

| Constant or resource | Exact bound |
| --- | ---: |
| MAX_EFFECT_REQUESTS_PER_EXECUTION | 1 |
| MAX_TARGETS_PER_REQUEST | 1 |
| MAX_COMMIT_STEPS_PER_PLAN | 8 |
| MAX_PRIMARY_WORLD_MUTATIONS_PER_EXECUTION | 8 |
| MAX_MANA_MUTATIONS_PER_EXECUTION | 2 |
| MAX_TRACE_ENTRIES | 32 |
| MAX_EFFECT_MAGNITUDE | 1_000_000L |
| MAX_MANA_VALUE | 1_000_000_000L |
| MAX_MANA_OPERATION_AMOUNT | 1_000_000_000L |
| MAX_DEADLINE_CHECKS_PER_EXECUTION | 10 |

Child intents are bounded by:

~~~text
min(
    P5 supplied remaining child budget,
    P5 hard maximum 32
)
~~~

P6 has no additional child queue. Plan construction records each step's maximum child
intent and primary-world-mutation contribution as a nonnegative integer, uses exact
checked addition, and rejects unless both aggregate demands fit the applicable limits.
A valid committer cannot perform an unplanned mutation, exceed a declared maximum, or
emit an undeclared child. Any late actual-over-declared condition is a programming
contract breach that throws P6ExecutionInvariantException and cannot be mislabeled as
a zero-mutation BOUND_EXCEEDED product rejection.

Every structural bound is checked before debit. Step count is checked during plan
construction; target count during request construction and resolution; trace demand,
child demand, and mutation demand during plan construction and again at their use
points; mana amount before service mutation; and arithmetic overflow before state
write.

A product-input bound violation is REJECTED / BOUND_EXCEEDED and guarantees mana
mutation zero and world mutation zero.

P6 adds no wall-clock timeout. It performs one inherited cancellation/deadline check
at entry, one before the debit/primary boundary, and one before each of at most eight
steps:

~~~text
1 + 1 + 8 = 10
~~~

P6 does not wait across ticks, sleep, block, or poll a future. Cross-call retained P6
operation objects equal zero.

### 55.20 Persistence, reload, stop, and crash

A P6 operation completes within one synchronous call and does not cross a tick. P6
does not persist an execution, plan, receipt, trace, pending compensation, or
operation result.

The only P6 persistent state is the gramarye:player_mana Attachment balance. P6 V0
creates no journal, reservation file, crash-recovery transaction, pending refund
queue, retry queue, global mana-account registry, or cross-player transfer state.

On datapack reload, P5's exact-revision lease preserves the current immutable
definition. An in-flight operation does not read latest, and the P6 ActionExecutor
registry does not reload. P6 V0 reload work is zero.

An in-flight transaction cannot outlive its method terminal. Server stop performs no
P6 global transaction cleanup and traverses no pending P6 operation because the
retained count is zero. The existing Attachment save lifecycle owns persisted balance.

After a process crash, P6 promises neither world rollback nor journal recovery of an
interrupted debit or refund. There is no persistent in-flight transaction; only a
completed Attachment mutation may be persisted by the normal platform save lifecycle.

### 55.21 API visibility

P6 V0 public/protected API delta is zero. The following are package-private:

- EffectPipeline;
- EffectResolver;
- EffectCommitter;
- EffectCommitPlan;
- EffectStep;
- ActionExecutor;
- ActionExecutorRegistry;
- EffectExecutionGuard;
- RuntimeExecutionGuard;
- ManaTransactionService;
- mana account, receipt, and transaction objects;
- the root-package P5 adapter;
- DamageEffectCommitPort and its test implementation;
- trace implementation.

Only already-existing typed IDs and definition types required by higher authority may
remain public. P6 adds no public mutable runtime surface.

P6 must not expose a mutable mana account, Attachment handle, transaction receipt,
commit plan, RuntimeExecutionContext, P5 queue, slot, lease, live Minecraft object,
generic executor registration, or bypass around P5 admission and budget.

Product values, the P5 integration adapter, test seam, and implementation detail
remain distinct. A test seam does not become a public integration API.

### 55.22 V0 randomness prohibition

P6 V0 randomness is NONE. Product and test code in P6 V0 must not use Random,
RandomSource, ThreadLocalRandom, Math.random, unordered pseudo-random iteration, or
an implicit platform random source.

A future random effect requires its owning gameplay phase to establish a seed owner,
bounded draw contract, and deterministic replay/order policy. P6 V0 reserves no seed
state and introduces no random API.

## 56. P6-A1.2 Closed Public Mana Attachment Definition Bridge and Registration Ownership Reconciliation

This section is the approved scoped amendment for P6-S2-R3. It resolves only the
Java package boundary between the existing player Attachment registration owner and
the P6 mana Attachment definition. It does not reopen any other P6-A1 decision or
authorize P6-S3.

### 56.1 Historical conflict

The historical P6-S2 implementation commit
`14b0d07aadef67c248a26648ca344bcba7f4150d` passed its local qualification but
failed remote Build run `33536429108`, attempt 1, in the P4-C memory gate. The
failed tree registered `player_skills` through `PlayerSkillAttachments` and
`player_mana` through `ManaAttachments`, while the inherited P4-C contract
required one Attachment registry-mutation owner.

P6-S2-R1 and P6-S2-R2 stopped before edit because a package-private-only bridge could
not cross the Java package boundary without exposing an unauthorized type or moving
unrelated domain ownership. Those stops and the historical failed commit remain
preserved.

### 56.2 Java package-visibility boundary

`PlayerSkillAttachments` is in `magic.definition.player`.
`ManaState`, `ManaAttachmentSerializer`, `ManaLifecycle`, and the typed
`AttachmentType<ManaState>` definition are package-private in
`magic.runtime.mana`. Java therefore does not permit the player package to
construct or name the typed mana definition directly.

Raw types, `Object`, unchecked casts, reflection, dynamic registry lookup, and a
public `ManaState` or transaction facade are not acceptable ways around this
boundary. A definition-only wildcard bridge is the smallest type-safe connection.

### 56.3 Rejected co-location model

Moving the mana definition, serializer, state, transaction service, or lifecycle
copy logic into the player-definition package is rejected. It would conflate the
independent `player_skills` and `player_mana` data categories, disturb the
single-truth boundary, and broaden the P4 player-definition owner beyond its
composition role.

Moving the player Attachment registration owner into the mana package is also
rejected. `PlayerSkillAttachments` remains the one platform registry-mutation
owner for both permanent player Attachment definitions.

### 56.4 Exact public definition bridge exception

The P6 V0 public/protected API rule is narrowed as follows:

~~~text
public/protected mutable runtime API delta = 0
public/protected transaction/account/state API delta = 0
authorized cross-package immutable definition bridge = exact 1
~~~

The sole exception is:

~~~text
package = com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.runtime.mana
type = public final class ManaAttachmentDefinitionBridge
constructor = private
~~~

This class is a Java package-wiring bridge, not a stable third-party integration API.

### 56.5 Exact bridge surface

The bridge has exactly these two public members:

~~~java
public static ResourceLocation attachmentId()
public static AttachmentType<?> attachmentType()
~~~

`attachmentId()` is nonnull and always equals `gramarye:player_mana`.
`attachmentType()` is nonnull and always returns the same immutable typed
definition instance that the mana package uses internally and the registry owner
submits.

The bridge has no public field, public constructor, public nested type, instance
method, generic public method, mutable static state, cache, event annotation, event
handler, registry mutation, builder, serializer, copy-policy configuration,
`getData`, `setData`, player read, transaction operation, account handle,
default-state factory, cast, or unwrap operation. No public signature names
`ManaState`.

### 56.6 Registration, definition, access, and lifecycle taxonomy

The four surfaces are distinct:

- registry mutation is the `DeferredRegister` entry and event-bus registration
  owned by `PlayerSkillAttachments`;
- typed definition is the package-private `AttachmentType<ManaState>`, default
  supplier, serializer, death-copy flag, and custom copy configuration retained by
  `ManaAttachments`;
- live access is the package-private `ManaAttachments.state` and
  `ManaAttachments.replace` facade used by the mana account adapter;
- lifecycle semantics are the pure exact-state copy performed by
  `ManaLifecycle`.

`copyOnDeath()` and `copyHandler(ManaLifecycle::copy)` configure the immutable
typed definition. They are not a second registry-mutation owner. The sole registry
owner is responsible for submitting that already complete definition.

### 56.7 Sole registry-mutation owner

`PlayerSkillAttachments` is the exact one Attachment registry-mutation owner. Its
single `DeferredRegister<AttachmentType<?>>` owns exactly one `player_skills`
entry and exactly one `player_mana` entry, then registers that one deferred
register on the mod event bus exactly once.

The mana entry obtains its exact ID and immutable definition through
`ManaAttachmentDefinitionBridge.attachmentId()` and
`ManaAttachmentDefinitionBridge.attachmentType()`. The player package does not
name `ManaState`, read or write mana, hold a mana balance, or create a second
persistent truth.

### 56.8 Retained ManaAttachments role

`ManaAttachments` remains package-private and retains:

- the exact `gramarye:player_mana` identity source;
- the strict serializer and schema;
- the fresh-default factory;
- the exact package-private typed definition;
- the package-private typed `getData` and `setData` facade;
- AVAILABLE and UNAVAILABLE state semantics;
- the custom pure lifecycle-copy configuration.

It is not an event subscriber, has no `RegisterEvent` handler, performs no platform
registry call, owns no `DeferredRegister`, and is not a second registry-mutation
owner. Its typed copy configuration does not independently submit or register a
definition.

### 56.9 GameTest inventory continuity

The pre-P6-S2 production baseline remains exactly 12 GameTests:

- `PlatformGameTests`: 4;
- `PlayerSkillAttachmentGameTests`: 2;
- `SkillSavedDataLifecycleGameTests`: 1;
- `SkillSubmissionRecoveryGameTests`: 3;
- `SkillDefinitionSubmissionGameTests`: 2.

`ManaLifecycleGameTests` contributes exactly seven unchanged P6-S2 GameTests.
Therefore the production inventory is:

~~~text
baseline 12 + P6-S2 7 = total 19
~~~

No unit-test or GameTest method is added, removed, or renamed by this reconciliation.

### 56.10 Direct-consumer synchronization

Every direct P4-C, P4-D, and P4-E source test or verifier that consumes Attachment
registry ownership, public-surface, exact-path, live-access, or production-GameTest
counts must use this taxonomy and the exact `12 / 7 / 19` arithmetic. Exact
allowlists may name only the actual bridge, owner, definition/access, test, script,
and this architecture path.

Package wildcards, filename-prefix exemptions, and blanket runtime-mana exemptions
remain forbidden. Workflow and Gradle topology do not change because they already
forward to the affected direct verifiers.

### 56.11 Public API risk containment

An external caller receiving `AttachmentType<?>` cannot obtain typed
`ManaState`, a player or account handle, a serializer, a default-state factory, a
transaction service, or any `getData` or `setData` operation from the bridge.
All mutable runtime and transaction surfaces remain package-private.

The bridge cannot register a second definition, mutate registry state, access a
player, create an Attachment value, or bypass `ManaTransactionService`. Its
wildcard return is intentional and prevents the package-private state type from
appearing in the public signature.

### 56.12 Supersession boundary

This section supersedes §55 only where the earlier text required an absolute

Attachment definition handle, described P6-S2 as having no public integration API,

The replacement is exact one immutable definition-only bridge, exact one registry

bounds, product decisions, exclusions, and P6-G01 through P6-G09 remain unchanged.

### 56.13 Unchanged mana and P5 semantics

This reconciliation changes no mana resource ID, persistent schema, numeric range,

## 57. P6-A1.3 Capability-Gated P6 Execution Bridge Product Authority

### 57.1 Status and Scope

This section is the approved scoped P6-A1.3 product-design amendment. Its work layer
is PRODUCT DESIGN and it is not product-blocking. It resolves only the confirmed Java
package-visibility conflict that prevented the P6-S4 adapter from connecting the
existing P5 execution seam to the completed P6-S1, P6-S2, and P6-S3 cores.

This amendment is documentation-only and is appended at the prior exact EOF. It
freezes the cross-package callable surface but does not add Java source, install a
production adapter, compose P6 execution, or begin P6-S4-R1. P6-A1.3 becomes complete
only when this documentation commit receives one unique exact-SHA, attempt-1 Build
run in which all six existing jobs complete successfully.

The only new product decision is:

~~~text
CAPABILITY-GATED CLOSED PUBLIC EXECUTION BRIDGE
~~~

Effect, mana, transaction, compensation, P5 scheduling, child-publication, numeric
bound, and no-real-damage decisions remain closed.

### 57.2 Confirmed Package-Private Composition Conflict

The existing P5 handoff is a package-private island in `com.yo1no.gramarye`. It
contains `RuntimeExecutionPort`, `RuntimeEvent`, `RuntimeExecutionContext`,
`RuntimeExecutionBatch`, `RuntimePortOutcome`, and `RuntimeChildPlan`, together with
the P5-owned package-private `RuntimeExecutionGuard` addition authorized by §55.5.
The required root-package adapter can name these types.

The completed P6-S1, P6-S2, and P6-S3 orchestration is a separate package-private
island in `com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.runtime.mana`. It includes
`ActionDamageTransactionEngine`, `DamageActionInvocation`, `ActionExecutorRegistry`,
the effect vocabulary and engine, the mana account and transaction types, and the S3
result types. A root-package adapter cannot name those types under Java package
access rules, while a mana-package adapter cannot implement the root-package
package-private `RuntimeExecutionPort`.

The earlier P6-S4 accessibility review therefore reached the product conclusion:

~~~text
PURE PACKAGE-PRIVATE COMPOSITION IMPOSSIBLE
~~~

This is a confirmed Java product-boundary conflict, not a compiler, build, naming,
or evidence-tool failure.

### 57.3 Rejected Models A, B, and C

Model A, direct package-private composition, is rejected because the mandatory root
adapter cannot directly access the mana-package orchestration surface.

Model B, minimum package-private relocation, is rejected because the transitive
execution closure reaches `PlayerManaAccountAccess`, which depends on the retained
package-private `ManaAttachments.state` and `ManaAttachments.replace` live-access
facade. Completing that relocation would require moving or exposing Attachment
persistent truth, its typed state, or its registration boundary. Those owners remain
frozen.

Model C, existing typed-seam reuse, is rejected because
`ManaAttachmentDefinitionBridge` is definition-only. Its exact two accessors expose
neither execution nor account composition, and that bridge must not gain player
access, transaction operations, `getData`, `setData`, an account factory, or an
unwrap operation.

The conflict must not be bypassed with a public `ManaState`, `ManaAccountAccess`,
`ManaTransactionService`, `ActionDamageTransactionEngine`, or
`EffectExecutionEngine`; a raw type, `Object` payload, unchecked cast, reflection,
`MethodHandle`, service loader, ambient factory, service locator, or global callback
registry is also prohibited.

### 57.4 Chosen Capability-Gated Model

The fixed call chain is:

~~~text
P5 package-private RuntimeExecutionPort adapter
-> root-package-only capability
-> P5-owned loaded-only input and scalar mapping
-> public but capability-gated mana-package execution bridge
-> package-private P6-S1 / P6-S2 / P6-S3 orchestration
-> normal return or unchanged throwable propagation
-> root adapter creates the existing RuntimeExecutionBatch
-> P5 remains the sole child publisher
~~~

The two new public types form a Java package-boundary bridge. They are not a
third-party integration API, ambient service, mutable runtime API, registry, service
locator, authentication system, or security boundary. The capability prevents
ordinary Java callers outside the root package from obtaining a legitimate invocation
token. It does not promise protection against reflection or hostile split-package
code, both of which remain outside the supported product model.

### 57.5 Exact Public Top-Level Types

After the authorized P6-S4-R1 implementation, the exact P6 V0 public top-level type
allowlist is:

1. existing
   `com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.runtime.mana.ManaAttachmentDefinitionBridge`;
2. new `com.yo1no.gramarye.P6RuntimeExecutionCapability`;
3. new
   `com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.runtime.mana.P6RuntimeExecutionBridge`.

The exact public P6 top-level type count is three. P6-S4-R1 introduces exactly two of
them. Additional P6 public top-level types and protected top-level types are zero.
The existing definition bridge retains its exact two public accessors and changes no
member, purpose, or ownership.

### 57.6 P6RuntimeExecutionCapability Contract

The exact declaration is:

~~~java
package com.yo1no.gramarye;

public final class P6RuntimeExecutionCapability
~~~

The class has one private static final singleton instance, a private constructor, and
this package-private static accessor:

~~~java
static P6RuntimeExecutionCapability forRuntimeAdapter()
~~~

It has zero instance fields, zero public or protected declared fields, zero public or
protected declared methods, and zero public or protected constructors. It cannot be
subclassed. Ordinary Java code outside `com.yo1no.gramarye` can name the type but
cannot construct it, call its accessor, or obtain its singleton.

The capability carries no event, context, server, player, entity, target, mana,
receipt, trace, result, thread, secret string, UUID, random token, or other product
data. It has no serialization, public factory, public singleton getter, authorization
registry, or equality-based permission scheme. The root adapter may retain the same
immutable stateless singleton for its lifetime.

### 57.7 P6RuntimeExecutionBridge Contract

The exact declaration is:

~~~java
package com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.runtime.mana;

public final class P6RuntimeExecutionBridge
~~~

The constructor is private. Public and protected fields and constructors are zero.
There is exactly one public static product operation, `execute`, and no public
`execute` overload. Its return type is `void` and it declares no checked exception.
There is no capability-free operation.

The bridge accepts no generic type parameter, raw type, `Object`, `Map`, NBT,
`Dynamic`, reflection carrier, varargs carrier, public rich result, or unbounded
collection.

### 57.8 Exact Execute Signature

The exact imports and operation signature are:

~~~java
import com.yo1no.gramarye.P6RuntimeExecutionCapability;
import java.util.UUID;
import net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation;
import net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer;

public static void execute(
        P6RuntimeExecutionCapability capability,
        ServerPlayer actor,
        ResourceLocation actionTypeKey,
        long requestId,
        long sourceEventId,
        UUID targetId,
        long magnitude,
        long manaCost,
        GuardPort guard)
~~~

Those Mojang-mapped platform types and FQCNs are exact. The fixed compensation policy
is internal and is not a public parameter.

### 57.9 GuardPort, GuardPoint, and GuardDecision

`P6RuntimeExecutionBridge` contains exactly three public nested product types and no
fourth one:

~~~java
public interface GuardPort {
    GuardDecision check(GuardPoint point, int stepIndex);
}

public enum GuardPoint {
    ENTRY,
    PRE_COMMIT,
    BEFORE_STEP
}

public enum GuardDecision {
    ALLOWED,
    CANCELLED,
    DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
}
~~~

`GuardPort` may be annotated `@FunctionalInterface`. It has exactly one abstract
method and zero other product-declared public methods. It is synchronous and
call-scoped. It cannot retain P5 context, return a future, create worker activity,
read wall time, mutate world or mana, or expose a P5 queue, scheduler, slot, or lease.

The exact step coordinate is:

| Guard point | Legal step index |
| --- | ---: |
| `ENTRY` | `-1` |
| `PRE_COMMIT` | `-1` |
| `BEFORE_STEP` | `0..7` |

Any other pairing causes the existing package-private
`P6ExecutionInvariantException`. The bridge maps this port one-for-one to the
package-private `EffectExecutionGuard`. The existing absolute invocation maximum
remains ten.

### 57.10 Capability Validation Ordering

The first product action in `P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.execute` is validation that
`capability` is nonnull. Before that validation, actor reads, action-key reads, guard
invocations, target use, mana reads or writes, receipt work, registry lookup, executor
invocation, effect resolution, trace or result creation, and world access are all
zero.

A null capability causes the existing package-private
`P6ExecutionInvariantException`. The bridge accepts no alternate capability
implementation, subclass, null sentinel, boolean bypass, capability-free overload,
or public acquisition route. Because the capability class is final and its only
constructor and accessor are respectively private and root-package-private, a
nonnull legitimate value has exactly one normal Java origin.

### 57.11 Scalar Invocation Contract

`actionTypeKey` is nonnull and is the exact `ResourceLocation` key of the current
`ActionType<?>` in the formal action registry. A string, class name, ordinal,
descriptor identity, payload shape, or reflection result cannot substitute for that
key.

Current P5 has one positive published identity for the executing request: the current
`RuntimeEvent.eventId()`. The exact lossless projection is:

~~~text
requestId     = event.eventId().value()
sourceEventId = event.eventId().value()
~~~

The two bridge fields intentionally carry the same positive value in P6 V0. They do
not use `hashCode`, identity hash, wall time, randomness, a synthetic request ID, or
a second global counter.

`targetId` is a nonnull stable UUID passed only after the P5 loaded-only view has
successfully resolved and validated the target. It grants no authority to look the
target up again or force-load it.

The exact scalar bounds are:

~~~text
1 <= magnitude <= 1_000_000
0 <= manaCost <= 1_000_000_000
~~~

The compensation policy remains exactly `REFUND_IF_NO_PRIMARY_MUTATION` and is not
exposed as a public argument.

The exact one public live platform input is `ServerPlayer actor`. The mana package
uses it only to construct a call-scoped `PlayerManaAccountAccess` bound to the
existing `gramarye:player_mana` truth.

The actor is never stored in a field, static, collection, result, trace, queue, or
background operation; returned; used as a damage target; or replaced by a player
found through a global list. Retention is zero at every normal or exceptional method
terminal. A null actor causes `P6ExecutionInvariantException` after capability
validation.

The root adapter calls the bridge only when the current admitted event has a legal,
already-loaded player actor. Without one, bridge invocation and mana access are zero,
the adapter returns a normal no-op completion, and no synthetic account is created.

### 57.13 Root Adapter Contract

P6-S4-R1 creates exactly one package-private final synchronous adapter in
`com.yo1no.gramarye` that implements the existing `RuntimeExecutionPort`. Its simple
name is an implementation choice. It has no public or protected member, no cross-call
runtime state, and no scheduler, queue, lease, or child-publication ownership.

For each call the adapter uses only the already-admitted exact P5 event, context,
definition, node, and typed action. It does not readmit, repin, query the latest
definition, allocate a replacement event identity, or resolve a target outside P5.
It obtains the actor, loaded-only target UUID, exact action registry key, validated
action scalars, and one-to-one guard mapping from that call. It maps both `requestId`
and `sourceEventId` to the current positive `event.eventId().value()` and invokes the
bridge at most once.

A normal bridge return maps to `RuntimePortOutcome.Completed` with
`RuntimeChildPlan.EMPTY`. Any throwable propagates as the identical object into the
existing P5 fault path. The adapter never publishes child work directly.

### 57.14 Pre-Bridge Mapping Failures

Every pre-bridge mapping failure has bridge invocation, mana mutation, world mutation,

detects it.

P5 resolves references before invoking `RuntimeExecutionPort`. A missing, unloaded,
wrong-server, or wrong-dimension reference therefore retains its existing typed P5
pre-port terminal outcome; adapter invocation and bridge invocation are both zero.
Those outcomes are not translated into `Completed`, and P5 loaded-only reference
semantics do not change.

After P5 has admitted the event and supplied a resolved execution context, an absent
legal `ServerPlayer` actor, a resolved target shape that cannot supply the required
damage target UUID, an absent formal `ActionType` key, missing required magnitude,
mana-cost, or target data, or an out-of-range scalar causes the adapter to return the
existing P5 normal `Completed + empty child plan` transport without invoking the
bridge.

The adapter must not substitute a synthetic production ID, default magnitude,
default mana cost, fixture constant, force-loaded target, alternate player, target
player as payer, or fabricated account.

After capability validation, the bridge performs this closed sequence:

1. validate actor, action key, target ID, and guard nonnull;
2. validate request ID, source event ID, magnitude, and mana-cost bounds;

8. use the exact production unavailable damage commit port;

10. inspect the rich closed terminal result;
11. release the result and return for each normal terminal;
12. throw the invariant exception for `COMPENSATION_FAILED`;
13. publish no children; and
14. retain no call-scoped operation object after any terminal.

Private static final production dependencies may contain only a stateless resolver or
engine, immutable `ActionExecutorRegistry`, stateless `ManaTransactionService`, and

or account map, `RuntimeEvent`, `RuntimeExecutionContext`, receipt, trace, transaction

Static initialization is pure and performs no formal-registry lookup, platform read,

## 58. P7-A1 Network Intent and Synchronization V0 Product Design Authority

### 58.1 Status and Scope

This section is the closed product authority for engineering phase `P7`, formally
named `P7 NETWORK INTENT AND SYNCHRONIZATION V0`. It fixes the smallest bounded,
server-authoritative PLAY-phase network layer that can reject malformed, abusive,
replayed, stale, or out-of-order client input; admit an authorized cast through the
existing P5 owner; and maintain bounded authoritative client mirrors.

This is a documentation-only, strict EOF amendment with `PRODUCT-BLOCKING = NO`.
It authorizes later P7-S1
through P7-S4 implementation but implements no payload, codec, handler, session,
rate limiter, P5 ingress, synchronization path, lifecycle hook, or client mirror.
The P7-A1 decision groups are `19 / 19 CLOSED`, the top-level numeric bounds are
`28 / 28 CLOSED`, unclassified product gaps are zero, and committed-authority
conflicts are zero.

Within P7 network scope this section is normative over the earlier P7 roadmap and
over repository-external P7-RO1 recommendations. In particular, it replaces the
roadmap's P7 `PresentationEventPayload` allocation with the exact admission ACK
defined below; presentation remains a P8 responsibility. P7-RO1 material remains
provenance and navigation evidence only.

Where provisional P7-RO1 evidence differs from the approved clauses in this
amendment, the amendment deliberately fixes the latter without reopening a product
choice: the exact nine ACK dispositions replace the provisional coarse vocabulary;
cooldown entries are slot plus remaining ticks rather than reference/revision
carriers; mana uses the capability-gated pull observation seam rather than a P6
post-transaction scalar callback; stop cleanup is the exact
`256 session + 256 reconciliation UUID + 64 permit` decomposition; and the global
work-unit gate is evaluated on the server logic thread. These are scoped P7-A1
corrections, not claims that historical external evidence was byte-for-byte the
same design.

This amendment does not supersede P5 scheduler ownership, P6 effect or mana
transaction semantics, Attachment persistent truth, P8 presentation authority, or
P9 actual-damage authority.

### 58.2 P7 Formal Identity

~~~text
phase        = P7
formal name  = NETWORK INTENT AND SYNCHRONIZATION V0
Chinese name = Network Intent 與同步
layer        = PRODUCT DESIGN
goal         = bounded server-authoritative intent ingress and authoritative sync
~~~

The client supplies intent only. Server state remains authoritative at every
authorization, admission, execution, transaction, and synchronization boundary.

### 58.3 Exact Scope

P7 owns exactly these product concerns:

1. one bounded C2S cast-intent payload;
2. the P7 protocol and payload registrar;
3. connection-scoped session identity;
4. sequence, duplicate, stale, gap, replay, and exhaustion semantics;
5. deterministic rate limiting;
6. pending-work permits and backpressure;
7. network-thread to logic-thread handoff;
8. sender, slot, target-hint, and exact-revision authorization;
9. token-safe P5 player-cast ingress;
10. admission acknowledgement;
11. authoritative mana full snapshots;
12. authoritative cooldown full snapshots;
13. login, disconnect, respawn, dimension, reload, and stop lifecycle;
14. bounded abuse diagnostics; and
15. client-side authoritative P7 mirrors.

The P6-to-P7 handoff is observation-only: P7 may observe the bounded mana scalar
through the exact capability-gated seam in §58.22, but it may not mutate mana or
invoke P6 execution.

### 58.4 Exact Exclusions

P7 does not own or alter P5 scheduling, queues, leases, child publication, P6 effect
resolution, P6 mana transactions, P6 direct execution, actual Minecraft damage,
production `ActionType` content, P8 presentation, P9 playable damage, Marker,
Construct, editor behavior, mana regeneration, a persistent network journal, or any
client-authoritative gameplay mutation.

P7 adds no configuration/login-data payload, packet batching, intent batching,
pending ACK queue, background refill task, second scheduler, persistent replay
window, public third-party network API, or two-process playable-client requirement.

### 58.5 P6 to P7 Handoff

P5 and P6 are complete inputs to P7, not subsystems for P7 to redesign. A legal
client cast terminates P7 ingress at an existing typed P5 root-admission result.
Only P5 can bind its runtime server token, create and order runtime work, own the
queue and lease, publish children, and later call its P6 execution port. P7 never
calls the P6 execution bridge directly.

For synchronization, the P6 mana Attachment remains the sole mana truth. P7-S4 may
use the exact observation-only bridge in §58.22 to project one scalar balance or an
unavailable marker. It may not expose the Attachment, mana state, transaction
service, receipt, or execution result.

### 58.6 Client/Server Trust Boundary

The client may provide only a sequence, slot, the single V0 input kind `CAST`, an
advisory aim direction, and one advisory entity network-ID hint. The server alone
decides the authenticated actor, connection epoch, exact equipped
`SkillReference`, exact retained revision, `ActionType`, node index, runtime cause,
target validity, mana truth, magnitude, mana cost, P5 ordering, P6 request/plan/result,
effect success, child publication, and client-mirror truth.

The client must not transmit or authoritatively choose a `SkillDefinition`,
definition revision, node index, `ActionType` key, final target UUID, dimension,
final magnitude, mana charge, cooldown, effect plan, result, P5 `EventId`, child
publication, or server tick. A locally predicted or cached client value never
becomes gameplay authority.

### 58.7 Exact Payload Families

P7 V0 has exactly four non-optional PLAY-phase payload families:

| Payload ID | Direction | Cardinality and role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gramarye:cast_intent` | `PLAY_TO_SERVER` | one payload equals one intent; batching zero |
| `gramarye:intent_ack` | `PLAY_TO_CLIENT` | one coarse admission acknowledgement |
| `gramarye:player_mana_sync` | `PLAY_TO_CLIENT` | one authoritative mana full snapshot |
| `gramarye:skill_cooldown_sync` | `PLAY_TO_CLIENT` | one authoritative cooldown full snapshot |

Other P7 V0 payload families are zero. Configuration/login-data payloads are zero.
P8 owns any future `PresentationEvent` payload.

### 58.8 CastIntent Envelope

The `gramarye:cast_intent` body has this exact canonical field order:

| Order | Field | Encoding | V0 constraint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `sequence` | fixed signed 64-bit long | product-valid range `1..Long.MAX_VALUE`; every fixed-long bit pattern decodes structurally |
| 2 | `slot` | unsigned 8-bit | `0..63` |
| 3 | `input_kind` | unsigned 8-bit | `CAST = 0`; every other value malformed |
| 4 | `presence_mask` | unsigned 8-bit | bit 0 aim; bit 1 entity hint; bits 2..7 zero |
| 5 | optional `aim_x` | signed 16-bit Q15 | present only with bit 0 |
| 6 | optional `aim_y` | signed 16-bit Q15 | present only with bit 0 |
| 7 | optional `aim_z` | signed 16-bit Q15 | present only with bit 0 |
| 8 | optional `entity_hint` | positive VarInt | present only with bit 1 |

The maximum actual encoded body is 22 bytes and the hard accepted ceiling is 32
bytes. Trailing bytes are `MALFORMED_PAYLOAD`. One packet carries exactly one
intent, and an intent carries at most one optional entity hint. Press, hold, release,
and repeat are outside P7 V0.

### 58.9 Aim and Entity Hint

Each present Q15 aim component must be in `-32767..32767`; `-32768` is reserved and
invalid. The all-zero vector is invalid. Before use, the server converts the three
components to deterministic scalars and normalizes them as an advisory direction.
The direction cannot choose a final target, magnitude, cost, or effect.

The optional entity hint is a positive VarInt in `1..Integer.MAX_VALUE` naming an
entity network ID in the actor's current dimension. UUID, dimension ID, block
position, collection, and target-list encodings are forbidden. On the server logic
thread, a present hint must resolve to the current loaded entity, on the same server
and dimension as the loaded actor, with the ID still naming that entity and the
target otherwise valid. Validation never loads a chunk or force-loads an entity.

An invalid or unavailable hint maps to `INVALID_TARGET` or `TARGET_UNAVAILABLE` as
appropriate. If sequence consumption has already occurred, this semantic rejection
does not restore the sequence. Even a valid hint is discarded after validation:
P7 retains no live `Entity`, passes no target UUID to P5, and the P5 V0 root target
remains `NO_TARGET`.

### 58.10 Protocol and Codec Version

The exact registrar version is `gramarye-p7-v0`; compatibility is `EXACT MATCH
ONLY`. A body-level schema/version field is absent, and same-major or cross-version
wire-compatibility promises are zero. Exactly one internal registrar owner registers
the four exact IDs for PLAY, using `playToServer` for cast intent and
`playToClient` for ACK, mana, and cooldown.

An unknown registrar version fails connection negotiation. An unknown payload ID
fails closed at the platform boundary. Unknown input kinds, disposition or
availability values, reserved mask or flag bits, structurally invalid aim/entity
values, structural overflow, and trailing bytes are `MALFORMED_PAYLOAD`. The fixed
long sequence always decodes structurally; `sequence <= 0` reaches the server-thread
semantic classifier as `INVALID_SEQUENCE` and maps to `REJECTED`, not malformed
disconnect. There is no public generic payload-registration API.

### 58.11 Session and Epoch

A P7 session identity is the authenticated player UUID plus a server-generated
connection epoch. The epoch is a positive signed long, begins at 1 for each server
process, advances by checked monotonic increment through `Long.MAX_VALUE`, never
wraps, is not persistent, and resets only with a new server process. Epoch-generator
exhaustion refuses new P7 sessions until server restart.

There is at most one active P7 session per player and 256 active sessions per
server. A session may retain only bounded scalar state: UUID, epoch, expected intent
sequence, exhausted flag, rate tokens, last-refill tick, per-tick ingress count,
strike count/window, pending-permit count, mana and cooldown sync sequences,
last-resync tick, and bounded diagnostic-throttle state.

A session must not retain `ServerPlayer`, `Level`, `Entity`, a packet buffer,
`RuntimeEvent`, `ManaReceipt`, `Throwable`, or raw payload history.

### 58.12 Sequence State Machine

The initial expected sequence is 1 and the legal range is
`1..Long.MAX_VALUE`. Only `received == expected` is exact-next. After accepting a
non-maximum value, expected advances by checked addition to `expected + 1`. Accepting
`Long.MAX_VALUE` moves the session sequence state to `EXHAUSTED`; there is no next
expected value and no wrap.

The authorization order in §58.17 consumes exact-next before later semantic
authorization. Therefore an exact-next intent rejected for liveness, spectator,
Attachment, slot, owner, retained revision, fixed mapping, target, or P5-admission
reasons remains consumed. Rate, global/per-player admission, `SERVER_BUSY`, reload,
and sequence-classification rejection do not consume it.

Sequence and rate state are never persistent. Reconnect creates a new epoch and
resets expected to 1. Respawn and dimension travel preserve the current epoch and
sequence.

### 58.13 Replay, Duplicate, Stale, and Gap

Before exhaustion the exact classifications are:

| Condition | Internal reason | Mutation | P5 calls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `expected > 1 && received == expected - 1` | `DUPLICATE_SEQUENCE` | none | 0 |
| `1 <= received < expected - 1` | `STALE_SEQUENCE` | none | 0 |
| `received > expected` | `SEQUENCE_GAP` | none | 0 |
| `received <= 0` | `INVALID_SEQUENCE` | none | 0 |
| state already `EXHAUSTED` | `SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED` | none | 0 |

The retained replay window is one scalar: current expected sequence. The maximum
accepted future gap is zero. P7 buffers no future sequence and keeps no replay
history. Once exhausted, every later intent returns `SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED` until a
new connection epoch is established.

### 58.14 Rate Limiter

Each session has one deterministic integer token bucket for the `CAST` family. Its
capacity and initial tokens are 8, refill is 2 tokens per authoritative server tick,
cost is 1 per decoded CAST intent, and the maximum is 8. Refill is calculated lazily
on the server logic thread. Wall-clock time and background refill tasks are absent.

Tick regression or an invalid tick is `INTERNAL_SERVER_FAULT` and consumes no
sequence. A player receives at most 8 server-thread intent evaluations per tick.
The server performs at most 64 complete P7 work units per tick, shared by intent,
reload reconciliation, and authoritative synchronization work.

A depleted bucket or exceeded per-player tick ceiling is `RATE_LIMITED`, consumes
no sequence, and calls P5 zero times. Rate strikes use a 100-server-tick window. The
eighth `RATE_LIMITED` strike causes a best-effort RATE_LIMITED ACK, disconnect, and
bounded cleanup. `SERVER_BUSY` does not add a rate strike.

The strike window is first-strike anchored. A first strike at authoritative tick
`t` opens the inclusive window `[t, t + 99]` with count one. Before classifying a
strike at any tick `>= t + 100`, P7 resets the count and anchors a new window at that
current tick, then records it as strike one. Non-strike traffic does not extend or
reset an open window. Reconnect creates a new session with no strike window. Tick
addition is checked; overflow follows `INTERNAL_SERVER_FAULT` rather than wrap.

### 58.15 Pending Permits and Backpressure

The network thread must acquire a pending-work permit before `enqueueWork`. The
hard limits are 8 pending intents per player and 64 per server. Failure to acquire a
permit is `SERVER_BUSY`, consumes no sequence, creates no queued ACK, and invokes no
P5 work. It produces at most one immediate best-effort `SERVER_BUSY` reply on the
same network thread, with `HAS_EXPECTED_NEXT=0`, `SEQUENCE_CONSUMED=0`, and
`RESYNC_RECOMMENDED=0`, then returns without `enqueueWork`. There is no batch intent
and no second P5 scheduler.

The immutable queued task may contain only the decoded `CastIntent`, authenticated
UUID, captured epoch, and a single-use permit token. It must not retain a
`ServerPlayer`, `IPayloadContext`, `ByteBuf`, connection object, `Entity`, `Level`,
or `Throwable`.

Permit ownership transfers exactly once from the network handler to the queued
task. A synchronous enqueue submission failure releases it immediately; a started
task releases it in `finally`, including current-session/epoch rejection. Session or
server terminal invalidation releases any permit whose task can no longer start.
The single-use token makes these paths mutually exclusive and exactly-once. The
`enqueueWork` future is neither retained nor chained.

### 58.16 Thread Handoff

The C2S registrar fixes `executesOn(HandlerThread.NETWORK)`. On the network thread,
the handler may only decode; perform structural size, mask, enum, and scalar checks;
capture the authenticated UUID and current epoch; acquire one permit; and either
send the one immediate best-effort BUSY reply described in §58.15 and return, or
create one immutable scalar task and call `enqueueWork` exactly once. It cannot mutate
sequence or rate gameplay state, resolve a skill/revision, read mana, validate a
world target, call P5 or P6, mutate the world, or retain a packet buffer or player.

On the server logic thread the task re-resolves the current session and player,
checks UUID/epoch and lifecycle gates, accounts work/rate/sequence, authorizes the
cast, invokes P5 at most once, produces the ACK disposition, and releases the permit
in `finally`.

Each S2C handler performs structural decoding on the network thread and exactly one
enqueue to the client main thread. Only that client main thread may mutate a P7
mirror. No handler retains its packet buffer or builds a future chain.

### 58.17 Authorization Order

Every server-side cast evaluation uses this fixed order:

1. current session UUID and epoch;
2. server still running;
3. sender still connected;
4. reload gate;
5. global 64-work-unit admission;
6. per-player hard ingress;
7. token bucket;
8. sequence classification;
9. exact-next sequence consumption;
10. player alive;
11. player is not a spectator;
12. `player_skills` Attachment available;
13. slot `0..63` binding exists;
14. exact `SkillReference` owner/account pairing;
15. exact retained revision remains admissible;
16. fixed cause and node-zero construction;
17. advisory target validation;
18. P5 ingress at most once;
19. ACK disposition; and
20. permit release.

The authoritative equipped-slot projection, not a client definition or revision,
selects the exact reference. P7 must not substitute `latestReference`, repin a
revision, or let the client choose an action or node.

For P7 V0, the frozen §24 serverbound checks are reconciled as follows. Connected,
alive, ownership, slot, and dimension checks remain mandatory in the order above.
Because the current production cooldown/continuation provider is absent, cooldown
and continuation-phase rejection are not applicable and must not be invented.
Because an entity network ID is only an advisory hint that is discarded before a
`NO_TARGET` P5 root, there is no V0 gameplay-distance threshold; loaded-only,
same-server, same-dimension, current-ID, and generic target-validity checks are the
complete hint policy. This narrowly supersedes frozen §24 only for the unavailable
cooldown/phase authorities and the non-target-bearing hint's distance check. A
future target-bearing cast, cooldown, or continuation phase must commit its own
server-side legality and distance authority before use.

### 58.18 Token-Safe P5 Ingress

P7-S3 is authorized to add this root-package, package-private operation:

~~~java
SkillRuntimeService.admitAuthenticatedPlayerCast(
        MinecraftServer server,
        ServerPlayer actor,
        SkillReference exactReference)
~~~

Its return type is the existing typed P5 admission result; it creates no public
result API. The operation is synchronous and server-logic-thread-only. P5 binds its
own runtime token internally. The caller cannot provide a token, `EventId`, revision
substitute, node index, cause, schedule, retention, or target.

The operation constructs exactly this fixed root and tail-calls existing
`admitRoot` exactly once:

~~~text
cause                         = gramarye:active_cast
nodeIndex                     = 0
schedule.delayTicks           = 0
schedule.deadlineHorizonTicks = 0
schedule.persistence          = MEMORY_ONLY
root depth                    = 0, minted by P5
root suborder/childSequence   = 0, minted by P5
target                        = NO_TARGET
~~~

`gramarye:active_cast` is a P5 admission-cause identity, not authorization for new
production `ActionType` content. P7 may not call P6 directly, construct a runtime
event that bypasses P5, repin, perform a latest lookup, publish children, or access
the P5 queue or lease.

### 58.19 ACK Contract

The `gramarye:intent_ack` body has fixed-long `sequence`, unsigned-byte
`disposition`, unsigned-byte `flags`, and an optional fixed-long `expected_next`, in
that order. It has exactly these nine wire dispositions:

| Value | Disposition |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | `ACCEPTED` |
| 1 | `REJECTED` |
| 2 | `DUPLICATE` |
| 3 | `STALE` |
| 4 | `SEQUENCE_GAP` |
| 5 | `SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED` |
| 6 | `RATE_LIMITED` |
| 7 | `SERVER_BUSY` |
| 8 | `UNAVAILABLE` |

All other disposition values are malformed. Flag bit 0 is `HAS_EXPECTED_NEXT`, bit
1 is `SEQUENCE_CONSUMED`, bit 2 is `RESYNC_RECOMMENDED`, and bits 3..7 must be zero.
The maximum actual body is 18 bytes and the hard ceiling is 32 bytes. There is one
ACK entry per packet and zero pending ACKs per player.

`ACCEPTED` means only that P5 accepted the root admission. It does not mean the root
was scheduled, executed, completed, produced an effect, charged mana, or mutated the
world.

For duplicate, stale, and gap, `SEQUENCE_CONSUMED=0`,
`HAS_EXPECTED_NEXT=1`, and `expected_next` is the current exact expected value. A
rate or server-busy response is not consumed; expected is present when server-thread
session state is safely readable and absent for network-thread permit rejection.
Exact-next semantic rejection and accepted P5 admission are consumed. A transition
to exhausted has no expected-next value. `RESYNC_RECOMMENDED` is used only for stale
or gap, an authoritative mirror mismatch, reload completion, or safe unavailable
recovery.

### 58.20 Failure-to-Wire Mapping

The closed P7 V0 internal reason vocabulary contains exactly these twenty reasons:

~~~text
MALFORMED_PAYLOAD
PROTOCOL_VERSION_MISMATCH
UNAUTHENTICATED_SENDER
UNAUTHORIZED_INTENT
UNKNOWN_SKILL
UNKNOWN_ACTION
INVALID_TARGET
TARGET_UNAVAILABLE
INVALID_SEQUENCE
DUPLICATE_SEQUENCE
STALE_SEQUENCE
SEQUENCE_GAP
SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED
RATE_LIMITED
SERVER_BUSY
P5_ADMISSION_REJECTED
P5_UNAVAILABLE
INTERNAL_SERVER_FAULT
DISCONNECTED
RELOAD_IN_PROGRESS
~~~

The fixed wire mapping is:

| Internal reason | Wire behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `MALFORMED_PAYLOAD` | no ACK; disconnect |
| `PROTOCOL_VERSION_MISMATCH` | connection negotiation rejection; no PLAY ACK |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED_SENDER` | no ACK; disconnect |
| `UNAUTHORIZED_INTENT`, `UNKNOWN_SKILL`, `UNKNOWN_ACTION`, `INVALID_TARGET`, `TARGET_UNAVAILABLE`, `INVALID_SEQUENCE`, `P5_ADMISSION_REJECTED` | `REJECTED` |
| `DUPLICATE_SEQUENCE` | `DUPLICATE` |
| `STALE_SEQUENCE` | `STALE` |
| `SEQUENCE_GAP` | `SEQUENCE_GAP` |
| `SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED` | `SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED` |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | `RATE_LIMITED` |
| `SERVER_BUSY` | `SERVER_BUSY` |
| `P5_UNAVAILABLE`, `RELOAD_IN_PROGRESS` | `UNAVAILABLE` |
| `INTERNAL_SERVER_FAULT` | no internal detail on wire; no ACK when state is uncertain |
| `DISCONNECTED` | no ACK |

An unexpected `RuntimeException` or `Error` is not converted to an accepted or
rejected gameplay result. Its identical object enters the platform/server fault
path; class, message, and stack are never sent to the client; the permit is released
in `finally`; and P7 retains zero `Throwable` objects.

The future S3 adapter must classify the current sealed P5 admission result with an
exhaustive no-default switch. `AcceptedMemoryOnly` maps to `ACCEPTED`.
`ServerNotRunning`, `ServerStopping`, and `KernelFaulted` map through
`P5_UNAVAILABLE` to `UNAVAILABLE`. `WrongThread` violates the server-thread ingress
contract and maps to `INTERNAL_SERVER_FAULT`, with no ACK when state is uncertain.
The remaining exact normal variants map through `P5_ADMISSION_REJECTED` to
`REJECTED`: `PersistentScheduleUnsupported`, `DelayOutOfRange`, `DelayOverflow`,
`DeadlineOutOfRange`, `DeadlineOverflow`, `DeadlineBeforeScheduledTick`,
`InvalidRuntimeReference`, `SkillRevisionUnavailable`, `InvalidEvent`,
`OwnerInstanceUnavailable`, `ActiveLineageCapacityExceeded`,
`ActiveBudgetAttributionCapacityExceeded`, `RootAdmissionBudgetExceeded`,
`CircuitBroken`, `SequenceExhausted`, and `TickExhausted`. A later P5 sealed-variant
change must fail the direct compile Gate until this mapping is explicitly updated;
it cannot fall through a default branch.

### 58.21 Mana Snapshot

The `gramarye:player_mana_sync` body is, in order, a fixed positive-long
`sync_sequence`, unsigned-byte `availability`, and fixed-long `balance`.
Availability 0 is `AVAILABLE`; availability 1 is `UNAVAILABLE`; all other values are
malformed. An available balance is in `0..1_000_000_000`. An unavailable snapshot
encodes balance zero while leaving the client mirror explicitly unavailable.

The actual body is at most 17 bytes and the hard S2C sync ceiling is 4096 bytes. It
is always a full snapshot: delta count and client prediction are zero. A newly
accepted snapshot completely overwrites the mana mirror.

Each outbound sync family has its own positive-long sequence, initially 1,
monotonic, checked, and non-wrapping. A client accepts only a value greater than the
last applied value, drops equal or older values, and accepts gaps because the
snapshot is complete. Exhaustion disconnects the session so a reconnect can create
new sequence state; it never wraps.

### 58.22 Mana Observation Bridge

P7-S4 is authorized to add exactly one public package-boundary type:

~~~java
public final class P7ManaSnapshotBridge {
    private P7ManaSnapshotBridge() {}

    public static long observeBalance(
            P6RuntimeExecutionCapability capability,
            ServerPlayer actor);
}
~~~

It has zero public overloads and zero public/protected fields. The first product
operation validates the capability as non-null. It returns `0..1_000_000_000` for
an available balance or `-1` for unavailable. The root-package P7 synchronization
owner reuses the existing singleton through package-private
`P6RuntimeExecutionCapability.forRuntimeAdapter()`; no public capability factory or
second capability type is added.

The bridge performs no mana mutation, exposes no `ManaState`, Attachment, or
transaction service, retains neither argument, creates no receipt, accesses no
world target, and sends no payload itself. It is a normal-Java package boundary,
not a supported external integration API; the supported external-integration API
count remains zero.

The P6-only allowlist and count in §57.5 and §57.19 remain exactly three and are not
relabelled as P7 surface. Within this observation-only P7 allocation, §58 narrowly
expands §57.21's capability-boundary exception from its two P6 types to a combined
P6/P7 capability-boundary subset of three. The cumulative relevant public top-level
allowlist becomes exactly four:
`ManaAttachmentDefinitionBridge`, `P6RuntimeExecutionCapability`,
`P6RuntimeExecutionBridge`, and `P7ManaSnapshotBridge`. The exact capability-boundary
subset is the latter three. The new P7 public-type delta is exactly one; the existing
two-member definition bridge and P6 execution-bridge signature remain unchanged.

The package-private `P6RuntimeExecutionCapability.forRuntimeAdapter()` caller
allowlist becomes exactly the existing `P6RuntimeExecutionPortAdapter` plus the
future root-package P7 synchronization owner. Only the former may call
`P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.execute`; P7 direct P6 execution calls remain zero. Exact
