### 58.23 Cooldown Snapshot

The `gramarye:skill_cooldown_sync` body contains, in order, a fixed positive-long
`sync_sequence`, a bounded VarInt `entry_count`, and entries sorted by slot. Each
entry contains an unsigned-byte slot in `0..63` followed by positive-VarInt
`remaining_ticks` in `1..Integer.MAX_VALUE`.

Entry count is `0..64`; slots are unique and strictly ascending; zero cooldowns are
omitted; duplicate slots and trailing bytes are malformed. This is a full snapshot,
so every absent slot is cleared in the client mirror. The maximum actual V0
structural body is 393 bytes and the hard ceiling is 4096 bytes.

There is currently no authoritative cooldown provider. Production V0 therefore
emits `entry_count = 0` and invents no value. P7-S4 may add a package-private
`P7CooldownSnapshotSource` whose production implementation is an immutable empty
snapshot. A later committed cooldown authority may replace that source without
adding public API.

P7 V0 has no continuation field, entry, or payload. This exact empty cooldown
snapshot and four-family model narrowly defer the implementation contract §11.2
generic `cooldown/continuation sync` wording for continuation only. Continuation
truth and synchronization require later committed product authority; they may not
be inferred, serialized into the cooldown entry, or added as a fifth P7 V0 payload.

### 58.24 Client Mirrors

P7 client state contains only the last ACK/coarse admission state, authoritative
mana availability and balance, authoritative cooldown entries, and the last applied
mana and cooldown sync sequences. The client main thread is the sole mutation
owner. A newer full snapshot overwrites its family mirror; disconnect or client
world unload clears all P7 mirrors.

Mirrors cannot mutate server truth, predict mana charge or cooldown, create a
`RuntimeEvent` or effect result, persist to a world, or retain a network buffer.
P8 presentation is not part of a P7 mirror.

### 58.25 Sync and Reconciliation

Full mana-plus-cooldown synchronization is requested on exactly session open,
respawn, dimension-travel completion, reload-reconciliation completion, and
periodic authoritative reconciliation. Except for an initial login in a new
session, a session receives at most one full snapshot set in 20 server ticks.

The P7 V0 direct post-mana-transaction notification count is zero. This exact trigger
set narrowly supersedes only the client-sync trigger timing in frozen §8-B's Mana
row (`登入與交易後`); it does not alter the transaction, Attachment truth, or
balance. The bounded periodic full snapshot is the V0 convergence route. A later
immediate transaction-sync route requires separately committed P7 authority and may
not be inferred from P6 execution.

Scheduling uses a coalesced set of unique UUID scalars, bounded to 256 entries, and
retains no live player. The server thread re-resolves each player. One session
reconciliation consumes one P7 work unit. Reload/sync reconciliation processes at
most 16 sessions per tick and shares the global 64-work-unit ceiling. If budget is
unavailable, the unique UUID remains coalesced rather than spawning an unbounded
queue.

### 58.26 Lifecycle

The existing P4 `SkillSubmissionRecoveryService` remains the sole
`PlayerLoggedInEvent` owner. P7 adds no second listener or event-order coupling.
Within login lifecycle only, this approved amendment supersedes the terminal tail of
P4 §17 B.5 from `E2 continuation -> return` to exactly
`E2 normal completion -> one P7 open-session handoff -> return`. P4 recovery and E2
ordering, identity, and result semantics otherwise remain unchanged.

P7-S4 must bind an exact-one, constructor-owned internal handoff into that existing
listener and the production composition root. It adds no public API, public callback,
setter, service locator, static fallback, reflection route, second listener, or
replaceable third-party seam. The handoff accepts only the current `ServerPlayer`,
opens scalar session state synchronously, retains no player, and returns `void`.
Concrete class name, file split, private helper, and internal package arrangement are
S4 implementation choices and must satisfy normal Java visibility without widening
the public surface.

On login the handoff assigns the checked connection epoch, initializes expected
sequence 1, tokens 8, strikes and pending count zero, both outbound sync sequences
to 1, and requests the initial full snapshot. Session-cap or epoch exhaustion
refuses the P7 session and gameplay admission and disconnects as appropriate.

On disconnect/logout, P7 removes the session, invalidates its epoch, releases or
invalidates permits, drops unsent ACK state, removes its reload/sync UUID, and
persists nothing. Client unload clears mirrors. Cleanup is bounded to 9 session
components.

Respawn/death clone and dimension travel preserve connection session, epoch,
sequence, and rate state, retain no old `ServerPlayer`, re-resolve the current
player, and request a full snapshot. There is no dimension-specific sequence state.

During datapack reload, the reload gate closes before reload-sensitive admission.
New intents return `UNAVAILABLE` / `RELOAD_IN_PROGRESS`, consume no sequence, and
call P5 zero times. After reload, P7 coalesces all active UUIDs into the bounded 256
set, processes at most 16 per tick, re-resolves exact references, and emits full
mana/cooldown snapshots without retaining live players.

Server stop accepts no new session or intent. Cleanup is bounded to 576 records:
256 active sessions plus 256 reload/reconciliation UUID entries plus 64 global
pending permits. The diagnostics ring is discarded as one service-owned container
reference rather than record-by-record stop work, so its capacity does not add to
the 576-record bound. There is no journal, flush, or persistent recovery.

### 58.27 State Ownership and Persistence

P7 server state is transient and limited to epoch, expected/exhausted sequence,
token bucket, per-tick ingress count, strike window, pending permits, outbound sync
sequences, last-resync tick, reload UUID set, and bounded diagnostics. Persistent P7
state count is zero.

P7 never writes world data, playerdata, mana Attachment fields, skill Attachment
schema, a journal, pending ACK state, or intent history. The P6 `player_mana`
Attachment remains authoritative mana truth; the existing P3/P4 owners remain
authoritative for skill references. P7 reads only bounded scalar projections.

### 58.28 Abuse and Diagnostics

The server diagnostic ring contains at most 256 records. A record may contain only
an authenticated UUID when known, authoritative server tick, coarse internal
reason, and saturating count. It must not contain raw packet bytes, payload history,
aim vector, target ID, block/entity position, `SkillDefinition`, `RuntimeEvent`,
`Throwable`, stack trace, or exception class name.

Counters are fixed and saturating. Log emission for one UUID/reason pair is limited
to one log per 100 server ticks; this throttle is distinct from diagnostic-ring
record capacity. Eight rate-limit strikes in a 100-tick window cause disconnect. A
malformed payload disconnects immediately with no ACK; other semantic rejections
normally produce only the coarse ACK and do not automatically disconnect.

### 58.29 API and Registration Ownership

One internal registrar owns all four payload registrations. Payload values, codecs,
handlers, sessions, rate types, permits, and mirrors are package-private except for
the minimum platform-required generated or nested surface. Public third-party
network integration API, generic packet handler API, `ServiceLoader`, reflection,
public `ByteBuf`, public mutable session/rate state, and reloadable payload registry
counts are each zero.

The exact new public package-boundary type authorized by P7 is
`P7ManaSnapshotBridge`, count one. Additional public P7 types and public integration
operations are zero. Direct P7 Gates must use an exact allowlist of type, package,
signature, caller, and purpose across existing P6 and new P7 boundary members;
package blankets, name-prefix acceptance, generic callback acceptance, and generic
`Bridge` exemptions are forbidden.

implementing method to use package-private visibility, even when the implementing
top-level class itself is package-private. The former conjunction was impossible:

~~~text

= package-private

RootIngressPort implementation method visibility
= package-private

all public/protected owner members
= 0

Java-closed
= NO
~~~

This contradiction concerns one member modifier only. It does not invalidate the
package boundary, capability, write-once installation, root-local mapping, service
identity, or instance-escape model.

### 59.9 Seven Hard Gaps

The seven gaps are one connected boundary problem, not seven independent product
designs:

1. `F01`: no typed network-package call to the root-package P5 owner;
2. `F02`: no path to the existing P5 service instance;
3. `F03`: no legal cross-package caller or result type for the authorized ingress;
4. `F04`: no path to the existing equipped-slot projection instance;
5. `F06`: no path to the existing owner and exact-revision validator instances;
6. `F07`: no package in the former design could name both P5 variants and P7
   dispositions; and
7. `F11`: no typed root-to-network installation seam.

All seven are closed together by a root-owned implementation that uses the exact
public controlled P4 Attachment/Store projections, sees the package-private P5
details, maps them to a deliberately coarse public nested enum, and is installed
once through the existing unforgeable capability. None requires a new persistent
truth, duplicate service, public service getter, or generic bridge.

### 59.10 Single Root Cause

The single root cause is that the network package, root package, and definition
service instances form separate Java package and composition islands. The required
types and exact production objects already exist, but no former seam can legally
carry both typed authorization inputs and the closed result across those islands.

The repair therefore joins composition, not persistent state: an exact public
package-boundary vocabulary and write-once port connect the islands, while the
root-local owner retains all service identities and all non-public P5 knowledge.

### 59.11 Rejected Models A–E

| Model | Proposal | Decision and reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | direct package-private call | rejected: root and network are different Java packages |
| B | relocate P5/P4 services or persistent truth | rejected: it would move `player_skills`, Store, scheduler/service ownership, or the sealed result boundary outside their frozen owners |
| C | public P5/P4 service getters or public P5 result | rejected: it would create an ambient bypass surface for `SkillRuntimeService`, the Attachment service, Store service, result hierarchy, or mutation authority |
| D | generic locator or callback | rejected: `Object`, raw type, reflection, `MethodHandle`, `ServiceLoader`, generic runtime maps, and global mutable setters erase the closed type/owner boundary |
| E | duplicate service instances | rejected: a second runtime, Attachment, Store, or slot/reference truth violates unique ownership and identity |

Model C includes and rejects a public `SkillRuntimeService` getter, a new public
`PlayerSkillAttachmentService` getter, a new public
`SkillDefinitionStoreService` acquisition route, a public
`RuntimeAdmissionResult`, and a public skill-reference mutation service. Model E
includes and rejects reconstructing any of the three existing service objects in
the network composition.

### 59.23 Root Authorization Order

Every `RootIngressPort.authorizeAndAdmit(...)` invocation follows this exact order:

1. validate `server` non-null;
2. validate `actor` non-null;
3. validate `targetCheck` non-null;
4. validate `slot` in `0..63`;
5. verify the server logic thread;
6. verify the actor belongs to the supplied server;
7. verify the actor UUID and current-player identity;
8. read authoritative `player_skills` truth;
9. call `PlayerSkillAttachmentService.equippedAt(actor, slot)` exactly once;
10. obtain the exact equipped `SkillReference`;
11. map an empty/missing slot to `UNKNOWN_SKILL`;
12. verify exact owner/account pairing;
13. verify that the exact retained revision remains available and admissible;
14. invoke `AdvisoryTargetCheck` exactly once;
15. map `INVALID_TARGET` or `TARGET_UNAVAILABLE` without a P5 call;
16. only on `VALID`, invoke token-safe P5 ingress at most once;
17. exhaustively map `RuntimeAdmissionResult`;
18. return the coarse `AdmissionDisposition`; and
19. retain no call-scoped object.

Target validation before reference/owner/revision validation and a P5 call before
`VALID` are prohibited. This path performs no raw NBT/playerdata access, latest
revision substitution, definition escape, direct queue insertion, direct pin,
direct lease access, or direct P6 call.

### 59.24 Equipped-Reference Projection

The only authoritative equipped projection is the current exact
`PlayerSkillAttachmentService.equippedAt(ServerPlayer, int)` operation. The input
is the current actor and slot `0..63`; the output, when present, is the exact stored
immutable `SkillReference`.

~~~text
equippedAt calls
= exactly 1 when the projection stage is reached

copied slot map / default skill / latest lookup
= 0 / 0 / 0

mutable Attachment / collection / definition escape
= 0 / 0 / 0

empty slot
= UNKNOWN_SKILL

unavailable Attachment truth
= P5_UNAVAILABLE

owner/account mismatch
= UNAUTHORIZED_INTENT
~~~

The exact reference is never repinned, replaced by `latestReference`, or inferred
from a client value.

### 59.25 Owner/Revision Validation

The root owner uses the exact existing typed projections:

~~~text
PlayerSkillAttachmentService.ownerId(actor)
SkillDefinitionStoreService.ownerOf(server, exactReference.skillId())
SkillDefinitionStoreService.find(server, exactReference)
~~~

The authenticated actor/account owner must equal the committed skill owner. A
missing skill/owner or exact retained revision is not replaced with a latest or
fallback revision. An owner mismatch maps to `UNAUTHORIZED_INTENT`; unavailable
service truth maps to `P5_UNAVAILABLE`; absence of the named skill or exact retained
revision maps to `UNKNOWN_SKILL`.

The `find` call uses the supplied exact reference. Any call-scoped materialized
definition is discarded before return; definition retention and cross-package
definition return are both zero. Validation performs no direct Store, world-file,
or playerdata read outside the existing services.

### 59.26 Advisory Target Lambda

The network-side production realization of `AdvisoryTargetCheck` is a typed,
call-scoped lambda. There is exactly one construction site as the target stage is
reached and no named production target-check implementation class.

It may capture only immutable `AimHint`, immutable `EntityHint`, and a stateless
target validator. It must not capture `MinecraftServer`, `ServerPlayer`, `Entity`,
`Level`, `IPayloadContext`, a buffer, a P4/P5/P6 service, or `Throwable`.

~~~text
invocations before earlier authorization succeeds
= 0

invocations when the target stage is reached
= exactly 1

VALID
= continue to P5

INVALID_TARGET
= AdmissionDisposition.INVALID_TARGET; P5 calls 0

TARGET_UNAVAILABLE
= AdmissionDisposition.TARGET_UNAVAILABLE; P5 calls 0

null result
= internal invariant failure; never defaults to VALID

callback retention at every terminal
= 0
~~~

Any `RuntimeException` or `Error` propagates as the identical object. Even after
`VALID`, the P5 V0 root target remains `NO_TARGET`; the advisory entity is discarded.

### 59.27 Token-Safe P5 Ingress

P7-S3-R1 may add exactly this package-private operation to the existing root-package
`SkillRuntimeService`:

~~~java
RuntimeAdmissionResult admitAuthenticatedPlayerCast(
        MinecraftServer server,
        ServerPlayer actor,
        SkillReference exactReference);
~~~

The operation is synchronous and server-logic-thread-only. It preserves the exact
reference and constructs the following fixed P5 root before tail-calling the
existing `admitRoot` at most once:

| Coordinate | Fixed value or owner |
| --- | --- |
| caller-supplied runtime token | `0` |
| caller-supplied `EventId` | `0` |
| runtime token | bound internally by P5 |
| `EventId` | created internally by P5 |
| skill reference | the exact supplied reference |
| latest lookup | `0` |
| node index | `0` |
| trigger cause | `gramarye:active_cast` |
| delay ticks | `0` |
| deadline horizon ticks | `0` |
| root depth | `0`, minted by P5 |
| root suborder/child sequence | `0`, minted by P5 |
| budget attribution and origin | exact authenticated actor under the P5-bound server token |
| target | `NO_TARGET` |
| execution data | no-runtime-execution-data value |
| persistence/retention | `MEMORY_ONLY` |
| existing `admitRoot` calls | at most `1` |

Wrong-thread ingress returns the existing typed P5 `WrongThread` result with zero
mutation. The method does not duplicate admission logic, insert directly into the
queue, pin outside the P5 owner, publish a child, or call P6. Its result and the
method itself remain package-private.

### 60.4 F06 Exact Gap

The sole current login event owner is
`com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.definition.submission.SkillSubmissionRecoveryService`.
Its `onPlayerLoggedIn(PlayerEvent.PlayerLoggedInEvent)` method completes P4-D
recovery and invokes the public sealed
`P4E2OnlineReconciliationDependency.reconcileAfterRecovery(...)` continuation in
the same synchronous server-logic-thread call chain.

The exact P4-E2 terminal result is known only inside the package-private
`P4E2OnlineReconciliationCoordinator`. Its normal terminal variants are
`NoChanges`, `RecoveryChanged`, and `Changed`. Its non-normal terminals are
`Deferred`, `Failed`, and `GenerationExhausted`. The public E2 dependency returns
`void`, so the submission-package owner cannot infer that classification after the
call.

The sole production P7 session owner is the package-private
`P7ServerSessionService` retained by the package-private
`P7NetworkComposition`. Neither P4 package can name or acquire that service. Before
this section there was no Java-legal typed path that simultaneously preserved the
unique P4 listener, the exact E2 result coordinate, the exact P7 session identity,
and the zero-locator/zero-reflection boundary.

### 60.5 F10 Exact Gap

The current `P7ReloadAdmissionGate` is package-private, event-unwired, and permits
mutation only from the server logic thread. The locked NeoForge 21.1.241
`AddReloadListenerEvent` is raised from the continuation of background reloadable
registry work. Its handler therefore has no server-logic-thread guarantee. Calling
the existing server-thread-only gate mutation there is invalid.

The locked completion coordinate is usable: `MinecraftServer.reloadResources(...)`
applies loaded resources with `thenAcceptAsync(..., this)`, then
`PlayerList.reloadResources()` posts `OnDatapackSyncEvent` with `player == null` on
the server logic thread. Before this section, however, there was no authorized
state transition connecting the earliest locked start signal to that completion
without mutating server-owned queue/session/world state off-thread or creating a
P7 worker/future chain.

### 60.6 F19 Exact Gap

The locked server-to-player send operation has a synchronous `void` submission
boundary. A normal return does not prove remote delivery or client application.
Before this section, authority did not uniquely decide:

- whether a normal return advances a sync-family sequence;
- whether a synchronous throw advances or restores that sequence;
- whether an ACK send failure invalidates the session;
- whether cooldown failure after successful mana submission rolls mana back;
- whether a partial full-sync submission is retried; or
- how sequence exhaustion interacts with the fixed mana-then-cooldown order.

Those observable transitions are fixed in §§60.22-60.30.

~~~text
PlayerLoggedInEvent
~~~

For `Deferred`, `Failed`, `GenerationExhausted`, quarantine, unavailable, or an

The internal P7 lifecycle outcome is not returned to P4:

| P7 lifecycle outcome | Required terminal behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `OPENED` | create the epoch, initialize intent/rate/sync state, and request the initial full snapshot |
| `ALREADY_ACTIVE` | preserve the existing session; create no second session or duplicate initial snapshot |
| `CAPACITY_REJECTED` | create no partial session; record one bounded diagnostic and disconnect the exact current actor once |
| `EPOCH_EXHAUSTED` | create no partial session; record one bounded diagnostic and disconnect the exact current actor once |
| `INTERNAL_FAULT` | create no partial session; enter the existing server fault path |

An unexpected port `RuntimeException` or `Error` propagates unchanged. P4 does not
translate it into a successful E2 terminal.

### 60.16 Cross-Thread Close-Request Exception

P7-S4 may add exactly one cross-thread-safe monotonic close-request scalar to
`P7ReloadAdmissionGate`. The recommended source form is one
`AtomicBoolean closeRequested`; the only equivalent is one `volatile boolean` with
the exact synchronized read/consume transition. Two close-request truths are not
permitted.

The exact package-private operation is logically:

~~~java
void requestReloadClose()
~~~

Its only permitted transition is `false -> true`; repeated `true -> true` is
idempotent. It may return `void` or an internal typed scalar result. It cannot open
the gate, clear the request, read or mutate sessions, snapshot players, mutate the
reconciliation queue, consume global work, alter a sync sequence, send a payload,
invoke P5/P6, retain the event/server/player, or schedule work.

This is the only P7 non-server-thread mutable product transition authorized by this
section. It creates no worker, executor, future chain, timer, or background cleanup.

### 60.17 Reload Gate State Model

The reload gate owns exactly two semantic coordinates:

1. the one JMM-safe `closeRequested` Boolean-like scalar; and
2. the server-thread-owned phase `OPEN` or `RECONCILING`.

Effective admission is closed when:

~~~text
closeRequested == true OR phase == RECONCILING
~~~

The server-thread admission path reads this effective condition before global-work,
rate, or sequence mutation. A closed gate yields existing
`RELOAD_IN_PROGRESS`/`UNAVAILABLE`, sequence consumption zero, and P5 calls zero.

| Current phase | `closeRequested` | Effective admission | Queue ownership | Permitted transition owner |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `OPEN` | `false` | open | server thread; normally periodic-only work | server thread |
| `OPEN` | `true` | closed | unchanged by background request | background may only set request |
| `RECONCILING` | `false` | closed | server-thread reconciliation set | server thread |
| `RECONCILING` | `true` | closed | current set continues; newer reload remains pending | background sets request; server owns everything else |

Public gate API and persistent gate state are both zero.

### 60.18 Start Event Allocation

P7 has exactly one reload-start owner. It handles
`AddReloadListenerEvent` and performs exactly one product call:

~~~text
reloadGate.requestReloadClose()
~~~

It does not call `event.addListener(...)`, obtain a server/player, inspect resources,
create a completion stage, or mutate any queue/session/world state. Duplicate event
delivery before completion is an idempotent repeated request, not a second queue or
second owner.

Other subsystems may retain their own reload listeners. The direct P7 rule is exact:
P7 reload-start owners one, P7 close-request call sites one, and P7 background
non-scalar mutations zero.

### 60.19 Completion Event Allocation

P7 has exactly one reload-completion owner. It handles
`OnDatapackSyncEvent` only when `getPlayer() == null`. A joining-player datapack-sync
event is not a reload completion and does not consume the close request.

On the server logic thread, completion performs this order:

1. ensure the gate is effectively closed at completion entry;
2. atomically consume the currently coalesced close request;
3. immediately on the same server turn set the phase to `RECONCILING`;
4. if no request was observed, record the bounded missing-start diagnostic;
5. snapshot active session UUID scalars only;
6. sort deterministically and coalesce into the sole bounded set;
7. retain no live player, server, level, event, or resource object; and
8. defer bounded processing to the exact server-tick owner.

No server admission can interleave between request consumption and the immediate
phase transition. A background start after the atomic consume sets the scalar back
to `true`, remains a newer pending request, and cannot be cleared by this completion.

The completion handler sends no unbounded loop and processes no more than the
server-thread bounds in §60.20.

### 60.20 Queue and Reopen Semantics

The existing §58 reconciliation model remains exact:

~~~text
coalesced queue/set identities
= exact 1

retained element
= authenticated UUID scalar only

capacity
= 256

maximum processed per server tick
= 16

work per processed session
= one unit from the existing shared GLOBAL_WORK budget of 64 per tick

live ServerPlayer retention
= 0
~~~

Each processed UUID is revalidated against the current UUID/epoch session and the
current player object. A stale or missing queue entry is skipped and removed from
the reconciliation set; this path cannot remove a newer or otherwise current
session. An eligible session submits a full mana/cooldown snapshot under
§§60.23-60.29. If shared global work is unavailable, the UUID remains coalesced for
a later tick; there is no immediate loop or retry queue.

When the set drains, the server thread performs exactly this test:

| Queue empty | `closeRequested` | Current phase | Next phase | Result |
| ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `false` | either | `RECONCILING` | `RECONCILING` | continue bounded drain |
| `true` | `false` | `RECONCILING` | `OPEN` | reopen exactly once |
| `true` | `true` | `RECONCILING` | `RECONCILING` | remain closed and await the matching later completion |

Only the server thread may transition the phase to `OPEN`.

### 60.21 Duplicate and Overlapping Reloads

The exact transition table is:

| Signal | Prior state | Atomic/server transition | Queue action | Reopen consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| start | `OPEN,false` | request `false -> true` | none | effective gate closes immediately |
| duplicate start before completion | `OPEN,true` | idempotent `true -> true` | none | remains closed; duplicate is coalesced |
| completion with request | either phase, request `true` | server consumes the observed request to `false`, then immediately enters/stays `RECONCILING` | merge sorted active UUID snapshot into sole set | open only after drain if no later request |
| start during reconciliation | `RECONCILING,false` | request `false -> true` | current set continues unchanged | current drain cannot reopen gate |
| repeated start during reconciliation | `RECONCILING,true` | idempotent `true -> true` | current set continues unchanged | remains closed |
| later completion during reconciliation | `RECONCILING,true` | consume the observed request, then immediately keep phase `RECONCILING` | merge/coalesce a fresh active UUID snapshot | drain combined set, then reopen if request false |
| completion without observed start | either phase, request `false` | enter/stay `RECONCILING`; preserve false | snapshot and process normally; record coarse diagnostic | reopen only after drain and no request |

The Boolean request intentionally coalesces duplicate start signals before a
completion. A start observed after completion consumption remains `true` and cannot
be lost by the current drain. The model has one request truth, one queue, and one
server-owned phase.

### 60.22 F19 Locked Send Semantics

The selected ordinary server-thread ACK and sync sender uses the locked inherited
server-player connection operation:

~~~java
actor.connection.send(CustomPacketPayload payload)
~~~

The declaring inherited surface is
`IServerCommonPacketListenerExtension.send(CustomPacketPayload)` and its exact JVM
descriptor is
`(Lnet/minecraft/network/protocol/common/custom/CustomPacketPayload;)V`. The P7
sender passes exactly one payload per invocation. A normal return is a local
submission boundary with the exact semantic label
`SUBMITTED_TO_CURRENT_CONNECTION`; P7's bounded internal classification remains
`SUBMITTED`. A synchronous `RuntimeException` or `Error` observed at the P7 sender
boundary is a submission failure. `ServerCommonPacketListenerImpl.send`
may wrap a lower synchronous connection fault in `ReportedException` before P7
observes it; P7 must propagate the identical object that P7 itself receives.

The only different send coordinate is the already-authorized immediate
network-thread BUSY response:

~~~java
context.reply(CustomPacketPayload payload)
~~~

Its declaring surface is `IPayloadContext.reply(CustomPacketPayload)` with the same
parameter-and-void-return descriptor. It is used only for that immediate BUSY path;
ordinary ACK, mana, and cooldown output never uses it. Mixed-side packet distributor
helpers are forbidden. No common/server P7 source gains a client-only descriptor or
client-bytecode dependency.

P7 installs no packet-send listener, asynchronous delivery callback, future,
polling state, or retry queue. The exact typed disconnect operation remains the
current player connection's
`ServerCommonPacketListenerImpl.disconnect(Component)` route, with exact descriptor
`(Lnet/minecraft/network/chat/Component;)V`. A synchronous ACK/mana/cooldown
submission-failure terminal invokes it exactly once if and only if the actor is
still current; no other failure branch may duplicate that invocation.

### 60.23 SUBMITTED Versus DELIVERED

Every typed P7 send invocation has exactly two locally observable results:

| P7 result | Observation | Delivery claim | Retained tracking |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| `SUBMITTED` | the locked send call returns normally: `SUBMITTED_TO_CURRENT_CONNECTION` | no claim of remote delivery, decode, application, or acknowledgement | `0` |
| `SUBMISSION_FAILED` | the locked send call synchronously throws the object observed by P7 | no packet-delivery claim | `0` |

A disconnect, channel drop, or remote failure after normal return does not change a
`SUBMITTED` transition. P7 V0 has no delivery acknowledgement. Its guarantee is
at-most-once local submission per trigger, not exactly-once wire delivery.

Periodic full snapshots and reconnect are later convergence mechanisms. They are
not retries of the prior payload and carry no packet history.

### 60.24 ACK Failure Transition

An ACK is attempted only when the exact UUID/epoch session is current, the actor is
re-resolved and current, and an ACK candidate exists. There is no ACK queue.

| ACK condition | Send calls | Intent/P5 state | Session action | Disconnect | Throwable action | Retry |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| no candidate or stale/disconnected actor/session | `0` | unchanged from completed authorization stage | existing lifecycle result only | as already required by that result | none | `0` |
| send returns normally | `1` | no additional mutation or rollback | preserve current session unless another terminal rule already applies | `0` from send success | none | `0` |
| send throws `RuntimeException` or `Error` | `1` | never roll back intent sequence or P5 admission | invalidate exact current session and remove session-owned rate/sync state | exactly `1` if the actor remains current | rethrow the same object observed by P7; retain none | `0` |
| cleanup also throws after send failure | `1` | never roll back | every exact-session invalidation/clearing stage is still attempted once | exactly `1` attempt if the actor remains current | original send object stays primary; cleanup objects may be suppressed; retain none | `0` |

The synchronous ACK-failure transition order is exact:

1. do not roll back the consumed intent sequence or any P5 admission result;
2. invalidate the exact current UUID/epoch session;
3. clear all state owned by that session, including transient sync and rate state;
4. invoke disconnect exactly once if the actor is still the current player object;
5. record one bounded coarse `P7IntentFailureReason.INTERNAL_SERVER_FAULT`
   diagnostic; and
6. rethrow the identical `RuntimeException` or `Error` observed by P7.

Each cleanup stage is isolated so that its own failure does not skip the remaining
authorized cleanup attempts. Such cleanup objects may be attached as suppressed to
the original send object, which remains primary; none is retained after the call
terminates. Failed ACK wire output, fallback ACK count, and retry count are zero.

For the existing eighth `RATE_LIMITED` strike terminal, the exact current session
remains current through the one best-effort ACK submission. After a normal return,
P7 invalidates that exact UUID/epoch and performs the already-authorized terminal
disconnect once. If submission throws, the failure invalidation path subsumes the
rate terminal cleanup and must not produce a second disconnect attempt.

### 60.25 Per-Family Sequence Advancement

Mana and cooldown each own an independent positive-long per-session sequence. Both
begin at `1`. No sequence is reserved or advanced before its own send call.

| Family pre-state | Own send outcome | Own next state | Other family | Session consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| current `n`, `1 <= n < Long.MAX_VALUE` | normal return | current becomes `n + 1` | unchanged unless its own later send returns normally | continue the full-set order |
| current `Long.MAX_VALUE` | normal return | family becomes `EXHAUSTED`; no wrap | unchanged unless its own later send returns normally | finish the permitted remaining family send, then invalidate/disconnect |
| current `n` | synchronous throw | remains `n` | unchanged, except an earlier family already submitted remains advanced | invalidate/disconnect and rethrow same observed object |
| already `EXHAUSTED` before full-sync start | no send | remains `EXHAUSTED` | no send and no mutation | invalidate/disconnect immediately |

Only a normal local submission advances or exhausts that payload family's sequence.
Remote delivery is irrelevant to this state transition.

### 60.26 Full-Sync Send Order

A full synchronization set has this fixed order:

1. materialize and validate the current mana and cooldown full snapshots;
2. submit mana exactly once;
3. only after mana returns normally, submit cooldown exactly once; and
4. classify the full set as submitted only if both calls return normally.

Preconditions are an exact current UUID/epoch session, current re-resolved actor,
one admitted unit from the existing shared global-work owner, valid snapshot values,
and neither family pre-exhausted. The production cooldown snapshot is the existing
authorized immutable empty full snapshot; P7 invents no cooldown truth.

There is no bundle submission, compensating send, ACK queue, sync retry queue, or
delta snapshot.

### 60.27 Partial Mana/Cooldown Failure

The full-set transition table is exact:

| Case | Mana call | Cooldown call | Mana sequence | Cooldown sequence | Full-set result | Terminal action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | normal | normal | advance or exhaust | advance or exhaust | `SUBMITTED` | preserve unless either family exhausted; then invalidate/disconnect |
| B | throws | `0` | unchanged | unchanged | `SUBMISSION_FAILED` | invalidate session, disconnect once, rethrow same observed object |
| C | normal | throws | remains advanced or exhausted | unchanged | `SUBMISSION_FAILED` | no mana rollback; invalidate session, disconnect once, rethrow same observed object |

Case C cannot report a successful full set. It cannot submit mana again, roll mana
back, send a compensating payload, retry cooldown, or retain the failed payload.

### 60.28 Sync Exhaustion

Each family has the exact range `1..Long.MAX_VALUE`. A normal send at a value below
the maximum advances by checked addition. A normal send at the maximum marks only
that family exhausted. No wrap is permitted.

If mana reaches exhaustion during a full set, cooldown is still submitted once in
the fixed order. If cooldown then returns normally, the exact session is invalidated
and disconnected after both submissions, whether or not cooldown also reached its
maximum. If cooldown throws, Case C in §60.27 applies and mana remains exhausted.

If cooldown reaches exhaustion after a normal mana submission, the session is
invalidated and disconnected after the cooldown call. If either family was already
exhausted before full-sync processing, both payload send counts are zero and the
session is immediately invalidated and disconnected.

Reconnect creates a new epoch and resets both sequences to `1`; it never revives an
exhausted session.

### 60.29 Session Invalidation and Disconnect

Every synchronous ACK, mana, or cooldown submission failure has one fail-closed
session result:

~~~text
exact current session
= INVALIDATED

all session-owned transient intent/rate/sync/throttle state
= REMOVED

pending-permit terminalization
= PRESERVES THE UNCHANGED F14 SOLE OWNER AND ARITHMETIC

P5 admission state rollback
= 0

P6 mana transaction/state rollback
= 0

disconnect attempts
= exactly 1 when the current actor remains available

retry / fallback payload
= 0 / 0
~~~

Invalidation uses UUID plus epoch and cannot remove a newer reconnect session. The
client mirror clears through the existing client disconnect/world-unload lifecycle.
Reconnect creates a new session and initial full snapshot; it is not a retry of the
failed submission.

### 60.30 Diagnostic and Wire Policy

Submission failure is classified as coarse `INTERNAL_SERVER_FAULT` for the bounded
server diagnostic path only. A diagnostic record may contain only the authenticated
UUID, authoritative server tick, coarse reason, and saturating count. Raw packet,
payload, aim, target, definition, stack, exception class/message, and `Throwable`
retention are zero.

| Failure | Wire result | Diagnostic | Throwable retention |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| ACK submission failure | failed ACK wire count `0`; no fallback | one bounded coarse internal-fault observation | `0` |
| mana submission failure | cooldown call `0`; no retry | one bounded coarse internal-fault observation | `0` |
| cooldown submission failure after mana success | mana remains submitted; no compensating send | one bounded coarse internal-fault observation | `0` |
| cleanup failure | no additional wire output | cleanup object may be suppressed on primary | `0` after terminal |

No internal fault detail is sent to the client.

### 61.3 P8 Controlled Acceptance and P9 Actual Gameplay Allocation

The six existing acceptance statements remain, with this exact allocation:

| Acceptance | P8 proof | P9 proof |
|---|---|---|
| `CAST_RELEASE` reaches a client | A trusted controlled `PRESENTATION_ONLY` server source enters the production emitter, budget, codec, NETWORK handoff, and client dispatch. | An actual cast/action commit emits through the same path. |
| `HIT` reaches tracking clients | A trusted controlled source enters the production emitter and the actual server watcher/range selector. | An actual projectile produces an authoritative hit and the event. |
| Missing Profile falls back | Pure resolver, catalog, and client factory/asset tests exercise per-channel fallback. | The actual playable slice repeats the condition. |
| Bad Appearance does not block cast | Existing P3/P4 fallback plus P8 integration prove that only presentation is degraded. | An actual cast repeats the assertion. |
| Particles disabled still leaves damage intact | P8 proves preferences and visual drop/failure cannot reach or alter an injected, already-fixed applied fact. It makes no actual-damage claim. | P9 proves one real authoritative damage mutation still occurs with particles disabled. |
| No per-particle synchronization | P8 wire/source tests prove that only a bounded event is sent. | P9 repeats inspection on the actual binding. |

Controlled sources are available only to trusted tests or an explicitly internal
presentation harness. They have no client-authoritative route, no arbitrary public
emit method, no world-mutation bypass, and no effect on gameplay success/failure
statistics. P8 V0 emits only wire kind codes `CAST_RELEASE(1)` and `HIT(3)`.
Reserving the other kind codes does not require P8 to implement their gameplay
systems.

The production kind mapper recognizes existing server trigger key
`gramarye:active_cast` as `CAST_RELEASE`. The exact controlled HIT coordinate is
`gramarye:p8_controlled_hit`; it is never registered as a gameplay trigger, decoded
from a client, accepted by normal submission, or emitted by P7. Only the same-package
direct qualification harness can construct that P5 test event and pair it with P6
test-double applied truth. All other P8-time trigger keys emit zero presentation
events. P9 later adds the real authoritative hit binding without changing the P8
kind code or controlled-source classification.

### 61.4 Exact P6 Post-Commit Applied-Fact Seam

The existing sole public bridge operation is replaced, not overloaded, by:

```java
public static void execute(
        P6RuntimeExecutionCapability capability,
        ServerPlayer actor,
        ResourceLocation actionTypeKey,
        long requestId,
        long sourceEventId,
        UUID targetId,
        long magnitude,
        long manaCost,
        GuardPort guard,
        AppliedFactObserver observer)
```

This declaration remains on
`com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.runtime.mana.P6RuntimeExecutionBridge`; it has no overload,
no checked exception, and still returns `void`. The same outer type gains exactly
these five public nested roles:

```java
@FunctionalInterface
public interface AppliedFactObserver {
    void observe(AppliedFact fact);
}

public record AppliedFact(
        AppliedTerminal terminal,
        int primaryMutationCount,
        List<AppliedStep> appliedSteps) {}

public record AppliedStep(int stepIndex, AppliedStepKind kind) {}

public enum AppliedStepKind {
    APPLIED,
    APPLIED_WITH_FAILURE
}

public enum AppliedTerminal {
    SUCCEEDED,
    PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED
}
```

The public compact record constructors are mandatory. `AppliedFact` requires
non-null fields and `List.copyOf`, one through eight steps, a
`primaryMutationCount` from one through eight and not less than the list size, and
contiguous indices starting at zero. `APPLIED_WITH_FAILURE` appears at most once,
only last, and only with `PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED`; `SUCCEEDED` contains only `APPLIED`.
`AppliedStep.stepIndex` is in `[0,7]`. These validation failures are invariant
failures, not presentation fallback.

The bridge validates capability non-null first, before reading any other argument.
It then validates actor, action key, target ID, guard, and observer non-null before
creating an invocation/account or calling the engine. A null observer causes the
existing package-private `P6ExecutionInvariantException` even when the eventual
terminal would have produced no fact; no gameplay or presentation work occurs. No
observer access precedes capability validation.

Inside `P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.executeCore`, the package-private
`ActionDamageTransactionResult` is finalized first. Existing `handleResult(result)`
runs before observation, thereby preserving terminal/invariant handling. Only then
does one bounded scan of the already-final trace copy `STEP_APPLIED` as `APPLIED`,
copy `STEP_APPLIED_WITH_FAILURE` as `APPLIED_WITH_FAILURE`, and omit
`STEP_NOT_APPLIED`.

| P6 terminal truth | Observer calls |
|---|---|
| `SUCCEEDED` with applied primary work | Exactly one, all copied steps `APPLIED`. |
| `PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED` | Exactly one for the still-applied prefix. A terminal `STEP_NOT_APPLIED` is omitted; an applied-with-failure step is the optional final copied step. |
| `REJECTED`, `FAILED`, or no primary mutation | Zero. |
| `COMPENSATED` | Zero because compensation removed the primary mutation. |
| `COMPENSATION_FAILED` | Zero; the existing invariant failure occurs. |

For each copied `AppliedStep`, the service offers at most one presentation event,
so an observer call creates at most eight logical offers. The applied step index and
`sourceEventId` are the internal fact identity used by exact coalescing. A primary
mutation count without a corresponding copied applied step never fabricates an
event. The mapper above selects `CAST_RELEASE` or controlled `HIT`; position,
direction, and optional entity numbers are copied from the same call-scoped resolved
context. `CAST_RELEASE` requires a resolved loaded player/entity origin and uses its
position; when a distinct resolved target position exists its direction is the
normalized origin-to-target vector, otherwise it is the origin entity’s normalized
look vector. `HIT` requires a resolved loaded entity/player target, uses that target
position, and the normalized origin-to-target vector.
Missing/non-finite required geometry drops that offer without changing the applied
fact.

The copy exposes no P6 result, trace, mana account, receipt, failure object, actor,
target object, definition, node, lease, pin, context, or `Throwable`. It never
re-executes an effect, changes mana/compensation/children, or performs latest lookup.

The exact root handoff is:

```java
final class P8AppliedFactHandoff
        implements P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.AppliedFactObserver {
    @Override
    public void observe(P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.AppliedFact fact);
}
```

`com.yo1no.gramarye.P8AppliedFactHandoff` is package-private final and has exactly
the Java-mandated public `observe` override, with no other public/protected field,
constructor, or method. Its exact call-scoped fields are the same
`P8ServerPresentationService`, `RuntimeEvent`, and `RuntimeExecutionContext` objects
supplied by the root adapter. Before returning it copies only bounded immutable
scalars, colors, Profile IDs, positions/direction, event/source IDs, and UUIDs into
the current-tick P8 value. It retains none of those three input objects or the fact.
Its sole constructor is the package-private non-null constructor
`P8AppliedFactHandoff(P8ServerPresentationService service, RuntimeEvent event,
RuntimeExecutionContext context)`; overloads and factories are zero. The adapter
passes the same three call-scoped objects named above, and construction itself has
no side effect.

`observe` catches `RuntimeException` only around
`P8ServerPresentationService.offerApplied(...)`, records fixed code
`OBSERVER_RUNTIME_EXCEPTION`, discards the complete call-scoped presentation batch,
and returns. The service stages all buffer, coalescing, and budget mutations in
call-scoped scratch and publishes them only after the entire `offerApplied` call
completes normally. On that caught exception no event or partial prefix from the
call remains and no prior buffer entry is changed; sequence values already allocated
under §61.11 remain consumed. It retains no
exception class, message, stack, or object. The service has a non-throwing `finally`
cleanup for its call-scoped scratch. `Error` is not caught by the handoff; cleanup
runs and the exact same object propagates through P6, the adapter, and P5. Gameplay
`RuntimeException`/`Error` outside this exact observer call remains governed by P5/P6
and is never swallowed by P8. P8 packet work occurs only in a later server post-tick
drain, so a visual send failure cannot retroactively trip the gameplay breaker.

### 61.5 Common Startup Extension API

The dedicated-server-safe public package is
`com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.presentation.api`. Its exact declared public surface is:

```java
public interface ProfileConfiguration {}

public enum ProfileChannel {
    SOUND(0), PARTICLE(1), TRAIL(2);
    public int wireCode();
    public static Optional<ProfileChannel> fromWireCode(int code);
}

public final class ClientFactoryKey<C extends ProfileConfiguration> {
    public ClientFactoryKey(ResourceLocation id);
    public ResourceLocation id();
}

public record ProfileCost(
        int particleStarts,
        int soundStarts,
        int trailStarts,
        int trailSegments,
        int lifetimeTicks) {}

public record ProfileTypeCapabilities(
        boolean supportsPrimaryColor,
        boolean supportsSecondaryColor,
        boolean supportsDirection,
        boolean supportsTrail,
        AppearanceParameterPolicy adjustableParameters) {}

public interface ProfileType<C extends ProfileConfiguration> {
    int currentConfigurationVersion();
    ProfileChannel channel();
    MapCodec<C> configurationCodec();
    ClientFactoryKey<C> clientFactoryKey();
    ProfileTypeCapabilities capabilities();
    ProfileCost estimateCost(C configuration);
    ValidationResult validate(C configuration, ValidationContext context);
}
```

Here `AppearanceParameterPolicy` is
`com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.capability.AppearanceParameterPolicy`, and
`ValidationResult`/`ValidationContext` are the existing public types in
`com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.validation`. All returns and constructor inputs are
non-null. A factory-key ID is at most 128 UTF-8 bytes. Configuration version is
`[0,65535]`. The adjustable map contains at most 16 entries and each parameter key
is at most 32 UTF-8 bytes. A baked/validated `ProfileCost` is bounded to particle
starts `[0,256]`, sound starts `[0,8]`, trail starts `[0,1]`, trail segments
`[0,48]`, and lifetime `[1,120]`. Invalid, null, duplicate, mismatched, over-cap, or
late startup registration fails the startup bake; it is not dynamically omitted.

`ClientFactoryKey` deliberately retains object identity semantics and does not
override `equals` or `hashCode`. The exact same generic key object is the common
type/client binding witness; only `key.id()` crosses the wire. The API accepts
bounded configuration and declarative cost/capability data. It exposes no mutable
catalog, session, P5/P6 service, world, runtime replacement, file/path/URL, Java
class name, shader source, or script.

`com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.api.registry.MagicRegistries` gains exactly:

```java
public static final ResourceKey<Registry<ProfileType<?>>> PROFILE_TYPE_REGISTRY_KEY;
public static final DeferredRegister<ProfileType<?>> PROFILE_TYPES;
public static Registry<ProfileType<?>> profileTypeRegistry();
```

`PROFILE_TYPE_REGISTRY_KEY` has exact registry location
`gramarye:profile_type`.
The registry is built with `maxId(63)`, `sync(false)`, and an `onBake` validation.
The registry and all third-party `DeferredRegister`s freeze through the normal
NeoForge registration lifecycle; no P8 `register`, `replace`, unfreeze, or runtime
mutation API exists. The registry contains at most 64 types, including all built-ins.

### 61.6 Client Startup Extension API

The client-only public package is
`com.yo1no.gramarye.client.presentation.api`; common/server classes never mention or
load it. Its exact surface is:

```java
public interface ClientProfileFactory<C extends ProfileConfiguration> {
    Availability availability(C configuration, AssetView assets);
    Result present(C configuration, Input input, Output output);

    enum Availability { AVAILABLE, UNAVAILABLE }
    enum Result { PRESENTED, UNAVAILABLE }

    interface AssetView {
        boolean soundExists(ResourceLocation id);
        boolean particleExists(ResourceLocation id);
        boolean resourceExists(ResourceLocation id);
    }

    interface Input {
        int eventKindCode();
        OptionalInt sourceEntityId();
        OptionalInt targetEntityId();
        double x(); double y(); double z();
        float directionX(); float directionY(); float directionZ();
        int primaryArgb(); int secondaryArgb(); int intensity();
        OptionalInt override(ResourceLocation key);
        long visualSeed(); long sequence();
    }

    interface Output {
        boolean particle(Particle command);
        boolean sound(Sound command);
        boolean trail(Trail command);
    }

    record Particle(
            ResourceLocation particleTypeId,
            double x, double y, double z,
            double velocityX, double velocityY, double velocityZ,
            int argb, float size, int lifetimeTicks) {}

    record Sound(
            ResourceLocation soundEventId,
            double x, double y, double z,
            float volume, float pitch) {}

    record Trail(
            ResourceLocation particleTypeId,
            OptionalInt trackedEntityId,
            double x, double y, double z,
            int argb, float size,
            int lifetimeTicks, int sampleIntervalTicks) {}
}

public record ClientProfileFactoryRegistration<C extends ProfileConfiguration>(
        ClientFactoryKey<C> key,
        ClientProfileFactory<C> factory) {}

public final class ClientProfileFactories {
    public static final ResourceKey<
            Registry<ClientProfileFactoryRegistration<?>>> REGISTRY_KEY;
    public static Registry<ClientProfileFactoryRegistration<?>> registry();
}
```

`ClientProfileFactories.REGISTRY_KEY` has exact registry location
`gramarye:client_profile_factory`.
`GramaryeClient` creates this registry only on the client, with `maxId(63)`,
`sync(false)`, and `onBake` validation. Third-party client code uses its own
`DeferredRegister` against `REGISTRY_KEY`. At bake, registry entry ID must equal
`registration.key().id()` and key object identity must equal the unique local frozen
`ProfileType.clientFactoryKey()`. Duplicate, null, mismatch, or over-64 binding is a
startup failure. A missing non-built-in binding is legal and makes the type locally
unavailable. All three built-in type/factory bindings are startup invariants;
default-asset availability is checked against each active client resource generation
and is not a registry-bake fact.

The two wildcard registries meet at exactly one client-only package-private generic
capture boundary. For a captured `ProfileType<C>`, that boundary first verifies the
catalog type ID, channel, configuration version, client-factory registry entry ID,
wire factory ID, and exact reference identity
`registration.key() == type.clientFactoryKey()`, and decodes/validates the
configuration as `C`. Only after those checks may its one generic helper contain the
sole localized `ClientProfileFactoryRegistration<?>` to
`ClientProfileFactoryRegistration<C>` unchecked cast, with exact
`@SuppressWarnings("unchecked")` scope on that helper. It returns a package-private
immutable bound pair retaining the same `C` for configuration validation,
`availability`, and `present`; the pair cannot escape the client execution owner.
Key/ID/type/version mismatch fails unavailable before the cast. Raw types,
`Object` transport, reflection, a second unchecked cast/suppression, and any public
binding/helper surface are zero.

Every implementation method required by these public interfaces is a mandatory
public Java override. `AssetView` is immutable query authority. `Input` contains only
bounded values/IDs. `Output` is the only presentation side-effect route and charges
the actual client budget before each platform call. It accepts only the factory’s
channel and only an asset ID of at most 128 UTF-8 bytes present in the current
resource index. Every command position is finite, within X/Z
`[-30000000,30000000]` and Y `[-2048,2048]`, and at squared distance at most 4096
from the event input position. Particle velocity components are finite in
`[-16,16]` blocks/tick. Particle/trail size must be finite in `(0,16]`, lifetime in
`[1,120]`, and trail interval in `[1,120]`; a present tracked entity number is in
`[1,2147483647]`. Sound volume is finite `[0,1]` and pitch `[0.5,2]`. Invalid or
resource-stale commands return `false` without a platform call.

Factory `availability` or `present` `RuntimeException` is contained at that exact
extension call, after non-throwing cleanup, then consumes the attempt, records a
bounded code, and permits the single default fallback. `Error` receives cleanup and
propagates. No `Throwable` is retained. This is a cooperative extension boundary,
not a sandbox for arbitrary code already loaded into the JVM.

### 61.7 Profile Types, Instances, Defaults, and Availability

The common startup registry reserves these exact type IDs and factory-key IDs:

| Channel/code | Type ID and factory-key ID | Non-removable default instance |
|---|---|---|
| SOUND / `0` | `gramarye:sound` | `gramarye:default_sound` |
| PARTICLE / `1` | `gramarye:particle` | `gramarye:default_particle` |
| TRAIL / `2` | `gramarye:trail` | `gramarye:default_trail` |

The three types count inside the 64-type limit, leaving 61 third-party slots. The
three default instances count inside 64 instances per channel and 192 total,
leaving 63 non-default slots per channel. Defaults are synthesized after every
successful parse, cannot be removed or replaced by datapack content, and therefore
make a valid server catalog contain at least three entries. A resource colliding
with a reserved default ID is an invalid ordinary entry and is omitted with a
bounded diagnostic.

The V0 built-in default configurations are fixed as follows. Object member order in
source JSON is irrelevant; canonical transmission sorts keys.

```json
{"sound":"minecraft:entity.experience_orb.pickup","volume_milli":600,"pitch_milli":1000}
{"particle":"minecraft:enchant","count":8,"speed_milli_blocks":50,"size_milli_blocks":250,"lifetime_ticks":20}
{"particle":"minecraft:enchant","segments":8,"sample_interval_ticks":2,"size_milli_blocks":200,"lifetime_ticks":16}
```

The rows correspond to sound, particle, and trail. Built-in codecs reject unknown
members and enforce all §61.12 limits. Resource presence is a client concern; the
common/server configuration contains only IDs and bounded numeric values.

Datapack Profile instances live at:

```text
data/<namespace>/gramarye/presentation_profiles/<path>.json
```

The Profile ID is `<namespace>:<path>`. The exact root shape is:

```json
{
  "format": 0,
  "type": "namespace:path",
  "type_version": 0,
  "configuration": {}
}
```

Only those four members are legal. `format` is exactly `0`; `type_version` is
`[0,65535]` and must equal the selected frozen type’s
`currentConfigurationVersion()`. V0 has no implicit version migration. The P8 reader
rejects duplicate JSON keys, bounds the source before parsing, and invokes the
registered `MapCodec` only inside an already-bounded configuration tree. Validation
and cost estimation must both succeed and fit the §61.12 per-instance maxima. The reader
retains the typed immutable configuration and its canonical sorted-key,
whitespace-free UTF-8 JSON, never the raw bytes/tree.

Locked `ResourceManager.listResources` produces lexicographically sorted effective
IDs. Platform enumeration performed inside that method is outside the P8 parser’s
own work budget. After it returns, P8 inspects at most the first 256 IDs, reads no
more than 16,385 bytes for each solely to obtain the one-byte oversize sentinel,
accepts/retains at most 16,384 bytes, and deterministically omits later IDs with one
bounded overflow diagnostic. Ordinary duplicate-ID replacement is already resolved
by resource-pack priority. An unknown type, wrong version/channel, invalid codec or
cost, overlong entry, or ordinary validation failure omits only that entry. An
unexpected loader/internal exception aborts the whole candidate. Capacity overflow
is resolved by ascending Profile ID: after defaults, the first legal entries fitting
both the per-channel and total limits are retained and excess entries are omitted.
Thus publication is always one complete bounded candidate, never a partially
mutated active snapshot.

One package-private immutable server snapshot owns the complete catalog and three
typed channel indices; the indices are views of that one object, not separate
truths. There is at most one active snapshot plus one pending candidate that runtime
lookup cannot reach. A stable, snapshot-backed instance of the existing public
`com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.definition.validation.ProfileAvailabilityView` is the
only validation adapter.

For `SOUND_PROFILE`, `PARTICLE_PROFILE`, and `TRAIL_PROFILE`, that adapter maps the
field to its channel and reports `AVAILABLE` only when the current active catalog
contains the ID in that channel. Absent or wrong-channel IDs report `MISSING`.
Before initial activation it reports `UNKNOWN`. Supplying
`PRIMARY_ARGB`, `SECONDARY_ARGB`, or `INTENSITY_MILLI` is a programming invariant
failure rather than a fabricated availability result. The adapter has stable object
identity while its owner atomically changes the referenced active snapshot.

A server Profile instance describes approved visual data; a client resource pack
supplies the referenced sound/particle/texture assets. A valid length-delimited
unknown client type is skipped without invoking its codec. A known type with a
missing/mismatched factory, version, asset, or locally invalid configuration is
marked unavailable without partially changing the client catalog. No Profile can
name a URL, filesystem path, class, shader source, or script.

### 61.8 Appearance Merge and Event Override Contract

The exact field-wise merge order is:

```text
module default → skill default → node override → trusted event patch
```

The module default is primary ARGB `0xFFFFFFFF`, secondary ARGB `0xFFFFFFFF`,
intensity `1000`, and the three built-in default Profile IDs from §61.7. Existing
skill `AppearanceDefinition` and node `AppearanceOverride` are reused directly.
For a scalar `OptionalInt`, absent means retain the preceding value and present means
replace it. For each Profile channel, `Inherit` retains, `Disabled` clears, and
`Specified(id)` replaces. There is no fourth state.

Existing P3/P4 storage owns its current behavior: type-correct out-of-policy numbers
may be clamped during tolerant storage decode, malformed bounded input may remain
`Unparsed`, over-hard-bound content becomes `Rejected`, and raw data remains only in
that owner. `Default`, `Unparsed`, or `Rejected` supplies no persisted overrides to
P8 and therefore resolves from the module default. P8 never reparses, copies, or
serializes that raw tree.

The event patch is a raw-free immutable pair consisting of the exact six-field
shape of existing `AppearanceOverride` and an immutable sorted map of zero through
eight `ResourceLocation` integer parameters. It is created only from trusted
server/action data. It is not public client input and is never persisted. Each key
is at most 32 UTF-8 bytes and unique. A parameter is legal only if:

1. the exact Action descriptor’s existing `AppearanceParameterPolicy` declares the
   key and value range;
2. at least one Profile type selected by the post-patch effective Appearance also
   declares the key; and
3. the value lies in the intersection of every applicable declared range.

Colors are all 32-bit ARGB bit patterns. Intensity is `[0,10000]`. Profile IDs must
be at most 128 UTF-8 bytes and resolve to the correct channel or its fallback. A
non-empty patch with any unknown key, wrong channel, absent capability, out-of-range
value, null, over-cap value, or invalid six-field value is ignored atomically,
records one bounded diagnostic, and leaves the already-fixed base appearance in
place. Event patches are never partially applied or clamped.

After merge, Profile resolution is independently performed per channel:

```text
specified/resolved ID → that channel's built-in default ID → disabled channel
```

The server replaces a missing/wrong-channel selected instance with the built-in
default before constructing the event. The internal effective value records a
bounded fallback/disabled reason for diagnostics, but that reason is not placed on
the wire. The client tries the transmitted instance/factory/asset and then the
same channel default at most once; if both are unavailable it drops only that
channel. Profile reload changes resolution for stable IDs and never creates or
edits a `SkillDocument` revision. An Appearance-only edit continues through the
existing immutable submission/store revision path.

The resulting event-side Appearance is immutable and contains only two ARGB ints,
one intensity int, zero or one resolved Profile ID for each channel, and the sorted
integer map. It contains no raw tree, mutable map, validator, availability view,
definition, node, action object, lease, or live gameplay object.

### 61.9 Exact P8 Wire Protocol

The existing unique
`com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.network.P7PayloadRegistrar` obtains
`registrar.versioned("gramarye-p8-v0")` from the same `RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent`
and adds exactly two non-optional `playToClient` registrations. The existing four
P7 registrations remain the exact `gramarye-p7-v0` family inventory. P8 adds no C2S
role, ACK, delivery tracker, or generic payload.

#### 61.9.1 `gramarye:profile_catalog`

The codec body has this exact order:

```text
u8        format = 0
i64       catalogGeneration, positive
VarInt    entryCount, canonical, 3..192
repeat entryCount, strictly ascending profileId:
  RL      profileId, UTF-8 payload <=128 bytes
  RL      typeId, UTF-8 payload <=128 bytes
  u8      channel, SOUND=0 / PARTICLE=1 / TRAIL=2
  RL      clientFactoryId, UTF-8 payload <=128 bytes
  VarInt  envelopeLength, canonical, 3..2048
  bytes   exact envelope slice:
    VarInt  configurationVersion, canonical, 0..65535
    bytes   remaining canonical sorted-key whitespace-free UTF-8 JSON object
```

The envelope length excludes its own VarInt prefix but includes configuration
version and JSON. The slice must be consumed exactly. Length delimitation lets an
unknown local type skip exactly one entry without decoding unknown configuration.
A known local type must match the frozen channel, factory-key ID, and supported
configuration version, then decode and validate the remaining JSON. Unavailable or
invalid known entries become unavailable entries with a bounded diagnostic; they
do not partially mutate the snapshot. Duplicate/unsorted IDs, invalid required
defaults, illegal code/version/count/string/length, truncation, trailing body bytes,
or body length over 491,520 is structural failure and installs nothing.

The worst legal entry is `130 + 130 + 1 + 130 + 2 + 2048 = 2441` bytes. The
maximum header is `1 + 8 + 2 = 11`; therefore `11 + 192 × 2441 = 468683`, leaving
22,837 bytes of the body limit. Canonical server output may be smaller but never
relies on compression.

#### 61.9.2 `gramarye:presentation_event`

The codec body has this exact order:

```text
u8        format = 0
i64       catalogGeneration, positive
u8        kind
u8        sourceFlags: bit0 sourceEntityId present,
                       bit1 targetEntityId present,
                       bits2..7 zero
[VarInt]  sourceEntityId when flagged, canonical positive <= Integer.MAX_VALUE
[VarInt]  targetEntityId when flagged, canonical positive <= Integer.MAX_VALUE
RL        dimension, UTF-8 payload <=128 bytes
f64 x, f64 y, f64 z, each finite
i16       directionXQ15
i16       directionYQ15
i16       directionZQ15
i32       primaryArgb
i32       secondaryArgb
selection sound
selection particle
selection trail
VarInt    overrideCount, canonical, 0..8
repeat overrideCount, strictly ascending unique key:
  RL      key, UTF-8 payload <=32 bytes
  i32     value
VarInt    intensity, canonical, 0..10000
i64       visualSeed, every bit pattern legal
i64       sequence, positive
```

Each selection is `u8 0` for disabled, or `u8 1` followed by a Profile RL of at
most 128 UTF-8 bytes for specified. `Inherit` is impossible after resolution and
has no wire code. Kind codes are fixed in frozen order:

```text
0 CAST_START             1 CAST_RELEASE          2 PROJECTILE_SPAWN
3 HIT                    4 EXPLOSION             5 SPLIT
6 CHAIN                  7 MARK_APPLY            8 MARK_TRIGGER
9 CONSTRUCT_SPAWN       10 CONSTRUCT_DESTROY
```

Other values are invalid. Q15 components are in `[-32767,32767]`; `-32768` and the
all-zero vector are invalid. The server starts with a finite non-zero direction,
normalizes it, rounds each clamped component times 32767, and rejects an all-zero
quantization. The client divides by 32767 and normalizes once. Position X/Z must be
within `[-30000000,30000000]` and Y within `[-2048,2048]`; the selected recipients
are additionally within 64 blocks in the same dimension.

The source summary is exactly the two presence flags and up to two connection-local
entity numeric IDs. It never carries entity UUID, player account, Skill ID/revision,
definition, owner, hidden action values, receipt, or debug text. The event contains
no individual particle position. Its computed worst codec body is 897 bytes and its
hard body limit remains 1024 bytes. Decoder and encoder require exact full consume.

#### 61.9.3 Decode and thread handoff

NETWORK decode checks readable body length before allocation, rejects non-canonical
VarInts and bounded strings before constructing `ResourceLocation`, and uses exact
bounded sub-slices. A structural codec failure throws the platform decoder failure
and closes the connection with zero catalog/event mutation. A semantic violation
found once a payload context exists calls
`IPayloadContext.disconnect(Component.translatable(
"disconnect.gramarye.invalid_presentation_payload"))`. No raw input or exception is
retained.

Only a fully valid payload can enter bounded client handoff. An event reserves the
shared event pool, captures the current connection, world, and resource generations,
and calls `enqueueWork` exactly once. A successful enqueue transfers reservation
ownership from the NETWORK handler to the main task and then, if admitted, to the
pending-event owner. The handler’s non-throwing `finally` releases only when that
transfer fails; the current owner releases exactly once on application, drop, or
lifecycle cleanup. The client-main event task rechecks all three captures plus the
payload’s exact installed catalog generation.

A catalog is connection-scoped and uses one latest-generation coalescing mailbox.
It captures and rechecks the connection generation only; client main evaluates it
against the then-current resource index. The transition from empty to occupied
schedules exactly one main drain. While occupied, a newer valid generation for the
same captured connection atomically replaces and releases the older mailbox value
without adding a task; an older/duplicate value drops, and the scheduled drain reads
the latest value. If a drain has already taken the slot, a later empty-to-occupied
transition schedules the next drain. Thus a newest valid catalog is never silently
dropped for slot capacity after the server has treated local submission as ready.
Mailbox ownership and any replaced value are released exactly once on install,
drop, replacement, disconnect, or cleanup.

Client main atomically installs a complete catalog or offers one event. There is no
decode-thread rendering, partial apply, pending replay, unbounded task enqueue, or
P7 mirror-state reuse.

### 61.10 Observable Encoded-Byte Accounting

P8 charges the exact deterministic uncompressed bytes emitted by the locked
`PacketEncoder` immediately before the optional compression stage. It encodes the
registered payload body into a bounded buffer and includes the locked
`CLIENTBOUND_CUSTOM_PAYLOAD` packet ID `25` (one VarInt byte) plus the serialized
payload identifier. The compression encoder, its conditional uncompressed-length
marker, compressed bytes, encryption, and the later outer frame-length VarInt are
excluded because their byte counts depend on connection configuration and encoded
content after this deterministic boundary. The body-only codec guard is separately
enforced. Send is attempted only if this checked `PacketEncoder` output charge fits.

For body size `B`:

```text
catalog ID UTF-8 bytes                         = 24
serialized catalog ID                         = 1 + 24 = 25
catalog charged bytes                          = B + 1 + 25 = B + 26
catalog maximum legal V0 body / charge          = 468683 / 468709
catalog hard body guard / corresponding charge  = 491520 / 491546

event ID UTF-8 bytes                           = 27
serialized event ID                           = 1 + 27 = 28
event charged bytes                            = B + 1 + 28 = B + 29
event maximum legal V0 body / charge            = 897 / 926
event hard body guard / corresponding charge    = 1024 / 1053
```

The registered-codec path has no inherited universal 1 MiB body guarantee; all
limits above are P8-owned. The hard-body rows are pre-decode guards, not reachable
legal V0 layouts. Two maximum legal catalogs cost 937,418 bytes and fit the 1 MiB
catalog-tick budget with 111,158 bytes remaining. Sixteen maximum legal events cost
14,816 bytes and fit a player’s 32 KiB tick budget. All 512 maximum legal event
deliveries cost 474,112 bytes and fit the 512 KiB global event budget with 50,176
bytes remaining; the independent count cap, not the byte cap, is tighter at that
maximum.

### 61.11 Sequence, Seed, Privacy, and Recipient Selection

The per-server `P8ServerPresentationService` owns one event sequence. After the
entire server offer is structurally and semantically valid, it allocates the next
positive `long` immediately before degradation, coalescing, buffer admission, or
recipient budgeting. Every such offer consumes its value even if later coalesced,
dropped, unaffordable, or unsent. It starts at one for each new real
`MinecraftServer` lifecycle epoch on the same root-owned service, never resets on
tick/reload/player/skill/world/resource
changes within that epoch, and never reuses gaps. `Long.MAX_VALUE` is allocated
once; afterward the service is exhausted and drops every otherwise-valid offer
until the next real server lifecycle start resets the same root-owned service into
a new epoch. It never wraps.

The exact visual seed is:

```text
z = 0x4752414D41525945L XOR sequence
z = (z XOR (z >>> 30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9L
z = (z XOR (z >>> 27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EBL
visualSeed = z XOR (z >>> 31)
```

Java signed-`long` overflow and unsigned right shift semantics are authoritative;
all 64-bit outputs including zero are legal. This is the Stafford Mix13 finalizer.
It uses no wall clock, gameplay RNG, client claim, or private secret. Recipients of
the same event get the same seed. A server restart can repeat it, and it promises
neither replay identity nor pixel equality across renderers/platforms.

On client main, a captured event must first match the current connection, world,
resource, and exact installed catalog generations. A mismatch drops it without
changing sequence high-water. A matching event is accepted only when
`sequence > lastAcceptedSequence` for that connection generation. The client then
updates high-water before Profile/factory lookup, pending capacity, local budget,
preferences, or renderer execution. Thus every structurally valid in-generation
event consumes its client order position even when presentation is locally dropped.
High-water resets only for a new connection generation; world/resource/catalog
changes never roll it back. There is no resend or replay for gaps.

Before any recipient enumeration, an online `PlayerList` size over 512 drops the
whole visual event. This prevents calling a watcher getter whose result could exceed
P8 ownership. Eligible candidates are current connected players having one of the
at-most-512 P8 readiness records; no chunk/entity/level is loaded.

For `CAST_RELEASE`, candidates are ready players in the event dimension within
distance squared 4096 of the event position; the source player is included only if
it passes those same rules. For `HIT`, candidates begin with the locked
`ChunkMap.getPlayersWatching(targetEntity)` result plus the target when it is a
player and the source player, then receive the same connected, ready, dimension,
and range filters. Controlled sources use these exact paths and cannot bypass them.

Candidates are deduplicated by UUID and ordered by category: target player `0`,
source player `1`, ordinary watcher/near player `2`; then ascending squared distance
from the event position; then unsigned UUID most-significant bits and unsigned UUID
least-significant bits. The first 32 survive. Events drain in ascending global
sequence, and individual sends for any recipient preserve that order. Recipient
filtering creates legal gaps. An opaque `PacketDistributor` fan-out is forbidden
because it cannot expose the count needed by P8 budgets.

### 61.12 Sole P8 Numeric-Bounds Authority

This is the one normative P8 limits table. A repeated number elsewhere in §61 is a
derivation or transition reference, not another owner. Count and byte limits are
conjunctive. All additions/multiplications use checked `long` arithmetic; arithmetic
overflow fails closed at the indicated check.

| Dimension | Exact hard bound and unit | Owner/check point | Excess or invalid result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Frozen common Profile types | 64 total, including 3 built-ins | startup type-registry bake | startup failure; no partial freeze |
| Frozen client factory bindings | 64 total, including 3 mandatory built-ins | client registry bake | startup failure; missing third-party binding is unavailable, not a late mutation |
| Adjustable parameters | 16/type; key 32 UTF-8 bytes | type bake | startup failure |
| Profile instances | 64/channel; 192 total, including one default/channel | server candidate construction | retain ascending legal IDs that fit; omit deterministic excess |
| Profile resource discovery | inspect/read first 256 sorted effective IDs/reload | after platform `listResources` returns | omit later IDs; one bounded diagnostic |
| Profile raw source | accepted/retained at most 16,384 bytes/entry and 4,194,304 bytes/reload; inspected at most 16,385 bytes/entry and 4,194,560 bytes/reload including one oversize sentinel/entry | bounded reader before parse | omit ordinary entry; unexpected loader failure aborts candidate |
| Profile JSON structure | depth 12 and 256 nodes/entry; 65,536 nodes/reload | strict parser | omit ordinary entry; retain no raw tree |
| Every Profile JSON string and Profile/type/factory/RL string | 128 UTF-8 bytes | startup, JSON, catalog, and event construction/decode | reject registration, omit entry, or structural wire failure according to layer |
