The 4 MiB accepted-byte, 4,194,560 inspected-byte, and 65,536-node reload values are
simple products of the per-entry and discovery limits. Java extension objects are
bounded by reference/count and their
canonical serialized input; P8 does not claim a byte-accurate heap sandbox for a
malicious third-party JVM mod. Likewise, platform resource enumeration before
`listResources` returns and work performed inside a third-party factory call are
outside P8-owned work, while the number of retained results and calls into those
boundaries remains hard-capped.

### 61.13 Deterministic Cost and Degradation

Every validated instance supplies one non-null estimated `ProfileCost` directly
checked against the sole per-instance bounds in §61.12; there is no separate
per-type maximum member. The server uses that immutable estimate for
logical preflight. The client sink, not the estimate, owns the actual particle,
sound, trail, lifetime, and handle charges. A sink returns `false` before the
platform call when a command cannot be charged. Presentation cost never debits
mana, P5 budget, P7 rate, cooldown, damage, or gameplay work.

The fixed degradation order is:

1. reduce actual particle count to remaining credits;
2. deterministically reduce spawn frequency and increase trail sampling interval;
3. remove secondary trail commands, preserving the first primary trail;
4. coalesce exact-identity same-tick server events;
5. deterministically drop deliveries/channels/presentations that still do not fit.

A stage that cannot reduce the budget currently being checked is skipped without
changing the order. Thus server wire-byte pressure proceeds to exact coalescing and
drop because client particle density does not shrink an already fixed event body.
Client preferences may perform additional reductions through the same stages and
may never increase work or affect gameplay.

Server coalescing is legal only when two offers are from the same
`sourceEventId` and applied-step index and have the same catalog generation, kind,
source/target summary, dimension, position, direction, effective Appearance, and
override map. It retains the earliest allocated sequence and seed; all later
allocated sequences remain consumed gaps. Distinct gameplay facts, positions,
recipients, or visual values never coalesce. There is no cross-tick coalescing.

After recipient selection, the drain builds at most 4,096 candidate deliveries. It
keeps target-self before source before ordinary recipient, nearer before farther,
unsigned UUID ascending, and earlier sequence before later sequence; dropping is
the exact reverse order. Actual sends are then grouped per recipient in ascending
sequence, preserving global order. Event send failure removes only that candidate.
Client eviction similarly preserves already-active higher-priority/nearer work and
drops the newest lower-priority channel owner first; expiry and trail truncation use
oldest-first removal. Every tie is resolved by sequence, channel code, then Profile
ID. No decision uses hash iteration order, clock time, timeout, GC, or random state.

### 61.14 Four Independent Generations

| Generation | Owner/type and advance | Reset/exhaustion | Wire/check/stale behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| Catalog | server service positive `long`; initial activation is `1`, each later globally successful activation adds one | reset only at the next real server lifecycle start on the same root-owned service; after `Long.MAX_VALUE`, retain old active and discard future candidates, never wrap | the only generation sent on P8 wire; client catalog/event must match exact active value; older/duplicate catalog and mismatched event drop |
| Connection | server has one positive non-wrapping login-epoch allocator and current UUID→epoch map; client has a process-lifetime positive non-wrapping counter advanced at connection open and logout | server allocator/map reset only at the next real server lifecycle start on the same root-owned service; client resets only at process restart; exhaustion makes later P8 connections unready/disabled without disconnect | local only; every retry/task captures exact epoch/generation; mismatch drops and releases; never resets event high-water within a connection |
| World | client connection-scoped positive `long`, advanced for each level load and unload | new connection starts a new world counter; exhaustion disables presentation until next connection | local only; pending/active world-bound visuals clear; mismatch drops; catalog/high-water remain connection truth |
| Resource | client process-local positive `long`, advanced only when the P8 resource listener’s complete index apply succeeds | process restart only; on exhaustion clear resource-bound visuals and fail closed until restart, never wrap | local only; P8-listener prepare/apply failure retains the last complete index/generation; exact captured event mismatch drops; no skill revision, catalog generation, sequence, or retry reset |

Catalog and server connection values are server-thread-owned. Client connection,
world, and resource values are client-main-owned; NETWORK only captures immutable
values and reserves counters. Catalog mailbox work captures only connection because
catalog truth is world/resource independent and resolves availability against the
current resource index on client main. Event work captures connection, world, and
resource and requires exact installed catalog generation. All transitions use exact
equality rather than ordering except that a client accepts a complete catalog only
when it has no catalog or the incoming positive catalog generation is greater than
the installed one.

### 61.15 Reload Activation, Readiness, and Retry

One `AddReloadListenerEvent` listener uses the standard prepare executor to read and
validate bounded Profile data and the standard apply executor only to stage an
immutable candidate. Its exact reload token is the reference identity returned by
that event’s `getServerResources()`. Java Profile types/factories do not reload.
Pending data is inaccessible to runtime lookup.

Initial successful data preparation activates at `ServerStartedEvent` before P5 is
allowed to enter `RUNNING`, producing catalog generation one, only when its token is
reference-identical to
`event.getServer().getServerResources().managers()`. A live candidate activates
only when the locked whole-reload success coordinate emits `OnDatapackSyncEvent`
with `getPlayer() == null` and its token is reference-identical to
`event.getPlayerList().getServer().getServerResources().managers()`. A
player-specific event never activates; it only schedules the already-active catalog
for that player. Because `OnDatapackSyncEvent` carries no reload token, there is no
tick/time-based pending cleanup. One inaccessible pending candidate remains bounded
until matching activation, replacement by a newer staged resource identity, or
server stop; replacement and stop release it exactly once. This closes ownership
without treating one listener’s apply or elapsed tick as whole-reload success.

Activation is atomic on the server logic thread:

1. validate that a pending candidate and active-generation capacity exist;
2. clear at most 128 old-generation current-tick events;
3. publish exactly one new immutable snapshot and increment catalog generation;
4. revoke every old readiness value;
5. create a deterministic ascending-UUID sync queue for at most 512 current
   connections; and
6. discard the old snapshot and pending ownership.

There is no partial publish or catalog history. A failed ordinary Profile entry was
already omitted while building a complete candidate. An unexpected/global reload
failure publishes nothing, keeps the old active catalog, leaves at most one pending
candidate inaccessible until replacement/stop, does not change readiness or skill
revision, and sends nothing.

Every server login allocates a new positive connection epoch and replaces any stale
record for that UUID. If catalog state is active and record capacity exists, its
retry key is exactly `(UUID, connectionEpoch, catalogGeneration)`. At each
`ServerTickEvent.Post`, P8 drains catalogs before events. Attempt one is made at the
next such catalog-first drain that has both per-player and global count/byte budget;
budget deferral is not an attempt. A normal synchronous local-submit return marks
that exact key ready and removes its queue record. This means only local ordering:
it is not delivery, decode, install, asset availability, or acknowledgement.

A catalog-send `RuntimeException` consumes the attempt and its count/byte charge,
keeps the recipient unready, and schedules the same bounded key for attempt two no
earlier than the following post tick. A second such failure is terminal for that key:
remove it and remain unready until a new connection epoch or catalog generation.
Disconnect, epoch/generation mismatch, or server stop cancels the key. Client
resource reload never renews attempts. No event is buffered for an unready player;
that delivery is dropped immediately with no replay.

On client main, a newer complete catalog rechecks only its captured connection
generation, evaluates availability against the current resource index, first clears
old pending events and active visuals, then installs atomically. Older or duplicate
catalog generations drop. The latest-generation mailbox rules in §61.9.3 prevent a
newer valid catalog from being lost merely because an older one is queued. Catalog
installation does not send an ACK. Every event requires exact installed catalog
generation as described in §61.11.

The P8 client resource listener publishes a replacement index only when its own
prepare and apply complete normally; failure inside that listener retains its old
index/generation. The locked platform exposes no global client-reload success hook,
so P8 neither claims nor simulates rollback if a later unrelated listener fails
after P8 apply. Any platform/user recovery reload is a new P8 listener cycle with a
new candidate. Catalog truth stays installed and its availability is recomputed
against whichever P8 resource generation is current.

### 61.16 Complete A–J Failure Matrix

| Class/layer | Gameplay and presentation result | Readiness/session/retry | Diagnostic, Throwable, and cleanup |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Persisted malformed Appearance; P3/P4 decode | Existing bounded `Unparsed`/`Rejected`/module fallback; gameplay definition remains usable; no new raw truth | P8 readiness/session unchanged; no P8 retry | existing bounded warning; P8 receives raw-free fallback only |
| B. Missing/unknown type or Profile instance; server resolve/client catalog | channel default, then disable only that channel; other channels and gameplay continue | readiness/session valid; no event replay/retry | bounded ID/code; discard temporary decode/config; no arbitrary lookup |
| C. Missing client asset/factory; client availability/present | one default factory/asset attempt, then drop that channel | catalog remains installed; session valid; no network retry | bounded code; release attempted handles; no URL/path/class load |
| D. Malformed, truncated, trailing, noncanonical, or oversize wire; NETWORK/handler | zero partial catalog/event mutation; safe structural rejection | terminate receiving connection with fixed translation reason; no P7 schema/delivery state added | decoder failure or explicit fixed disconnect; release reservation/buffer; retain no raw/exception |
| E. Budget/capacity exhaustion; server or client ledger | fixed degradation then deterministic event/channel/presentation drop; a newer valid catalog replaces an older catalog-mailbox value rather than dropping for slot capacity; gameplay unchanged | readiness stays as-is; no retry/replay | bounded saturation code/counter; each reservation owner releases exactly once |
| F. Stale generation or sequence; client main/server retry | deterministic discard; no fallback into a different generation | no high-water rollback; stale server key cancelled; no retry/replay | optional deduplicated fixed code; close stale visual/task handles |
| G. Local send failure; server drain | catalog failure leaves unready and uses at most one later retry; event failure drops only that recipient delivery | catalog policy is exactly §61.15; event preserves existing readiness/session and never disconnects | catch only per-send `RuntimeException`, fixed code, no object retention; release encoded buffer; `Error` cleanup then propagation |
| H. Expected factory failure; exact client extension call | typed `UNAVAILABLE` or contained `RuntimeException` consumes one attempt, tries default once, then channel drop; gameplay unchanged | catalog/session remain; no network retry | fixed code, close partial handles, no class/message/stack/Throwable retention; `Error` propagates after cleanup |
| I. Unexpected `RuntimeException`/`Error`; internal boundary | P8 observer `RuntimeException` alone becomes diagnostic/drop after gameplay truth is fixed; gameplay-origin exception remains P5/P6 truth; other internal failures are not misreported as normal degradation | transport failure cannot call back into P5 breaker; no retry unless G catalog case; session effects only where D requires | every owner performs bounded non-throwing cleanup; `Error` always propagates as the same object; no `Throwable` history |
| J. Failed server datapack reload or failed P8 client resource-listener cycle | server candidate does not activate and old catalog/gameplay continue; P8 client prepare/apply failure retains its old index; no partial P8 apply or skill revision | existing readiness remains; no sends/retry reset | server pending stays inaccessible until exact replacement/stop; client discards its failed candidate; no raw tree; no claim of observing failure in a later unrelated client listener |

This matrix does not claim that P8 can make a malformed connection, arbitrary
`Error`, or malicious loaded mod harmless. It precisely isolates expected visual
failure while preserving structural rejection and invariant visibility. P7
ACK/mana/cooldown failure and disconnect semantics remain exclusively P7-owned.

### 61.17 Exact Cross-Package and Composition Model

The root-package server owner is exactly:

```java
package com.yo1no.gramarye;

final class P8ServerPresentationService {
    static P8ServerPresentationService create();
    ProfileAvailabilityView profileAvailabilityView();
    void registerAfterP5(IEventBus gameBus);
    void handleServerStarted(ServerStartedEvent event);
    P8PresentationOfferOutcome offerApplied(
            RuntimeEvent event,
            RuntimeExecutionContext context,
            P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.AppliedFact fact);
}

enum P8PresentationOfferOutcome {
    ACCEPTED,
    DEGRADED,
    DROPPED
}
```

Both declarations are package-private; the service is final. The outcome is the
closed value for normal offer/budget behavior and is never thrown. `RuntimeEvent`
and `RuntimeExecutionContext` are the existing package-private top-level root types,
not nested bridge types. The service owns one stable availability-view identity and
may hold exactly one active `MinecraftServer` lifecycle identity while that server
is active. It has no public/protected member and no acquisition outside root
composition.

For this aggregate return, an eligible per-step offer is a copied applied step that
maps to an authorized §61.3 event kind and has all required §61.4 geometry. The
return is `ACCEPTED` exactly when at least one eligible offer exists and every such
offer is admitted unchanged as a distinct retained event. It is `DEGRADED` exactly
when at least one presentation from the call survives, but any eligible offer was
coalesced, deterministically degraded, or dropped. It is `DROPPED` exactly when no
presentation from the call survives, including zero eligible offers, invalid
geometry, or total budget/capacity rejection. This classification is computed only
after the atomic normal publication described in §61.4; the handoff does not use it
to affect gameplay.

The exact production constructor/factory changes are:

```java
// com.yo1no.gramarye.P5RuntimeProjector
P5RuntimeProjector(ProfileAvailabilityView profiles)

// com.yo1no.gramarye.P6RuntimeExecutionPortAdapter
P6RuntimeExecutionPortAdapter(
        P6RuntimeExecutionCapability capability,
        P8ServerPresentationService presentationService)

// com.yo1no.gramarye.SkillRuntimeService
static SkillRuntimeService create(
        IEventBus gameBus,
        SkillDefinitionStoreService storeService,
        SkillSubmissionPolicyProvider policyProvider,
        ProfileAvailabilityView profiles,
        P6RuntimeExecutionCapability capability,
        P8ServerPresentationService presentationService)

// com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.definition.submission.SkillDefinitionSubmissionService
public static SkillDefinitionSubmissionService production(
        PlayerSkillAttachmentService attachments,
        SkillDefinitionStoreSubmissionPort storePort,
        SkillSubmissionPolicyProvider policyProvider,
        ProfileAvailabilityView profiles)
```

The old three-argument public `production` descriptor and compatibility overloads
are zero. The zero-argument production `P5RuntimeProjector` and production adapter
path that reacquires a capability are removed; focused package-private test
constructors may remain. The package-private `P6ExecutionBridgeInvoker` test seam
receives `P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.AppliedFactObserver` as its exact final parameter.
All arguments are non-null before publication.

The adapter constructs exactly one call-scoped `P8AppliedFactHandoff` for the same
`RuntimeEvent` and `RuntimeExecutionContext` being executed and supplies it as the
new bridge observer argument. An unmapped/no-op P6 input invokes neither bridge nor
observer. A mapped invocation still calls the bridge at most once and returns the
existing `Completed + empty child plan`; observer presence never changes children
or gameplay transport.

The only public registration-only Java bridge needed to keep the established
subpackage registrar as sole event subscriber is:

```java
package com.yo1no.gramarye;

public final class P8PayloadRegistrationBridge {
    public static void register(PayloadRegistrar registrar);
}
```

It has a private constructor, zero public/protected fields, and exactly that one
public static operation. It exposes no payload/service/session value and can run
only during startup; null or duplicate invocation is a startup invariant failure.
`P7PayloadRegistrar.registerPayloads` obtains the exact P8-version NETWORK
`PayloadRegistrar` and invokes this bridge once after registering its unchanged P7
family. The bridge owns only root-package package-private P8 payload codecs/handlers;
it is not an event subscriber, second registrar, sender, or runtime locator.

The common/root handler forwards through one write-once package-private client
dispatch port whose initial state is disconnected/fail-closed. The existing public
`com.yo1no.gramarye.GramaryeClient` has the exact constructor
`public GramaryeClient(IEventBus modBus)`. That constructor alone creates the one
client Profile-factory registry, one immutable resource-index owner, and one P8
client execution/lifecycle owner, then installs the exact owner into the forwarding
port once. There is no replacement/uninstall/runtime setter or public client-owner
getter. Common payload code contains no `net.minecraft.client` reference; the
client implementation is reached only after the client mod entrypoint loads.

### 61.18 Exact Bootstrap, Thread, and Lifecycle Order

`Gramarye` performs this production order:

1. register the existing registries plus the Profile type registry on the mod bus;
2. create exactly one `P8ServerPresentationService` and obtain its exact stable
   `ProfileAvailabilityView` once;
3. obtain `P6RuntimeExecutionCapability.forRuntimeAdapter()` exactly once;
4. derive the existing P7 `LoginReadyPort` from that same capability and compose
   the unchanged P4-E2 login path;
5. pass the same availability-view object to the four-argument submission factory;
6. create `SkillRuntimeService` with that view, the same capability, and the same
   P8 service; this constructs `P5RuntimeProjector(view)` and the P6 adapter and
   registers P5’s LOWEST post-tick/stopping/stopped handlers;
7. invoke `p8Service.registerAfterP5(NeoForge.EVENT_BUS)`, which registers the P8
   LOWEST post-tick and reload/connection/stop handlers after P5;
8. create/install the unchanged P7 authenticated ingress with the same capability;
   and
9. register one root `ServerStartedEvent` handler.

At server start, the root handler calls `p8Service.handleServerStarted(event)` first
and only then snapshots P5 limits and calls
`skillRuntimeService.handleRuntimeStarted(...)`. P8 therefore has an active initial
catalog before P5 enters `RUNNING`. At `ServerTickEvent.Post`, P5 drains/executes
first and P8 drains the resulting current-tick presentation offers second. At stop,
P5 stops before P8 clears. The P8 service registers after P5 specifically to preserve
this same-priority ordering.

All P5/P6 offer work, P8 event construction, budget selection, recipient enumeration,
catalog activation, readiness, and send submission run on the exact server logic
thread. Profile reload prepare parsing runs only on the platform prepare executor;
its apply stage transfers one immutable candidate to server lifecycle handling. P8
creates no thread, executor, timer, future owner, blocking wait, or recursive event
loop.

NETWORK performs only bounded decode, immutable capture, and reservation. Each
event payload calls `enqueueWork` exactly once. Catalog payloads use §61.9.3’s
latest-generation mailbox and schedule a main drain only on empty-to-occupied, with
at most one outstanding drain per connection generation. Catalog/resource
publication and presentation execution occur on client main. Normal particle/sound
paths and bounded trail sampling run only on
their required client thread/render coordinates. Factories receive no raw client,
level, entity, session, or service handle.

The process-scoped frozen common/client registries survive server/world changes.
The server service resets sequence, catalog, diagnostics, retry/readiness, pending
candidate, and tick budgets for a newly started server and clears all of them plus
its sole server identity at stop. Client logout clears catalog, event high-water,
pending tasks/events, readiness-derived state, and active visuals; world unload
clears world-bound tasks/visuals; resource activation closes old resource handles
before the new index becomes visible. Entity untracking/despawn causes any tracked
trail owner to close without retaining the entity.

Legal long-lived state is limited to frozen registry descriptors, one active catalog
and bounded typed configuration, service ports/counters, at-most-512 readiness
records, a current-tick event buffer, one client catalog, one active resource index,
and the bounded active client presentations in §61.12. It is illegal to retain raw
P5/P6 context, Player/Entity/Level (except the exact active-server lifecycle identity
already stated), definition/node/action objects, lease/pin, receipt/result/trace,
raw Profile input, or `Throwable` history.

### 61.23 Known Limits and Non-Claims

P8-A1 supplies design authority, not product bytes. Current production still has no
P8 catalog, event, emitter, payload, client renderer, resource, controlled harness,
or real damage binding. A local payload submission proves only ordering at that
connection API; P8 has no delivery ACK. The deterministic seed is not a replay or
pixel-equality guarantee. The client resource listener proves only its own atomic
prepare/apply; the locked platform has no later all-listener client-reload success
callback for P8 to observe. The registered-codec path has no general platform 1 MiB
guarantee beyond P8’s own checks. P8 bounds its work after resource enumeration and
its calls into cooperative extensions, not arbitrary allocation/code inside the
platform or a malicious loaded JVM mod. P9 alone will prove actual projectile, hit,
exactly-once damage, and particles-off-still-damage.

These limits are accepted, finite boundaries rather than open product choices.
There is no remaining D01–D10 alternative, `TBD`, or implementation-time product
decision in this active section.

source freeze, commit, or push because two authority gaps were found:

   capability tuples and `ProfileCost` formulae over their full legal configuration
   domains.

is useful development evidence only; it is not a product qualification, source
freeze, or earlier authority for its provisional choices.

  public bridge;
- one aggregate resolution captures exactly one immutable active catalog snapshot
  and uses one view bound to that snapshot;
- the complete capability tuples, stored estimates, and declared-work ceilings for

different package route, snapshot model, tuple, formula, or accounting stage.

| `PresentationSequence.java` | `PresentationSequence` | Root global event sequence and pure visual-seed allocation. |

Thus twelve current physical units containing twenty-six package-private top-level
declarations move. Every listed declaration remains package-private. Existing
constructors, fields, operations, nested types, record components, enum vocabulary,
and semantic outcomes retain their current visibility and behavior except for the
package declaration, necessary imports, and exact internal linkage required here.
No second copy remains at `OLD_MAIN`.

This complete physical move preserves Java rules that a partial move would break:

- unnamed-module sealed `PresentationEventCreation` and its two direct permitted
  records remain in one package as Java requires; the current source unit moves
  intact for continuity, without freezing later private file grouping;
- `PresentationCost.Arithmetic` and its nested permitted results move with their
  outer owner;
- the public runtime-neutral sealed hierarchies are only consumed, not extended,
  so their permits lists do not change;
- static imports and nested-role references are updated to the new root FQCNs;
- `PresentationLimits` remains the sole internal limits owner and
  `AppearanceSemantics` remains the sole merge/default/fallback owner.

Co-location grants Java access only. The S1 purity boundary continues to forbid
dependencies on `RuntimeEvent`, `RuntimeExecutionContext`, `MinecraftServer`, the
P8 service itself, network/client/I/O/concurrency owners, persistent state, or live
gameplay objects. No `Object`, reflection, unchecked cast, duplicate algorithm,
public constant getter, or service locator may substitute for this move.

Any later package-private client execution owner that directly consumes the moved
budget, degradation, or ordering semantics is likewise root-co-located or privately
nested in a root-package owner and is reached through root `GramaryeClient`
composition. This does not move the fixed common or client public APIs and does not
authorize a bridge into `com.yo1no.gramarye.client.presentation.api`.

### 62.5 Exact Snapshot-capture Member and View

`P8ServerPresentationService` remains package-private and remains the sole root
catalog/reload/publication owner. Section 61.17's product-facing service declaration
is extended by exactly this additional package-private call-scoped operation:

```java
Optional<AppearanceResolutionSnapshot> captureAppearanceResolutionSnapshot();
```

Necessary private implementation methods and narrowly focused package-private test
seams remain allowed within §§61–62 and add no public product surface; the word
"exactly" above applies to the new resolution-capture contract, not to a frozen
inventory of private method bodies.

`AppearanceResolutionSnapshot` is a package-private `static final` nested class of
`P8ServerPresentationService`. It has a private constructor accepting the exact
immutable internal `CatalogSnapshot` and exactly these package-private observation
operations:

```java
long catalogGeneration();
PresentationProfileView profiles();
```

It declares no public or protected constructor, operation, or field. It does not
implement `PresentationProfileView`; it owns one stable snapshot-bound lambda/view,
avoiding a new mandatory public interface override. Its constructor cannot accept a
generation separately from contents.

`captureAppearanceResolutionSnapshot()` performs exactly one volatile read:

```text
captured = activeSnapshot
captured == null → Optional.empty()
captured != null → new AppearanceResolutionSnapshot(captured)
```

The wrapper's generation and view both derive from that same `CatalogSnapshot`
object. `profiles()` never reads the service, `activeSnapshot`, generation
high-water, pending candidate, registry, or resource manager. It projects an entry
only as the existing immutable root-co-located descriptor:

```java
PresentationProfileDescriptor(
    ResourceLocation id,
    ProfileChannel channel,
    ProfileTypeCapabilities capabilities,
    ProfileCost estimatedCost)
```

The exact package-private `PresentationProfileView` contract remains:

```java
Optional<PresentationProfileDescriptor> find(ResourceLocation id);
```

Typed configuration, `ProfileType`, catalog-entry identity, canonical resource
representation, service identity, and a per-lookup provider do not cross this seam.

### 62.6 Capture Timing, Generation Pairing, and State Semantics

`P8ServerPresentationService.offerApplied(...)` is the sole production caller. It
calls `captureAppearanceResolutionSnapshot()` exactly once per aggregate
`offerApplied` invocation, after required null, server-thread, and lifecycle checks
and before iterating or merging any eligible applied step and before any profile
selection, default lookup, capability check, estimate lookup, sequence allocation,
or event construction. The caller passes only `captured.profiles()` to the moved
`AppearanceSemantics`; every eligible step, channel, selected/default/fallback
lookup, capability check, and estimated-cost lookup in that aggregate invocation
uses the same view. Every event created by that invocation obtains its catalog
generation only from `captured.catalogGeneration()` and never reads
`catalogGenerationHighWater` separately.

The state matrix is exact:

| Service state at capture | Resolution behavior |
|---|---|
| No active snapshot, including pending-only or stopped | Capture is empty; the aggregate `offerApplied` result is `DROPPED` before lookup and before sequence/event allocation. Before initial activation, the distinct live validation adapter remains `UNKNOWN` exactly as §61 specifies. |
| Active A, no pending | The complete call uses A. |
| Active A plus non-queryable pending B | The complete call uses A; pending B is unreachable. |
| Failed reload while A is active | A remains active and the complete call uses A. |
| Successful B publication before capture | The call may capture and wholly use B. |
| Successful B publication after A was captured | The current call finishes wholly on A; the next call may capture B. |

The stable public `ProfileAvailabilityView` is a separate live validation adapter.
It may observe later active snapshots across independent validation calls and is
never passed to `AppearanceSemantics` as a resolution view.

An in-flight reference to immutable A is a short call-local reference, not another
authoritative active snapshot or retained history. It requires no deep copy,
lease/refcount, long-lived read lock, or reload lock. The service retains its sole
authoritative `activeSnapshot` field, and `AppearanceResolutionSnapshot` necessarily
retains private final call-scoped `snapshot` and `profiles` fields. No additional
owner may store the captured wrapper, bound view, or captured snapshot reference in
a field or place it into a `SkillDocument`, validated gameplay core, player
Attachment, persistent store, applied-fact handoff, current-tick buffered event,
diagnostic/history record, async task, or cross-tick operation; none may survive the
immediate aggregate resolution call. The service and live provider do not escape
through the wrapper.

Descriptor, capability, and cost objects are call-local scratch only. Only the
existing bounded immutable effective Profile IDs, scalars, parameter map, resolution
reasons where already authorized, and numeric catalog generation may survive into
already-authorized outputs. No descriptor, typed configuration, type object, view,
catalog, provider, reload token/resource-manager identity, catalog-entry object
identity, or mutable callback survives the call.

### 62.7 Direct A/B Snapshot Acceptance

The future direct product test is finite and controlled:

1. construct immutable controlled-test snapshots A and B with the same
   selected/default ID set but distinguishable generations, selected descriptors,
   and fallback descriptors; this package-private binding model may use synthetic
   fallback facts solely to make lookup origin observable, while separate catalog
   tests prove that a production snapshot always contains the exact fixed built-in
   defaults;
2. capture A exactly once at resolution entry;
3. publish B at a controlled boundary before or between semantic lookups;
4. prove selected sound, particle, trail, missing/wrong-channel default fallback,
   parameter capability, estimated cost, and emitted generation all come from A;
5. begin the next resolution and prove all of those facts come from B;
6. prove the captured view performs zero provider/active-pointer reads and the
   returned semantic/event values retain no wrapper, view, catalog, service,
   configuration, or type object.

This does not require an illegal cross-thread server reload, worker, stress loop,
GC observation, or timeout. It tests one capture and controlled publication at the
contract boundary.

### 62.8 Common Built-in Capability and Cost Rules

For every built-in, configuration version is exactly V0, the object codec rejects
unknown members, every asset `ResourceLocation` is at most 128 UTF-8 bytes, and
asset existence remains client availability rather than server validity. The actual
capability tuple is ordered as:

```text
(supportsPrimaryColor,
 supportsSecondaryColor,
 supportsDirection,
 supportsTrail,
 adjustableParameters)
```

`false` means that Appearance input cannot alter that built-in's channel output.
`true` permits bounded deterministic use of that input but authorizes no additional
channel, factory invocation, command/start, segment, or lifetime. The separate
global intensity input may only attenuate or suppress future built-in work; it may
never increase work above configuration and estimate bounds. All three built-ins
use `AppearanceParameterPolicy.none()`, whose integer-range map is exactly empty.
Their configuration members are not event-adjustable parameters. Each built-in
declares and consumes no integer event parameter and therefore contributes no
applicable range; a parameter may still be admitted through another co-selected
third-party Profile type's declared range under §61.8.

The tables in §§62.9–62.11 are each built-in's complete accepted configuration
domain. `validate(C, nonNullContext)` adds no policy-dependent narrowing and returns
valid for every table-legal configuration. Malformed, unknown-member, or
out-of-domain codec input is an ordinary entry omission; null configuration/context
or an impossible built-in invariant is an internal programming/startup failure
under the existing vocabulary.

The actual public estimate tuple is ordered as:

```text
ProfileCost(
    particleStarts,
    soundStarts,
    trailStarts,
    trailSegments,
    lifetimeTicks)
```

| Component | Exact declared unit |
|---|---|
| `particleStarts` | Maximum particle starts requested by the instance's one factory call. |
| `soundStarts` | Maximum sound starts requested by that call. |
| `trailStarts` | Maximum trail owners started by that call. |
| `trailSegments` | Maximum simultaneously retained segment capacity of that trail work. |
| `lifetimeTicks` | Maximum bounded tick lifetime associated with the instance estimate; never an implicit multiplier. |

The components are independent resource dimensions. They are never folded into a
weighted score and starts/segments are not implicitly multiplied by lifetime. The
formula input is exactly the immutable typed configuration after strict decode and
successful validation and before catalog insertion. The resulting estimate is
stored with that entry. One entry's estimate is never mutated or re-estimated for an
event override, preference, degradation, or coalescing operation; fallback selects
the already-stored default entry and its own estimate.

The server uses the stored estimate for logical preflight. The client output sink
charges actual retained/degraded particle starts and live credits, sound starts and
handles, and trail owners/retained segments immediately before each applicable
platform call or retention. Trail sampling opportunities are bounded by `Q`; there
is no separate sample ledger. A materialized sampler particle charges the existing
particle-start and live-credit ledgers. Factory-call, event-count/bytes, and
delivery-count/bytes ledgers remain separate §61 ledgers and are not hidden in
`ProfileCost`. An estimate is a conservative declared-work bound, not a measured
GPU or audio-engine cost.

Every built-in formula is integer-only projection of validated bounded values plus
constants. It has no floating-point rounding. Invalid/null input is rejected by the
existing codec/constructor/programming-invariant vocabulary before cost storage.
All later aggregation uses checked `long` addition/multiplication; overflow fails
closed without adopting partial state. No wrap, implicit truncation, NaN, or
infinity is a legal accounting outcome.

### 62.9 Sound Built-in

The exact identity is type/factory `gramarye:sound`, default instance
`gramarye:default_sound`, and channel `SOUND`. Its complete legal configuration is:

| Member | Domain and unit |
|---|---|
| `sound` | Valid `ResourceLocation`, at most 128 UTF-8 bytes. |
| `volume_milli` | Integer `[0,1000]`, converted only at the client to volume `[0,1]`. |
| `pitch_milli` | Integer `[500,2000]`, converted only at the client to pitch `[0.5,2]`. |

Its complete capability tuple is:

```text
(false, false, false, false, AppearanceParameterPolicy.none())
```

Primary/secondary colors, direction, trail semantics, and integer event parameters
cannot alter sound output. The exact stored estimate for every legal sound
configuration `S` is the NEW PRODUCT DECISION:

```text
C_sound(S) = ProfileCost(0, 1, 0, 0, 1)
```

Sound asset, volume, and pitch do not change this conservative one-start
reservation. `volume_milli = 0` is legal but is not declared a cost-free Profile;
a renderer may suppress the actual platform call, while the catalog estimate stays
one. The lifetime component `1` is the mandatory minimum accounting value, not a
claim that the platform clip lasts one tick. Active-sound truth remains the sink's
§61 thirty-two-handle cap. One factory call may accept at most one sound start and
may issue no particle or trail command.

### 62.10 Particle Built-in

The exact identity is type/factory `gramarye:particle`, default instance
`gramarye:default_particle`, and channel `PARTICLE`. Its complete legal
configuration is:

| Member | Domain and unit |
|---|---|
| `particle` | Valid `ResourceLocation`, at most 128 UTF-8 bytes. |
| `count` | Integer `[0,256]`, maximum starts declared by one factory call. |
| `speed_milli_blocks` | Integer `[0,16000]`, milli-blocks per tick before bounded client conversion. |
| `size_milli_blocks` | Integer `[1,16000]`, milli-blocks before bounded client conversion. |
| `lifetime_ticks` | Integer `[1,120]`, ticks. |

Its complete capability tuple is:

```text
(true, false, true, false, AppearanceParameterPolicy.none())
```

The factory may use primary color and direction in its bounded particle output. It
must ignore secondary color and may not create a trail or consume event parameters.
The exact stored estimate for legal particle configuration `P` is the NEW PRODUCT
DECISION:

```text
C_particle(P) = ProfileCost(P.count, 0, 0, 0, P.lifetime_ticks)
```

Speed and size do not change the number of starts. `count = 0` is the sole
configuration-level built-in no-start. One factory call may accept no more than
`count` particle starts, and each accepted particle may live no longer than
`lifetime_ticks`. Each successfully started live particle holds one actual live
credit for its bounded actual lifetime; `count × lifetime` is not invented as a
single `ProfileCost` component.

### 62.11 Trail Built-in

The exact identity is type/factory `gramarye:trail`, default instance
`gramarye:default_trail`, and channel `TRAIL`. Its complete legal configuration is:

| Member | Domain and unit |
|---|---|
| `particle` | Valid `ResourceLocation`, at most 128 UTF-8 bytes. |
| `segments` | Integer `[1,48]`, maximum simultaneously retained segment credits. |
| `sample_interval_ticks` | Integer `[1,120]`, ticks between sample opportunities. |
| `size_milli_blocks` | Integer `[1,16000]`, milli-blocks before bounded client conversion. |
| `lifetime_ticks` | Integer `[1,120]`, ticks. |

Its complete capability tuple is:

```text
(true, true, true, true, AppearanceParameterPolicy.none())
```

One bounded trail owner may use primary and secondary colors and direction. The
secondary color is part of that same owner; it never authorizes a second trail
start. `supportsTrail = true` permits the one bounded sampling/history behavior.
This built-in declares and consumes no integer event parameter. The exact stored
estimate for legal trail configuration `T` is the NEW PRODUCT DECISION:

```text
C_trail(T) = ProfileCost(0, 0, 1, T.segments, T.lifetime_ticks)
```

Size and sampling interval do not change the conservative retained-capacity
estimate. One factory call may create at most one trail owner, retain at most
`segments` segment credits simultaneously, and keep it no longer than
`lifetime_ticks`. For effective lifetime `L` and effective interval `I`, with an
initial sample at age zero and later samples every `I` ticks while age `< L`, the
exact opportunity bound and rounding are:

```text
Q(L, I) = 1 + floor((L - 1) / I) = ceil(L / I)
```

The implementation uses `1 + (L - 1) / I`, not the overflow-prone
`(L + I - 1) / I`. Across the legal domain `Q` is `[1,120]`. Simultaneously retained
segments are bounded by `min(T.segments, samplesProducedSoFar)`; after capacity,
oldest-first truncation preserves the configured cap. A trail sampler platform
particle attempt also meets the actual particle-start and live-credit ledgers,
while materialized retained history meets the trail-segment ledger. `Q` bounds
opportunities but creates no new accounting dimension; these are distinct resources,
not duplicate byte charges.

### 62.12 Degradation, Fallback, Coalescing, and Actual Charge

The §61 degradation order remains exactly particle reduction, frequency/sample
reduction, secondary-trail removal, exact-identity coalescing, then deterministic
drop. No stage recomputes or mutates stored `ProfileCost`; the following effective
parameters govern actual charges:

| Stage | Sound | Particle | Trail |
|---|---|---|---|
| Particle reduction | Inapplicable; skip. | `effectiveCount = min(configuredCount, remaining ACTUAL_PARTICLE_STARTS per-tick credits, remaining LIVE_PARTICLE_CREDITS slots)`; actual starts decrease, stored count does not. Every admitted command charges one of each applicable credit. | Stored trail estimate does not change; each materialized sampler particle independently meets both applicable actual particle ledgers. |
| Frequency/sample reduction | No mutable built-in sound frequency; skip. | Deterministic suppression makes current `effectiveCount = 0`; no actual start/live charge. | `effectiveInterval = max(configured interval, imposed minimum interval)`, bounded at 120; `Q(L,effectiveInterval)` decreases or stays equal. Start/lifetime/capacity estimate remains fixed. |
| Secondary trail removal | Inapplicable. | Inapplicable. | Inapplicable to the V0 built-in: `secondaryArgb` is an attribute of its sole retained primary owner, not a second command/owner. Section 61's general stage remains unchanged for a separately classified non-built-in/output presentation when applicable; it does not strip the built-in attribute or manufacture another start. |
| Exact coalescing | Execute the retained exact-identity event once. | Same. | Same; generations must match. |
| Disable/drop | Zero actual channel work; no invalid lifetime-zero cost is created. | Zero actual channel work. | Zero actual channel work and retained credits are not acquired. |

The server's missing/wrong-channel selection resolves to the built-in default and
its descriptor/estimate from the same captured snapshot. The exact default stored
estimates are:

```text
default sound    = ProfileCost(0, 1, 0, 0, 1)
default particle = ProfileCost(8, 0, 0, 0, 20)
default trail    = ProfileCost(0, 0, 1, 8, 16)
```

Client selected-instance failure permits the existing single default fallback. The
failed factory invocation consumes its factory-call attempt; already accepted
commands stay charged; default output incurs its own actual sink charges; already
received event/delivery bytes are not charged again. If the default is unavailable,
only that channel drops. Fallback is never free.

Exact same-tick coalescing retains and executes one event, not the sum of its
estimates; later sequence values remain consumed gaps. Events of different catalog
generations cannot coalesce. Work that actually executes is charged once, while one
event or delivery body is never double-charged because a channel falls back.

### 62.13 Direct Arithmetic and Domain Examples

Tuple notation below is
`(particleStarts,soundStarts,trailStarts,trailSegments,lifetimeTicks)`.

| Case | Capability/domain result | Stored `ProfileCost` | Actual/degraded result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default sound: asset fixed by §61, volume 600, pitch 1000 | Legal; all four booleans false, empty adjustable map | `(0,1,0,0,1)` | At most one actual sound start. |
| Sound minimum: volume 0, pitch 500 | Legal; zero volume is not an authority-level free Profile | `(0,1,0,0,1)` | A suppressed platform call charges zero actual start; otherwise at most one. |
| Sound maximum: volume 1000, pitch 2000 | Legal | `(0,1,0,0,1)` | Still at most one start. |
| Sound volume 1001 or unknown object member | Invalid codec domain | No catalog entry/cost | Existing omission/failure vocabulary. |
| Missing sound selection | Default lookup from the captured generation | `(0,1,0,0,1)` | Default actual work is charged. |
| Default particle: count 8, speed 50, size 250, lifetime 20 | Legal; primary/direction only | `(8,0,0,0,20)` | At most eight starts/live credits. |
| Particle minimum: count 0, speed 0, size 1, lifetime 1 | Legal configuration no-start | `(0,0,0,0,1)` | Zero actual particle start. |
| Particle maximum: count 256, speed 16000, size 16000, lifetime 120 | Legal even when a current budget cannot fit it | `(256,0,0,0,120)` | Degrade to remaining credits or drop; do not reject decode merely for transient budget. |
| Particle count 23/lifetime 67 with seven credits | Legal | `(23,0,0,0,67)` | Actual starts at most seven; frequency suppression reduces them to zero without changing stored cost. |
| Particle count 257, size 0, or lifetime 121 | Invalid codec/constructor domain | No catalog entry/cost | Rejected before estimate storage. |
| Missing particle selection | Default lookup from the captured generation | `(8,0,0,0,20)` | Default actual starts/live credits are charged; fallback is not free. |
| Default trail: segments 8, interval 2, size 200, lifetime 16 | Legal; all four booleans true, empty adjustable map | `(0,0,1,8,16)` | `Q = 1 + floor(15/2) = 8`; retained at most eight. |
| Trail minimum: segments 1, interval 1, size 1, lifetime 1 | Legal | `(0,0,1,1,1)` | `Q = 1`; one owner and at most one segment. |
| Trail scalar maxima: segments 48, interval 120, size 16000, lifetime 120 | Legal | `(0,0,1,48,120)` | `Q = 1`; stored capacity remains conservatively 48. |
| Trail maximum frequency: segments 48, interval 1, lifetime 120 | Legal | `(0,0,1,48,120)` | `Q = 120`, retained at most 48 with oldest-first truncation. |
| Default trail interval degraded 2 → 4 | Legal monotone reduction | Stored `(0,0,1,8,16)` unchanged | `Q` decreases from 8 to 4. |
| Trail segments 0/49 or interval 0/121 | Invalid codec/constructor domain | No catalog entry/cost | Rejected before estimate storage. |
| Missing trail selection | Default lookup from the captured generation | `(0,0,1,8,16)` | `Q = 8`; default owner/sample/segment work is actually charged. |
| Valid Appearance color/intensity override plus valid event-direction change | Legal only through each tuple: sound ignores colors/direction, particle may use primary/direction, trail may use both colors/direction; intensity is monotone-reducing only | Each selected entry's stored tuple is unchanged | Output facts may change, but actual work never increases beyond stored/configured bounds. |
| Event parameter such as built-in `count` or `segments`, when all selected Profiles are these built-ins | Rejected atomically with `IGNORED_PARAMETER_WITHOUT_PROFILE_CAPABILITY` because all three adjustable maps are empty | Existing base selection and stored estimates remain | It is not reinterpreted as a configuration override; a co-selected third-party declaration remains governed by §61.8. |
| Explicitly disabled or finally dropped channel | Legal Appearance outcome, no selected factory work | No estimate is evaluated for execution | Zero actual channel work; no lifetime-zero `ProfileCost`. |

Aggregate boundary checks remain mechanical and independent:

```text
16 × 256 concurrent retained live credits = 4096
    (exact live-credit occupancy cap across bounded lifetimes/multiple ticks;
     each individual tick is independently capped at 512 successful starts)
17 × 256 = 4352
    (over the live-credit occupancy cap; must degrade/reject actual work)
32 × 48 retained trail segments = 1536 (exact retained-segment cap)
33 × 48 = 1584                          (must reduce/remove/drop)
8 accepted sound starts = tick cap; a ninth is skipped/dropped
```

Those products use checked `long` multiplication. A direct ledger probe from
`Long.MAX_VALUE` plus one must report arithmetic overflow and leave the preceding
ledger state unchanged; it is not a legal built-in configuration. Every legal
built-in formula itself fits the public `ProfileCost` constructor bounds without
rounding or overflow.

### 62.14 Provisional Candidate Classification

The preserved S2 candidate did not own product authority. This amendment classifies
its three observed provisional definitions as follows:

| Candidate choice | Final classification and reason |
|---|---|
| Sound `(false,false,false,false,none)` and `(0,1,0,0,1)` | **ADOPTED WITH NEW AUTHORITY.** It exposes only guaranteed sound behavior and conservatively bounds one start for every legal configuration. |
