### 63.3 Canonical playable skill and fixed identities

The one P9 vertical slice is named `starter_bolt_v0`. Its four canonical registry
IDs are exact:

- TriggerType `gramarye:active_cast`;
- ActionType `gramarye:spawn_projectile`;
- TriggerType `gramarye:effect_hit`;
- ActionType `gramarye:damage`.

The canonical formal graph has exactly two nodes, in display order and runtime index
order:

1. display node 1 / runtime node index 0: `active_cast` -> `spawn_projectile`;
2. display node 2 / runtime node index 1: `effect_hit`, whose source is runtime node
   index 0, output ordinal 0, with `includeDerived=true`, -> `damage`.

Node 0 declares exactly one output, ordinal 0, of output kind `PROJECTILE`. Node 1
declares no output. Both edges and payloads are part of the immutable revision. No
implementation may special-case a slot, entity, action ID, or node index in place of
registry decode, document validation, projection, trigger matching, and action
dispatch.

The canonical `SkillDocument` schema version is 0. Its exact serialized V0 payload
maps and meanings are:

- `active_cast`: `{}` with no payload fields;
- `spawn_projectile`: `{"profile_code": 0, "mana_cost": 0}`;
- `effect_hit`: `{"source_node_index": 0, "source_output_ordinal": 0,
  "include_derived": true}` and no client-selected target;
- `damage`: `{"magnitude": 4000, "mana_cost": 0}`.

The corresponding package-private Java payload after-set is exactly the empty
singleton enum
`P9ActiveCastTriggerPayloadV0 implements TriggerPayload { INSTANCE }`,
`record P9SpawnProjectileActionPayloadV0(int profileCode, long manaCost)
implements ActionPayload {}`,
`record P9EffectHitTriggerPayloadV0(int sourceNodeIndex, int sourceOutputOrdinal,
boolean includeDerived) implements TriggerPayload {}`, and
`record P9DamageActionPayloadV0(long magnitude, long manaCost)
implements ActionPayload {}`. The codecs map only
the snake-case fields above; there is no alias, defaulted omitted field, generic map,
or public payload type.

Profile code 0 is the sole P9 code and means `starter_bolt_v0`; every other code is
invalid and rejected before request resolution. Unknown descriptor payloads continue
to obey the existing opaque round-trip rule, but an unknown payload can never execute
as this canonical slice.

Descriptor capabilities and inspector projections are exact:

| Descriptor | `TriggerCapabilities` / `ActionCapabilities` | Inspector projection |
|---|---|---|
| `active_cast` | source `NONE`, target `NONE`, continuation false, exact event kind `gramarye:active_cast`, source scopes `{CURRENT_INSTANCE}`, granularities `{PER_EVENT}` | source `NONE`, target `NONE`, provides-current-target false, references empty. |
| `spawn_projectile` | source `NONE`, target `NONE`, self false, outputs `{PROJECTILE}`, split/chain/repeat false, modifies-blocks/transfers-mana/persistent-state/requires-live-entity false, control `NONE`, appearance parameters `none()` | source `NONE`, target `NONE`, references empty, produced outputs `{PROJECTILE}`. |
| `effect_hit` | source `PRIOR_NODE`, target `REQUIRED`, continuation true, exact event kind `gramarye:effect_hit`, source scopes `{SOURCE_FAMILY}`, granularities `{PER_SOURCE}` | source `PRIOR_NODE`, target `CURRENT_TARGET`, provides-current-target true; one `SOURCE` reference at payload path `source_node_index` to node 0 requiring `PROJECTILE`. Output ordinal 0 and include-derived true remain in the typed resolved payload and its package-private P9 runtime matcher projection; the existing public `ValidatedTriggerReferenceProjection` shape is unchanged. |
| `damage` | source `NONE`, target `REQUIRED`, self false, outputs empty, split/chain/repeat false, modifies-blocks/transfers-mana/persistent-state false, requires-live-entity true, control `NONE`, appearance parameters `none()` | source `NONE`, target `CURRENT_TARGET`, references empty, produced outputs empty. |

All schema-0 descriptors use the empty adjacent migration plan. Validation requires
the exact closed values above and returns ordinary validation issues for invalid
player data. It never throws to represent an ordinary payload error.

### 63.4 Per-player document, revision, and semantic fingerprint

Each player receives a separately owned formal `SkillDocument`: a stable nonzero
command-derived `SkillId`, owner equal to that player's identity, exactly the graph and typed
payloads in §63.3, and a normal immutable revision produced through the existing
Draft -> validation -> submission -> Store pipeline. P9 introduces no global shared
skill reference, side database, mutable definition, or privileged Store write path.

`P9StarterSkillIdentityV0` is the exact pure Java projection
`new SkillId(UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes(("gramarye:starter_bolt_v0" + "\0" +
playerUuid.toString()).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)))`, where `toString()` is the
canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID form. The hashed byte sequence is the ASCII
starter prefix, exactly one `0x00` byte, and that lowercase UUID text; it contains
neither the two bytes backslash-plus-zero nor a platform-default encoding. Java's
name-UUID version bits
make the result nonzero; the same player always obtains the same route and distinct
players are additionally protected by normal Attachment owner checks. The derived
ID is not a credential or a global shared reference. A pre-existing draft/latest
route or Store identity at that ID is inspected exactly and never overwritten on a
semantic/owner collision.

Every newly created canonical document uses `AppearanceDocument.Default.INSTANCE`
at top level and `AppearanceOverrideDocument.None.INSTANCE` on both nodes. These are
the exact canonical defaults; the implementation does not choose a profile or
override at provisioning time.

The exact semantic recovery key is `StarterGameplayFingerprintV0`. It is the ordered
tuple of the two runtime node indices, their four exact type IDs, every canonical V0
payload field and value, node 0's `PROJECTILE` output ordinal 0, and node 1's exact
source selector and `includeDerived` flag. It deliberately excludes `SkillId`,
revision number, owner identity, and `Appearance`; those values are identity,
ownership, revision, or presentation rather than gameplay semantics. Thus a unique
owner-valid starter whose appearance was customized remains the same gameplay
candidate and is reused; recovery never rewrites its appearance.

An equipped reference is always the exact `(SkillId, revision)` returned by Store.
A later edit creates a different revision and cannot mutate a projectile already
admitted under an earlier exact reference.

### 63.5 Legal acquisition, recovery, and equipment

The sole normal-player provisioning surface is the permission-level-zero server
command `/gramarye starter`. It runs on the authoritative server thread for the
issuing player only. Console, command block, fake or absent player, and another
player as target are rejected; the command has no operator-only alternate form.

Provisioning is serialized on the server thread and fail-closed. Store submission
and Attachment publication retain their existing separate atomic owners; the whole
algorithm is deliberately recoverable rather than a new cross-owner transaction:

1. Read equipment slot 0 first. If occupied, re-read its exact Store revision,
   verify owner, decode through the formal registries, and compare
   `StarterGameplayFingerprintV0`. One owner-valid semantic match returns idempotent
   success without scanning, minting, or equipping. Any missing, stale,
   undecodable, wrong-owner, or nonmatching occupied reference rejects without
   changing that slot or any other state.
2. Only when slot 0 is empty, call the existing public read-only route
   `SkillDefinitionStoreService.submissionPort().observePendingRecovery(
   MinecraftServer, SkillOwnerId)`. Proceed only when it returns
   `PendingRecoveryProjection.Available` with an empty `chains()` list.
   `Available` with any chain, `TargetInvalid`, or `Unavailable` rejects without
   mutation. The command never invokes package-private
   `SkillSubmissionRecoveryService.recoverPersistedPlayer(ServerPlayer)`; login
   recovery remains the sole journal mutation owner. Then read the
   player's current bounded list of at most 256 `LatestStateView` values and examine
   only definitions owned by this player. For each present exact pointer, re-read
   its Store revision, verify owner again, decode through the formal registries, and
   compare the fingerprint. An invalid candidate is not a match and is never
   repaired in place.
3. Exactly one semantic match reuses its exact stored reference. More than one match
   is an ambiguity and fails without creating, equipping, or overwriting anything.
   With zero matches, compute `P9StarterSkillIdentityV0`. If the Attachment has any
   explicit latest pointer for that ID, or Store `latestReference` or `ownerOf`
   reports any state for that ID—including canonical Store state without a matching
   Attachment pointer—the route is inconsistent/colliding and rejects. Only when
   both the Attachment explicit latest route and Store authority are absent may the
   command inspect the exact Draft at that ID: reuse it only
   when its complete canonical bytes/base state equal the command's required Draft;
   any other existing Draft is a collision and rejects without overwrite. If absent,
   require the inherited 32-Draft cap to have space, then perform an immediate
   same-server-tick `findDraft` reread and require the route still absent before
   invoking `PlayerSkillAttachmentService.putDraft`. This reread is mandatory
   because `putDraft` is an ordinary replacement-capable P4 owner; P9 may never use
   that capability to overwrite a nonidentical same-ID Draft. Publish exactly that
   one canonical Draft. Submit the same
   caller-known ID through the existing validation/submission/Store path and require
   the returned exact reference to decode and match before selection.
4. A pre-Store rejection may leave only that same deterministic canonical Draft;
   later command/reconnect/restart recovers it by ID and never mints a second Draft.
   A committed Store step with interrupted latest publication remains exclusively
   under existing journal/login recovery; the command rejects until recovery is
   terminal and then finds the same semantic candidate. It never deletes a Draft,
   rewrites editor state, invents another recovery marker, or retries automatically.
5. Immediately call `equippedAt(player, 0)` again and require an available empty
   result before invoking `setEquipped(player, 0, Optional.of(reference))`. This
   reread is mandatory because `setEquipped` is replacement-capable. Rejection or
   an observation that the serialized slot is no longer empty leaves the slot
   unchanged and fails without a fallback slot or overwrite.

Creation failure, validation failure, Store rejection, Attachment rejection, or
ambiguous recovery is fail-closed. There is no rollback that deletes an immutable
revision: if submission succeeded but later equip failed, the valid owned revision
remains and a later bounded recovery can find it. This is not duplication of
persistent truth.

### 63.6 Client input and P7 sequence ownership

The client registers exactly one P9 key mapping, default key `R`, in client-only
source and through the platform's client key-mapping registration event. On each
discrete key press it attempts exactly one send of the existing P7 `CastIntent` for
slot 0, with the P7 optional target and direction hints absent. It creates no new P9
packet and transmits no skill ID, revision, action, geometry, target, damage, mana,
or presentation fact.

The physical owners are exact. Package-private final
`com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.network.P9ClientKeyMappings` is annotated with
`@SuppressWarnings("removal")` and
`@EventBusSubscriber(modid = Gramarye.MOD_ID, value = Dist.CLIENT,
bus = EventBusSubscriber.Bus.MOD)` solely because `RegisterKeyMappingsEvent` is an
`IModBusEvent`; the narrow suppression covers only the locked platform's
for-removal `bus()`/`Bus` selector and cannot suppress raw/unchecked diagnostics.
It delegates registration of the sole key to package-private final game-bus client
owner `P9ClientCastInput`. That owner handles `ClientTickEvent.Post`; existing
same-package `P7ClientLifecycleEvents` calls its package-private connection open and
close methods on `LoggingIn`/`LoggingOut`. Client level unload does not reset a live
connection sequence. Each actual payload is exactly
`new CastIntentPayload(new CastIntent(sequence, 0, CastInputKind.CAST, 0, null,
null))`.

Sequence ownership is per live client connection. The first sequence is 1 and the
allowed range is 1 through `Long.MAX_VALUE`. A press while the sender or connection
is unavailable is suppressed without consuming a value. For every actual send
attempt, the client snapshots the current value and advances to the next value—or
marks the connection exhausted for `Long.MAX_VALUE`—*before* invoking the locked
varargs method `PacketDistributor.sendToServer(CustomPacketPayload,
CustomPacketPayload...)` with the one leading `CastIntentPayload` and an empty
additional-payload array. Therefore successful return, uncertain submission,
`RuntimeException`, and `Error` each consume that value exactly once; the same
`RuntimeException` or `Error` propagates and the value is never retried or reused.
After an attempted send of `Long.MAX_VALUE`, further presses on that connection are
suppressed until disconnect. A later valid press after an earlier failed attempt uses
the next value unless the connection is exhausted. A new connection begins again at
1 and P7's server session state determines admission. Key repeats are individual
platform press events and remain subject to the existing P7 token bucket and replay
checks.

Common and dedicated-server code must not load the key mapping, client sender,
renderer, or other client-only class. The sender obtains only the already-authorized
network registration surface; no common static initializer refers to it.

### 63.7 Server-observed cast geometry

P7 first performs its existing root authorization in the existing order: connection
and player identity, main-thread handoff, sequence/replay/rate admission, slot,
exact Store reference, owner, capability, and an `AdvisoryTargetCheck` result of
`VALID`. Only after those checks pass does the
root package-private P7 ingress implementer sample the current `ServerPlayer` eye
position and normalized server look vector. It ignores all client hints.

The exact origin in blocks is:

```text
eyePosition + normalizedServerLook * 0.10 + (0.0, -0.10, 0.0)
```

Every source component and computed origin component must be finite. The look vector
must have finite, positive squared length and is normalized before encoding. Each
normalized component is multiplied by 32767, rounded using Java
`StrictMath.rint` (nearest integer with ties to even), and clamped to
`[-32767, 32767]`. `-32768` is reserved and invalid. Individual zero components are
valid, but the encoded three-component tuple must not be all zero. Decode divides
each component by 32767.0 and normalizes the decoded vector once more before applying
motion; decode failure or a zero/nonfinite result rejects the cast.

The package-private immutable scalar handoff is exact:

```java
record CastGeometryExecutionDataV0(
        ResourceLocation dimension,
        double originX,
        double originY,
        double originZ,
        int directionXQ15,
        int directionYQ15,
        int directionZQ15,
        int profileCode) implements RuntimeExecutionData {}
```

Its compact constructor is pure. It requires nonnull dimension, finite coordinates,
`-30_000_000.0 <= originX/originZ < 30_000_000.0`,
`-20_000_000.0 <= originY < 20_000_000.0`, the exact Q15 rules above, and profile
code 0. These are structural limits only; it performs no Level, chunk, build-height,
or world-border lookup. After geometry calculation and before constructing the
record, P7 requires the player's current `ServerLevel` dimension to equal the
dimension field and `BlockPos.containing(origin)` to satisfy
`serverLevel.isInWorldBounds`, `serverLevel.isLoaded`, and
`serverLevel.getWorldBorder().isWithinBounds(originX, originZ)`. P5 repeats the
structural/same-dimension check at root admission, and the spawn handoff repeats the
live Level/loaded/world-border predicates immediately before mutation.

The record contains no `ServerPlayer`, `Level`, `Vec3`, client object, runtime server token,
tick, capability, Store, or service reference. P7 invokes the new package-private
four-argument P5 root ingress shape
`admitAuthenticatedPlayerCast(MinecraftServer, ServerPlayer, SkillReference,
CastGeometryExecutionDataV0)`. P7's connection sequence is already consumed by its
own session/replay owner and does not cross this unchanged public RootIngressPort
boundary.

This is a narrow P9 extension of the existing package-private ingress, not a public
P7 boundary change. P5—not P7—captures and binds the positive runtime tick and exact
`RuntimeServerToken` while admitting the root. Wrong-thread, stopped runtime,
wrong-server, invalid geometry, bad profile, stale exact reference, or overflow
rejects before any action, mana, entity, or presentation effect.

### 63.8 Root admission, lifetime horizon, and retained authority

For this canonical P9 cast only, the P5 root execution horizon is exactly 100 runtime
ticks. This narrowly supersedes the earlier P9-unimplemented root horizon of zero;
all other P5 admissions keep their existing rules. Existing P5 coordinates remain
exact: `baseTick = checked(currentRuntimeTick + 1)`, root delay is 0,
`scheduledRuntimeTick = baseTick`, and
`deadlineRuntimeTick = checked(baseTick + 100)`. Overflow rejects. P5's deadline is
inclusive for queued event execution. A projectile hit must occur strictly before
that deadline so a child published after the current drain remains eligible at the
next P5 drain.

P5 pins the admitted exact `(SkillId, revision)`, owner, instance ID, root event ID,
runtime server token identity, lease, remaining budgets, and absolute deadline. It
does not re-resolve LatestStateView during the flight. Unequipping slot 0 or creating
a newer revision after admission does not revoke the in-flight exact revision.
Owner logout, death, dimension change, connection replacement, runtime stop, reload
shutdown, server mismatch, token mismatch, lease loss, or missing exact revision
does invalidate it. A later connection with the same player UUID cannot revive an
invalidated permit.

The retained object is a P5-owned, root-package, package-private one-future-child
permit. Its REAL mode contains exactly one private final identity reference to the
same `SkillRuntimeService` owner that created and indexed it; that owner is the sole
object mutated by both entity-facing operations. The field and service identity are
inaccessible to the entity: the entity retains only the permit and cannot query,
extract, cast to, or otherwise obtain general P5 service authority. The permit is
not a P6 execution context, GuardPort, transaction receipt, CommitPlan, observer,
trace, `ServerPlayer`, world object, Store handle, scheduler, or general event
publisher. It is live pending ownership, not completed-event history, and it is
never persisted or sent to a client.

### 63.9 Permit reservation and state machine

For a valid node-0 `spawn_projectile` action, the root P6 adapter must ask the
current context's one-shot P5 opener to detach the one continuation from the
existing current-dispatch child reservation before it invokes P6 resolution, mana
handling, or the world spawn commit. The adapter owns that call-scoped reservation
until successful
entity insertion transfers it. Reservation failure rejects the action. Any guard,
resolve, plan, observer, arithmetic, commit, exception, or spawn failure before
transfer closes the reservation exactly once.

The reservation performs zero random draws and preserves P4's sole production
`UUID.randomUUID()` owner. From positive `runtimeServerToken.value()` and the held
positive future child `heldChildEventId.value()`, it constructs the exact
deterministic pair:

```text
permit UUID     = new UUID(runtimeServerToken.value(), heldChildEventId.value())
projectile UUID = new UUID(~runtimeServerToken.value(), heldChildEventId.value())
```

The complemented most-significant half makes the two UUIDs unequal; the positive
token/EventId and complement make both nonzero. P5 binds both UUIDs, the positive runtime server token, root
identities, owner, dimension, source family, absolute deadline, and capacity for
exactly one future child before constructing the entity. A defensive all-zero value,
equality between the two UUIDs, collision in the active permit index, or
already-loaded entity UUID fails closed with no retry and no alternate/random ID.
The same transition atomically detaches exactly one firm P5 child-reservation unit,
including its future EventId, from the current source dispatch. Its identity is
deterministically ordinal 1 of the existing current-dispatch reserved range,
`eventIdStart + 1`, and its later child sequence is 1. Detach decrements only the
call-scoped `currentReservationCount`; the instance, attribution, and server
`reservedPending` counts for that unit remain held by the active permit. The
`currentReservationOwner` is cleared exactly when the decremented call-scoped count
becomes zero and otherwise remains the same exact instance; this metadata transition
does not release the detached unit. The
ordinary completed-empty execution batch then releases every other unit in the
current reservation. Once a permit has detached, a nonempty ordinary
`RuntimeChildPlan` from that node is an invariant rejection and closes the permit;
the same reserved ID can never also become an immediate child. Event high-water is
not advanced a second time. Unused IDs from the remainder of the originally
reserved range remain ordinary permanent holes. The detached unit counts against
the instance, attribution,
server-pending, lineage-work, direct-child, and zero-delay work ceilings throughout
RESERVED and OPEN. Reservation also proves that the immutable event-ancestry depth
is within its existing bound, but depth is a property rather than sibling capacity
and is never decremented or released. Minting the EventId permanently advances P5's
event sequence; that headroom is consumed even if the reservation later closes
unused. Claim converts the reserved pending work rather than incrementing it; close
releases only the live pending/capacity counts and never the depth fact or EventId.
Lineage headroom is computed with checked nonnegative arithmetic as
`eventsPerSkillInstance - instance.lifetimeEvents - instance.reservedPending`.
Existing committed children are already counted in `lifetimeEvents`; every detached
permit remains in `reservedPending`. Claim atomically decrements the instance,
attribution, and server detached reserved-pending counts, adds the exact committed
child, and increments `lifetimeEvents` exactly once. Close decrements only those
three detached reserved-pending counts. No duplicate lineage counter is introduced.
The permit identity is independent of the planned projectile UUID. The server entity
constructor installs the planned UUID before insertion; the first valid hit claim
only verifies that the loaded entity still has that exact UUID. It never first-binds
or changes either identity. A zero, currently active-index-colliding, mismatched, or
inactive UUID fails closed; P9 creates no historical UUID tombstone after cleanup.

The exact externally meaningful state machine is:

```text
RESERVED
  -- successful addFreshEntity and ownership transfer --> OPEN
  -- SPAWN_NOT_APPLIED / any pre-transfer failure -----> CLOSED_NO_HIT

OPEN
  -- first eligible living hit atomically queued ------> CLAIMED_PENDING_DAMAGE
  -- wrong thread/server precondition -----------------> OPEN (REJECTED; zero mutation)
  -- owning-server validation/queue reject ------------> CLOSED_NO_HIT
  -- block/miss/expiry/unload/owner loss/stop ----------> CLOSED_NO_HIT

CLAIMED_PENDING_DAMAGE
  -- damage child terminal/unload/stop -----------------> CLOSED_AFTER_HIT

CLOSED_NO_HIT or CLOSED_AFTER_HIT
  -- every later claim/close ---------------------------> same closed state
```

Only `OPEN` may publish. The package-private entity-facing capability exposes exactly
two narrow operations: `claimLoadedEntityHit(MinecraftServer,
ProjectileHitCandidateV0)`, which may atomically allocate and queue the sole child,
and non-publishing idempotent `closeWithoutHit(MinecraftServer,
ProjectileClosureReason)`. Neither operation is public or protected. Both delegate
only to the permit's one private-final exact
`SkillRuntimeService` owner identity, which mutates the same active index, instance,
pending counts, queue, and lease graph that created the permit. The entity cannot
obtain that owner reference. The owner service has internal stop/fault cleanup;
there is no public
cancel, schedule, publish, query-service, or state-mutation escape hatch.

A successful legal slice has at most one continuation claim, one child event, one
P6 damage invocation, and one platform `hurt` attempt. The first OPEN callback at or
after deadline cannot itself counterfeit a close from the wrong thread/server. On
the owning server thread, an at/after-deadline claim closes/discards without
publication. Duplicate callbacks and every callback after that or another closure
are no-ops except bounded diagnostics.

### 63.10 Source lineage, matching, and child publication

Node 0's successful output source family is the immutable tuple:

```text
SourceFamilyKey(
  same SkillInstanceId,
  sourceEventId = node 0 EventId,
  producerNodeIndex = 0,
  outputOrdinal = 0)
```

Its exact package-private scalar carrier is:

```java
record SourceFamilyKey(
        SkillInstanceId skillInstanceId,
        EventId sourceEventId,
        int producerNodeIndex,
        int outputOrdinal) {}
```

The compact constructor requires nonnull positive identities, node index 0, and
output ordinal 0 for this slice. It performs no Store, entity, or world lookup.

The exact SkillReference and direct `sourceDerivationDepth=0` are adjacent immutable
lineage fields and are always verified with the complete key. The permit retains all
of them. An entity UUID, permit ID, target UUID, request ID, or action ID is never a
substitute for source lineage. A source selector matches only the same
SkillInstanceId, sourceEventId, exact revision, producer node index, and output
ordinal. With `includeDerived=false`, only source-derivation depth 0 matches. With
`includeDerived=true`, source-derivation depth 0 through the frozen P5 maximum of 32
matches. Negative source depth, source depth greater than 32, checked-increment
overflow, wrong family, or arbitrary projectile identity rejects. P9 produces no
derivative output; its accepted hit is the direct source-depth-zero member, but the
flag therefore has real and testable semantics.

On the first accepted hit, P5 atomically revalidates token, server, owner/lifecycle,
dimension, lease, exact reference, deadline, instance budget, node budget, and the
one-child reservation. P5 then converts the exact future EventId held by that
reservation into the child and queues node index 1 with delay 0 for the next
scheduler cycle. The
child has parent EventId equal to node 0's event ID, child sequence exactly 1,
existing P5 event-ancestry `derivationDepth=1`, the direct
`sourceDerivationDepth=0` output-family source, and the unchanged absolute root
deadline. Event-ancestry depth and source-derivation depth are distinct,
independently bounded fields; `includeDerived` reads only the latter. A rejected or
cancelled collision consumes no additional EventId and never publishes the one
already held by the reservation.
Collision code never calls node 1 or P6 synchronously.

When node 1 later enters P6, its P6 `requestId` and `sourceEventId` both equal the
held child EventId because that is the current `RuntimeEvent`. The family carrier's
`sourceEventId` remains the node-0 EventId. These unequal coordinates are both
required and must never be normalized to one another.

Queue refusal, allocation overflow, or any revalidation failure closes the permit
without a child. The absolute deadline is never renewed: an accepted hit before the
deadline receives only the remaining horizon, and a hit at or after the deadline
closes without publication.

The accepted child's `createdRuntimeTick` is the current P5 runtime tick, its delay
is 0, and its `scheduledRuntimeTick` is therefore that same current dispatch tick,
exactly as existing P5 child scheduling requires. The entity callback never invokes
P5 during the child's parent dispatch; it enqueues after the current P5 drain, so the
already-eligible child executes at the next drain without synchronous re-entry.
Publication is legal only when the current tick is strictly before the held inclusive
deadline. The future EventId is minted by P5 while the source event is in flight and
then held across the entire RESERVED/OPEN lifetime using the existing firm
child-reservation sequence rules. Claim never mints a second ID. Closing an unused
reservation leaves the ordinary permanent sequence hole that already follows from
unused firm P5 child capacity; IDs are never reused or rewound.

### 63.11 Replacement P6 public transaction boundary

The sole P6 public entry remains
`com.yo1no.gramarye.magic.runtime.mana.P6RuntimeExecutionBridge`. Its existing public
top-level type count and capability-first acquisition remain unchanged. Its old
ten-parameter damage-scalar `execute` operation is removed and is not retained as an
overload or compatibility bridge. It is replaced by exactly this Java contract:

```java
public static void execute(
        P6RuntimeExecutionCapability capability,
        ServerPlayer actor,
        Invocation input,
        GuardPort guard,
        WorldCommitPort commitPort,
        AppliedFactObserver observer);

public sealed interface Invocation
        permits SpawnProjectileInvocation, DamageInvocation {}

public record SpawnProjectileInvocation(
        ResourceLocation actionTypeKey,
        long requestId,
        long sourceEventId,
        ResourceLocation dimension,
        double originX,
        double originY,
        double originZ,
        int directionXQ15,
        int directionYQ15,
        int directionZQ15,
        int profileCode,
        long manaCost) implements Invocation {}

public record DamageInvocation(
        ResourceLocation actionTypeKey,
        long requestId,
        long sourceEventId,
        UUID targetId,
        long magnitude,
        long manaCost) implements Invocation {}

public interface WorldCommitPort {
    CommitDisposition commitSpawn(SpawnCommit command);
    CommitDisposition commitDamage(DamageCommit command);
}

public record SpawnCommit(
        long requestId,
        long sourceEventId,
        ResourceLocation dimension,
        double originX,
        double originY,
        double originZ,
        int directionXQ15,
        int directionYQ15,
        int directionZQ15,
        int profileCode,
        long manaCost) {}

public record DamageCommit(
        long requestId,
        long sourceEventId,
        UUID targetId,
        long magnitude,
        long manaCost) {}

public enum CommitDisposition {
    APPLIED,
    NOT_APPLIED
}
```

For both variants the public numeric identity is derived from the *current*
`RuntimeEvent` and is exact:

```text
requestId == sourceEventId == current RuntimeEvent.eventId().value()
```

Thus node 0 uses the node-0 EventId and node 1 uses its held child EventId. These
two P6 fields identify the current P6 request; they are not P5 lineage aliases. In
particular, node 1's `ProjectileHitExecutionDataV0.sourceFamily().sourceEventId()`
remains the node-0 EventId and is intentionally distinct from node 1's P6
`sourceEventId`.

All applicable compact constructors reject null IDs, keys, and dimensions;
nonpositive request or source IDs; coordinates outside the pure static domain in
§63.7; an illegal/all-zero Q15 tuple; `-32768`; nonzero profile code; nonpositive or
over-ceiling magnitude; and mana outside existing P6 bounds. Generic P6
`DamageInvocation` and `DamageCommit` preserve the existing inclusive magnitude
domain `1..1_000_000`, including values not divisible by 1000. Divisibility by 1000
and exact abstract-magnitude-to-float conversion are additional checks only in the
exact P9 `gramarye:damage` descriptor, mapper, resolver, and P9 world-commit path;
the canonical P9 value is 4000. Constructors make no live build-height,
loaded-chunk, world-border, entity, or other world lookup; the P7/P5/root handoff
checkpoints in §63.7 own those predicates.
The sealed `Invocation` permits exactly its two
records. `WorldCommitPort` is intentionally not sealed: in the unnamed Java module a
public sealed interface cannot legally permit the required package-private root
implementation in a different package. Its openness at the Java type level is
closed in production by unforgeable package-private capability acquisition, the
single root composition, and exact static/JAR inventories.

The method remains `public static void`, returns no receipt, plan, result, mutation,
or runtime capability, declares no checked exception, and has no overload. Null
`CommitDisposition`, null guard result, null applied fact, or an unrecognized sealed
value is an invariant failure. The bridge never catches or translates a
`RuntimeException` or `Error` from the guard, commit port, or observer; the same
object propagates. Cleanup owners may perform non-throwing idempotent cleanup but
must not mask or replay the primary failure.

### 63.12 Closed P6 request, step, resolve, and commit semantics

The internal P6 effect request family after P9 contains exactly
`SpawnProjectileRequest` and the existing `DamageEffectRequest`. The sealed
`EffectStep` family contains exactly `SpawnProjectileStep` and `DamageEffectStep`.
The production action-executor registry contains exactly the keys
`gramarye:spawn_projectile` and `gramarye:damage`; the former projects a typed spawn
invocation and the latter a typed damage invocation. Both are pure and deterministic.
No executor obtains a world, P5 service, entity manager, Attachment, Store, or P8
publisher.

The package-private action projection after-set and exact descriptors are:

```java
sealed interface ActionInvocation
        permits SpawnProjectileActionInvocation, DamageActionInvocation {
    ResourceLocation actionRegistryKey();
    EffectRequestId requestId();
    SourceEventId sourceEventId();
    long manaCost();
    CompensationPolicy compensationPolicy();
}

record SpawnProjectileActionInvocation(
        ResourceLocation actionRegistryKey,
        EffectRequestId requestId,
        SourceEventId sourceEventId,
        ResourceLocation dimension,
        double originX,
        double originY,
        double originZ,
        int directionXQ15,
        int directionYQ15,
        int directionZQ15,
        int profileCode,
        long manaCost,
        CompensationPolicy compensationPolicy) implements ActionInvocation {}

record DamageActionInvocation(
        ResourceLocation actionRegistryKey,
        EffectRequestId requestId,
        SourceEventId sourceEventId,
        DamageTargetReference target,
        long magnitude,
        long manaCost,
        CompensationPolicy compensationPolicy) implements ActionInvocation {}

interface ActionExecutor {
    ActionExecutorOutcome execute(ActionInvocation input);
}

sealed interface ActionExecutorOutcome
        permits ProducedActionRequest, NoActionRequest {}

record ProducedActionRequest(EffectRequest request)
        implements ActionExecutorOutcome {}
```

`NoActionRequest.INSTANCE` remains the sole no-request result. The immutable
`ActionExecutorRegistry` has exactly two entries keyed by
`gramarye:spawn_projectile` and `gramarye:damage`. Each executor requires both its
matching sealed input subtype and exact registry key; null, cross-variant, or
mismatched-key input returns `NoActionRequest`, never a cast/default success. The
compact constructors enforce §63.7/§63.11 scalar bounds without world access.

The request after-set removes `target()` from the common interface and is exact:

```java
sealed interface EffectRequest
        permits SpawnProjectileRequest, DamageEffectRequest {
    EffectRequestId requestId();
    SourceEventId sourceEventId();
    long manaCost();
    CompensationPolicy compensationPolicy();
}

record SpawnProjectileRequest(
        EffectRequestId requestId,
        SourceEventId sourceEventId,
        ResourceLocation dimension,
        double originX,
        double originY,
        double originZ,
        int directionXQ15,
        int directionYQ15,
        int directionZQ15,
        int profileCode,
        long manaCost,
        CompensationPolicy compensationPolicy) implements EffectRequest {}

record DamageEffectRequest(
        EffectRequestId requestId,
        SourceEventId sourceEventId,
        DamageTargetReference target,
        long magnitude,
        long manaCost,
        CompensationPolicy compensationPolicy) implements EffectRequest {}
```

Only the damage variant owns/requires `target()`. Spawn has no sentinel target,
permit, actor, world, UUID, context, or service field. Request validation is an
exhaustive sealed switch.

The step and internal commit after-sets are exact:

```java
sealed interface EffectStep permits DamageEffectStep, SpawnProjectileStep {
    int index();
    EffectStepKind kind();
    int declaredPrimaryMutationUpperBound();
    int declaredChildIntentUpperBound();
}

enum EffectStepKind {
    DAMAGE,
    SPAWN_PROJECTILE
}

record SpawnProjectileStep(
        int index,
        ResourceLocation dimension,
        double originX,
        double originY,
        double originZ,
        int directionXQ15,
        int directionYQ15,
        int directionZQ15,
        int profileCode,
        int declaredPrimaryMutationUpperBound,
        int declaredChildIntentUpperBound) implements EffectStep {
    @Override
    public EffectStepKind kind() {
        return EffectStepKind.SPAWN_PROJECTILE;
    }
}

interface EffectCommitPort {
    boolean isAvailable();
    EffectStepOutcome commitSpawn(
            SpawnProjectileRequest request,
            SpawnProjectileStep step);
    EffectStepOutcome commitDamage(
            DamageEffectRequest request,
            DamageEffectStep step);
}
```

The `EffectStepKind` declaration order preserves existing `DAMAGE` ordinal 0 and
adds `SPAWN_PROJECTILE` ordinal 1. `SpawnProjectileStep.kind()` is fixed to the
latter; its index is 0, primary-mutation upper bound is 1, and child-intent upper
bound is 0. Request IDs and mana remain on the request rather than being duplicated
on the step; the external P5 continuation is not a P6 child intent.

`EffectCommitPort` replaces `DamageEffectCommitPort`, whose after-count is zero.
`PreparedEffectExecution`, the sole `EffectExecutionEngine`, and the existing sole
`ActionDamageTransactionEngine` are generalized in place to this port and the
sealed action/request families; those owner names remain exact and no parallel
engine/loop/alias is added. The transaction engine's package-private execution
shape becomes
`execute(ActionInvocation, ManaAccountAccess, int, EffectExecutionGuard,
EffectCommitPort)` and still returns the existing closed
`ActionDamageTransactionResult` family. All existing mana, compensation, result,
failure, and Throwable vocabularies remain unchanged.

The existing `EffectResolver.resolve(EffectRequest, int)` descriptor is unchanged;
its one production implementation exhaustively maps spawn request to spawn step and
damage request to damage step. The commit loop exhaustively matches exactly
`(SpawnProjectileRequest, SpawnProjectileStep)` or
`(DamageEffectRequest, DamageEffectStep)`. A cross-variant pair takes the existing
`UNSUPPORTED_COMMIT_STEP` invariant terminal; there is no default success. The
call-scoped bridge adapter builds the matching public `SpawnCommit` or
`DamageCommit` from request identity/mana plus step scalars, maps public `APPLIED`
and `NOT_APPLIED` to the existing internal `EffectStepOutcome`, rejects null, and
propagates the same `RuntimeException`/`Error`. Production `isAvailable()` is true
because the old unavailable production port is removed; direct test doubles retain
the false path.

The existing `TARGET_RESOLVED` trace stage, position, and count remain. For damage it
means exact target resolution. For targetless spawn it means request-specific
reference validation completed with target cardinality zero and dimension/geometry
validation complete. It never means a fake/sentinel target and no new trace stage is
added.

The existing P6 bounds—one request, one target, at most eight plan steps/primary
mutations, two mana mutations, ten guard checks, and a 32-entry call trace—remain
ceilings. Each canonical P9 invocation resolves to exactly one step. Existing guard
points, compensation policy, result terminals, applied-step vocabulary, and ordered
commit behavior remain unchanged. P9 adds no random draw and no retry.

Before resolution the adapter verifies actor/server identity and reserves
continuation availability as §63.9 requires. The engine alone owns the existing
ENTRY, PRE_COMMIT, and BEFORE_STEP guard checks. The pure spawn resolver verifies
the typed request IDs, fixed profile, dimension, geometry, cost, and supplied child
capacity; its invocation does not contain a permit and the resolver performs no
hidden P5, actor, server, guard, or world query. The
`SpawnProjectileStep` copies only the validated scalar values. At ordered commit,
the handoff revalidates and consumes the exact call-scoped reservation. The injected
port returns `APPLIED` only if one completely initialized entity was
accepted by `ServerLevel.addFreshEntity`; false returns `NOT_APPLIED`. An exception
or uncertain platform result is not rewritten as `NOT_APPLIED`, and the operation
is never replayed.

The adapter/bridge verifies damage actor/server and current hit execution-data
identity. Before dispatch and at each node-1 ENTRY, PRE_COMMIT, and BEFORE_STEP guard,
P5 looks up `ProjectileHitExecutionDataV0.permitId()` in its active-permit index and
requires the exact indexed permit object to be CLAIMED_PENDING_DAMAGE and bound to
the current `RuntimeEvent`, held child EventId, instance, reference, token, and
source family. The engine owns the same guard points and receives only their closed
decision; no P6 or entity permit getter exists. Pure damage resolution verifies
the typed request IDs, target, exact magnitude, zero canonical cost, and supplied
child capacity. At ordered commit the port returns `APPLIED` only when the one
platform `hurt` call returns
true; false returns `NOT_APPLIED`. A primary mutation count and applied fact arise
only from `APPLIED`. Neither a resolved request nor a collision is itself applied
truth.

### 63.13 Adapter, invoker, and world-commit composition

`com.yo1no.gramarye.P6RuntimeExecutionPortAdapter` remains the one package-private
P5-to-P6 adapter. Its input mapper becomes an exact sealed/typed mapper for the two
registered actions. Its package-private `P6ExecutionBridgeInvoker` descriptor is
replaced in lockstep with the six-argument public method. No old scalar invoker or
overload remains.

The exact package-private mapper/invoker after-set is:

```java
record P6RuntimeExecutionInput(
        ServerPlayer actor,
        P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.Invocation invocation) {}

@FunctionalInterface
interface P6RuntimeExecutionInputMapper {
    Optional<P6RuntimeExecutionInput> map(
            RuntimeEvent event,
            RuntimeExecutionContext context);
}

@FunctionalInterface
interface P6ExecutionBridgeInvoker {
    void execute(
            P6RuntimeExecutionCapability capability,
            ServerPlayer actor,
            P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.Invocation input,
            P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.GuardPort guard,
            P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.WorldCommitPort commitPort,
            P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.AppliedFactObserver observer);
}
```

The input record requires the matching sealed invocation and exact actor identity.
There is no separate action key, target, magnitude, mana, geometry, or permit field
beside that invocation, and no old ten-argument invoker overload.

For node 0 the adapter validates `CastGeometryExecutionDataV0`, obtains the P5
continuation reservation described in §63.9, constructs the one
`SpawnProjectileInvocation`, and creates one call-scoped
`com.yo1no.gramarye.P9WorldEffectHandoff`. For node 1 it validates
`ProjectileHitExecutionDataV0`, constructs one `DamageInvocation`, and creates a new
call-scoped handoff. In both cases it creates the existing call-scoped
`P8AppliedFactHandoff` observer and invokes P6 once. Every early or exceptional node
0 path closes an adapter-owned reservation; successful spawn transfers the OPEN
permit to the entity before the bridge call returns.

For each node the adapter obtains the IDs solely through the current source-backed
`P6RuntimeExecutionIdentity.fromPublishedEventId(event.eventId().value())`, so
`requestId == sourceEventId == event.eventId().value()` exactly. On node 1 the held
child EventId is the current event ID; the node-0 EventId remains separately in
`ProjectileHitExecutionDataV0.sourceFamily().sourceEventId()` and must not be copied
into either P6 identity field.

`P9WorldEffectHandoff` is a root-package, package-private final class implementing
`P6RuntimeExecutionBridge.WorldCommitPort`. Its constructor is package-private; all
fields are private final; it has no public/protected constructor, field, static
member, getter, nested escape type, or service-locator access. Its only public
members are the two Java-mandated interface overrides `commitSpawn(SpawnCommit)` and
`commitDamage(DamageCommit)`. A handoff is retained for one P6 call only and captures
only the call's actor, server, execution data, and optional Opened aggregate. It is
never stored in an entity or global registry.

Its one constructor descriptor and four retained fields are exact:

```java
P9WorldEffectHandoff(
        MinecraftServer server,
        ServerPlayer actor,
        RuntimeExecutionData executionData,
        Optional<RuntimeProjectileContinuationOpenResult.Opened> openedContinuation);
```

The constructor accepts only `CastGeometryExecutionDataV0` plus one present REAL
RESERVED `Opened`, or `ProjectileHitExecutionDataV0` plus an empty value. Every
other data/Opened pairing rejects. The four corresponding fields are exactly one
private-final `MinecraftServer`, `ServerPlayer`, `RuntimeExecutionData`, and
`Optional<RuntimeProjectileContinuationOpenResult.Opened>`; there is no retained
`RuntimeExecutionContext`, `RuntimeEvent`, P6 request/step/plan, P8 observer, Store,
Attachment, or locator.

Spawn handoff constructs the projectile with all stable state, its planned UUID, and
its final RESERVED permit before calling `addFreshEntity`. A successful insertion
without that permit is structurally impossible. False, validation failure, or
exception transitions RESERVED to closed. Only after true does the handoff invoke
the same Opened aggregate's one-shot
`transferAfterAppliedSpawn(server, projectile)`; only
`TRANSFERRED` yields `APPLIED` and transfers entity ownership exactly once. Damage
handoff resolves exact currently loaded entity UUIDs and types from the stored hit
data, rechecks the projectile UUID and authenticated-caster witness after the
immediately preceding P5 guard established the child-event-to-indexed-permit
binding, and cannot fall back to a latest entity, name, network ID, client hint, or
unindexed permit object.

The package-private P5 reservation handle is named
`com.yo1no.gramarye.RuntimeProjectileContinuationPermit` and is a final concrete
class, not an abstract class or Java interface whose methods would become implicitly
public. It has an internal REAL/UNAVAILABLE mode established only by package-private
construction. Its claim and close methods are its exact two package-visible
operations. It has no public/protected member, constructor, or field. A REAL permit
contains exactly one private-final `SkillRuntimeService owner` identity; UNAVAILABLE
is noncapturing. That field is never exposed by an accessor and is used only by the
two operations. This avoids a constructor cycle and does not grant an entity a
general `SkillRuntimeService` reference. Permit, opener, and Opened contain zero
`Thread`, `ThreadLocal`, executor, task, future, or async fields; each operation asks
the exact supplied `MinecraftServer`/P5 owner to verify its current server-thread
predicate at call time.

The Opened transfer result is exactly `TRANSFERRED`, `REJECTED`, or
`ALREADY_TRANSFERRED`. Only the call-scoped world handoff calls it, and only after
`addFreshEntity` returned true. The owner requires the supplied object to be the
currently loaded exact planned UUID, dimension, caster witness, and permit-identity
witness. `TRANSFERRED` atomically changes RESERVED to OPEN without changing
pending/cap counters. Wrong server/thread/object returns `REJECTED` with zero state
mutation; a second call returns `ALREADY_TRANSFERRED`. Either result
other than `TRANSFERRED` after a true insertion is an invariant fault: the known
entity is discarded, the reservation is closed if possible, no APPLIED fact is
fabricated, and no retry occurs. On false return or a pre-transfer Throwable, the
adapter/handoff invokes the permit's same-server
`closeWithoutHit(server, SPAWN_NOT_APPLIED)` path, which may close RESERVED
directly. The entity never retains or can obtain Opened.

`RuntimeExecutionContext` retains its existing eight components in their existing
order and adds exactly one ninth package-private call-scoped component,
`RuntimeProjectileContinuationOpener projectileContinuationOpener`. The opener is a
package-private final concrete object backed by the current `SkillRuntimeService`,
server slot, source event, and `ChildReservation`; it is not a public functional
port and is never retained after the execution-port call. Its sole package-visible
operation is:

```java
RuntimeProjectileContinuationOpenResult openProjectileContinuation(
        ActionOutputKind outputKind,
        int outputOrdinal);
```

The first invocation consumes the opener exactly once. Only `(PROJECTILE, 0)` on
the exact canonical node 0, with `ChildReservation.capacity() >= 1`,
`executionBudget.zeroDelayChildCapacity() >= 1`, and
`currentRuntimeTick < sourceEvent.deadlineRuntimeTick()`, can detach ordinal 1.
Invalid arguments, either zero capacity, deadline/lifecycle failure, or an invariant
failure return the matching rejection without a permit, and no second invocation
may succeed. Every later invocation returns
`INVARIANT_REJECTED` without another ID, counter transition, or permit. The adapter
may obtain the opener only from the current context component and must not retain
either object.

The package-private call shapes are exact:

```java
RuntimePermitClaimDisposition claimLoadedEntityHit(
        MinecraftServer server,
        ProjectileHitCandidateV0 candidate);

RuntimePermitCloseDisposition closeWithoutHit(
        MinecraftServer server,
        ProjectileClosureReason reason);
```

The opener's closed result is a package-private sealed abstract class
`RuntimeProjectileContinuationOpenResult` with exactly two package-private nested
final variants, `Opened` and `Rejected`. `Opened` contains the nonnull REAL permit,
nonzero planned projectile UUID, the same private-final `SkillRuntimeService` owner
identity, and one private transfer-consumed bit. It exposes only package-visible
`permit()`, `plannedProjectileId()`, and the one-shot operation
`RuntimePermitTransferDisposition transferAfterAppliedSpawn(MinecraftServer,
P9StarterProjectile)`.
`RuntimePermitTransferDisposition` is a package-private enum with exactly
`TRANSFERRED`, `REJECTED`, and `ALREADY_TRANSFERRED`. All three identities originate
from
the same atomic P5 reservation; construction rejects an UNAVAILABLE permit or a
UUID not bound by that reservation. This call-scoped aggregate is the sole legal way
the handoff obtains the planned ID and activation authority without exposing a
permit owner/UUID accessor to the entity. `Rejected` contains one exact reason. The
rejection reason enum has exactly `CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE`,
`LIFECYCLE_UNAVAILABLE`, and `INVARIANT_REJECTED`. The permit's claim result is
exactly `QUEUED`, `REJECTED`, or `DUPLICATE_OR_LATE`; its close result is exactly
`CLOSED`, `ALREADY_CLOSED`, or `REJECTED`. A wrong thread or wrong
`MinecraftServer` returns `REJECTED` from either operation with zero state mutation;
it cannot counterfeit a close. The owning server's bounded lifecycle/deadline pass
later performs the actual closure. All named types are package-private fixed classes,
records, enums, or sealed results. `ProjectileHitCandidateV0` has exactly projectile
UUID,
target UUID, dimension, finite hit X/Y/Z in §63.7's static domain, and three legal
nonzero-tuple Q15 direction components. P5 verifies those untrusted scalars against
permit-owned token, instance, exact reference, source family, deadline, parent, held
EventId, and the currently loaded entities. It then constructs
`ProjectileHitExecutionDataV0` with the permit ID/source family inserted by P5; the
entity cannot supply or replace them. Runtime token, exact reference, instance,
deadline, parent/child EventIds, and event-ancestry depth remain solely on the child
`RuntimeEvent`, are equality-checked against the permit, and are not duplicated in
the execution-data record.

`closeWithoutHit` means “close without publishing another hit”; it is also the
idempotent entity-facing removal route after a prior claim. It may transition OPEN
to CLOSED_NO_HIT, CLAIMED_PENDING_DAMAGE to CLOSED_AFTER_HIT, or an adapter/handoff-
owned RESERVED permit to CLOSED_NO_HIT for `SPAWN_NOT_APPLIED`/pre-transfer cleanup,
but can never create, retry, or replace a child. UNAVAILABLE and wrong-thread/server
calls return `REJECTED` with zero mutation. The exact `ProjectileClosureReason`
after-set is
`SPAWN_NOT_APPLIED`, `BLOCK_OR_INVALID_HIT`, `RANGE_EXHAUSTED`, `AGE_EXHAUSTED`,
`DEADLINE_REACHED`, `OWNER_INVALIDATED`, `ENTITY_OR_LEVEL_REMOVED`,
`RELOAD_INVALIDATED`, `SERVER_STOPPED`, `RUNTIME_FAULT`, `CLAIM_REJECTED`, and
`DAMAGE_TERMINAL`; private diagnostic layout is implementation freedom.

### 63.14 Entity registration, construction, and client rendering

Register exactly one entity type, `gramarye:starter_projectile`, under the frozen mod
namespace. It uses `MobCategory.MISC`, size `0.25F x 0.25F`, `.noSave()`,
`.noSummon()`, tracking range 4 chunks, update interval 10 ticks, and velocity
updates enabled. The common
entity class is exactly `com.yo1no.gramarye.P9StarterProjectile`, root-package,
package-private, and final, and extends
`ThrowableItemProjectile`. It carries no public gameplay API.

The platform factory constructor `(EntityType<? extends
ThrowableItemProjectile>, Level)` accepts a client-side `Level` only and installs a
noncapturing permit in its internal UNAVAILABLE mode. The builder's `.noSummon()`
blocks the ordinary server summon route; any other server-side invocation of this
factory constructor throws an invariant failure before insertion. Every client
callback branches locally on client side/UNAVAILABLE and never fabricates a
`MinecraftServer`, calls either server-parameter permit operation, claims/closes,
damages, or initiates an authoritative discard; ordinary tracking owns client
removal. The server
constructor receives the REAL RESERVED permit, planned UUID, the admitted
`ServerPlayer actor`, and all immutable stable scalar data. It installs that UUID,
calls the ordinary `Projectile.setOwner(actor)`, and stores exactly one additional
private final transient `ServerPlayer authenticatedCasterIdentity` before insertion.
It checks server level and identity and stores every stable constructor-derived
scalar in private final fields. Exactly two private server-thread-only product fields
are mutable: `boolean locallyClaimedOrTerminal`, which moves monotonically from
false to true before the first terminal/claim call, and finite
`double accumulatedTravelDistance`, which starts at 0.0 and moves monotonically
through checked/clamped values no greater than 64.0. Neither is persisted or synced,
and no array/atomic wrapper is used to evade this exact field inventory. The
client constructor stores no caster (`null` is confined to UNAVAILABLE/client
branches). No `setPermit`, general
post-construction setter, lookup by service locator, reflection, delayed injection,
or mutable `Optional` is allowed. UNAVAILABLE cannot publish or close server work.
The caster field exists solely for `==` comparison with the currently resolved actor
at hit claim and damage commit; it is never serialized, synced, exposed, copied into
P5, or used as a service handle, and dies with the bounded entity.

The two and only two constructor descriptors are exact:

```java
P9StarterProjectile(
        EntityType<? extends ThrowableItemProjectile> type,
        Level level);

P9StarterProjectile(
        EntityType<? extends ThrowableItemProjectile> type,
        ServerLevel level,
        ServerPlayer actor,
        RuntimeProjectileContinuationOpenResult.Opened openedContinuation,
        CastGeometryExecutionDataV0 geometry);
```

Both are package-private. The first is the platform/client factory route and rejects
a server-side `Level`. The second requires `actor.serverLevel() == level`, the
Opened aggregate to be REAL/RESERVED and internally identity-consistent, and the
geometry dimension/live predicates to match the same level. It destructures that
same aggregate without retaining it. Before `addFreshEntity`, it installs the
aggregate's planned UUID, owner, exact initial position, decoded/re-normalized
motion, REAL permit, caster witness, and all immutable scalar flight state. There is
no overload,
post-construction permit/UUID injection, source-EventId parameter, or server factory
fallback.

The server handoff supplies the same validated
`RuntimeProjectileContinuationOpenResult.Opened` that it owns; the entity retains
only the aggregate's permit and installed UUID after construction. Neither value may
be substituted, re-derived, or randomly regenerated; both are obtained only by
destructuring that same Opened. The permit itself exposes no UUID or owner accessor.

The entity declares no additional UUID field: its planned identity is installed in
and read from the inherited Entity UUID. The entity has exactly two additional
package-visible, non-mutating identity
witnesses: `boolean hasAuthenticatedCasterIdentity(ServerPlayer candidate)` and
`boolean hasContinuationPermitIdentity(RuntimeProjectileContinuationPermit
candidate)`. Each performs only `==` against its corresponding private-final field;
neither exposes an object or UUID. The permit-object witness is used only by the
Opened transfer path and P5 claim/guard; damage handoff uses the caster witness and
inherited UUID after the immediately preceding P5 guard has established the exact
permit binding. No other package-visible gameplay operation is authorized.

The rendered item is always vanilla `Items.AMETHYST_SHARD`. Package-private final
client-only `com.yo1no.gramarye.P9StarterProjectileClientEvents` uses the same
class-local `@SuppressWarnings("removal")` plus MOD-bus Dist.CLIENT subscriber shape
as §63.6 and registers `P9StarterProjectileRegistration.type()` with the platform
`ThrownItemRenderer` during `EntityRenderersEvent.RegisterRenderers`. There is no
custom texture, model, item, data pack, or P8 projectile-spawn payload. Entity
registration is common; renderer and key registration are physically client-only
and absent from dedicated-server load edges.

The class's exact platform override surface is five members: public `tick()`,
protected `getDefaultItem()`, protected `onHitEntity(EntityHitResult)`, protected
`onHitBlock(BlockHitResult)`, and public `onRemovedFromLevel()`. It does not override
the final `Entity.discard()`, expose a public constructor, or widen another member.
`onRemovedFromLevel()` delegates the platform lifecycle then invokes its idempotent
close path once; it never publishes a hit.

### 63.15 Motion, sweep, range, and tick ordering

The initial motion is the decoded/re-normalized Q15 direction multiplied by exactly
1.5 blocks/tick. The implementation sets that vector directly; it does not call a
`shoot` overload that consumes random values. Inaccuracy is zero and random draws
are zero. Active flight applies the platform throwable values: air drag 0.99, water
drag 0.8, and gravity 0.03.

Each active entity tick performs at most one standard platform movement collision
sweep. P9 creates no second candidate scan, ray trace, or retry loop. Before a sweep
the entity locally checks server-side level, stored dimension, finite state,
lifetime, and its locally available exact owner identity/liveness. It does not and
cannot read the P5 runtime tick or deadline, and it does not query P5 through a third
permit operation. Every hit claim revalidates the owner service's current token,
lease, lifecycle, and strict-before-deadline predicate before publication. Age 0 is
the first eligible sweep. Once age reaches 100,
termination happens before another sweep, so there are at most 100 sweeps. The root
absolute deadline may terminate earlier.

Deadline ownership stays entirely in P5. On the existing LOWEST-priority
`ServerTickEvent.Post`, P5 performs the existing checked runtime-tick advance and
per-tick reset, then the ordinary inclusive event drain, and then exactly one
bounded active-permit sweep of at most 128 entries. After that inclusive drain, an
OPEN permit with `currentRuntimeTick >= deadlineRuntimeTick` is closed with
`DEADLINE_REACHED` and its loaded entity is discarded. A
CLAIMED_PENDING_DAMAGE permit at equality is retained only for its already committed
child to finish in that inclusive drain; its terminal hook closes it. If that exact
child is still committed/deferred at the first post-drain sweep where
`currentRuntimeTick > deadlineRuntimeTick`, P5 removes/expires that child through
the existing event/index accounting and closes the permit. A fault during this
ordering transfers control to the existing P5 fault cleanup and never creates a
second sweep or gameplay retry. Consequently the 100th legal entity sweep occurs
while P5 is still strictly before the deadline, and a child accepted there may run
at the immediately following inclusive drain.

P9 tracks accumulated actual movement distance with finite checked arithmetic. If a
proposed tick segment would exceed the remaining distance to 64.0 blocks, it clamps
that final segment to the exact remaining distance, sweeps that segment once, and
then terminates at exactly 64.0 if no accepted collision occurred. It does not take
one full overshooting step. Nonfinite movement, negative accumulation, arithmetic
loss, or an origin/position outside loaded legal world bounds closes without a
child. P9 never force-loads a chunk.

The hard caps are one entity/permit per accepted cast and per SkillInstance, 16 per
player, and 128 per server. Both an adapter-owned reservation and a transferred
entity occupy the same logical slot; transfer does not increment counts. Cap checks
and reservations occur before P6/world mutation. `max + 1` rejects without spawn,
child, mana, or presentation. Platform entity tracking remains the existence and
location truth. P5 owns one bounded active-permit index, exactly
`Map<UUID, RuntimeProjectileContinuationPermit>`, keyed by permit UUID and capped at
128. Each value is the sole permit object already containing the bound token,
dimension, planned entity UUID, owner identity, deadline, state, and pending/event
coordinates; there is no parallel scalar cleanup record. The index is an authority
and cleanup index, not a scheduler or second entity truth, and is never exposed to
the entity.

### 63.16 Persistence, reload, restart, and owner invalidation

The projectile and permit have zero persistent bytes and zero custom gameplay sync
bytes. The entity's ordinary platform type, transform, velocity, owner tracking, and
fixed item rendering are not reclassified as P9 custom gameplay state. No permit,
instance, queue, hit, trace, or revision lease is serialized.

Chunk unload, level unload, datapack/resource reload transition, orderly server
stop, the existing `RuntimeException` fault path, or process restart explicitly
invalidates every affected projectile and permit. `.noSave()` means the entity is
not restored. On ordinary cleanup P5 closes held/queued work, releases its instance
and exact revision lease after no work remains, and clears the bounded active index.
Startup never rebinds an entity, scans NBT for a permit, or replays a
cast/hit/damage. A fresh runtime server token makes every stale identity invalid.

The datapack reload edge is exact and introduces no locator. The existing
`Gramarye` instance registers a private `AddReloadListenerEvent` listener that calls
package-private `SkillRuntimeService.requestP9ReloadInvalidation()`. That operation
only sets the service's private-final `AtomicBoolean p9ReloadCloseRequested`; it may
run off the server thread and performs no gameplay mutation. P9 root admission
rejects while the bit is set. At an owning LOWEST `ServerTickEvent.Post` that
observes the bit, P5 does so *before* tick advance/drain and invokes its private
idempotent bounded P9 invalidation routine. It removes every committed or deferred
P9 event—both `CastGeometryExecutionDataV0` roots and
`ProjectileHitExecutionDataV0` children—then closes every active permit/entity;
non-P9 events remain untouched. An already-dispatching node 0 observes the bit at
the existing P5 pre-dispatch, P6 guard/open, and transfer checkpoints and cannot
publish or transfer a post-reload projectile. Post does not clear the bit. The
existing root also registers a private
`OnDatapackSyncEvent` listener. Only the full-reload event (`event.getPlayer() ==
null`) invokes package-private `SkillRuntimeService.completeP9Reload(MinecraftServer)`
on the server thread. Because reload completion can execute before another Post,
`completeP9Reload` synchronously ensures that same bounded invalidation before
clearing the bit; this is a no-op over already removed entries if an earlier Post
performed it. Per-player sync never clears the bit. On initial startup, the existing
`handleRuntimeStarted` clears a bit that may have been set by initial listener
construction only after asserting the new server slot, queue, instance map, and
active-permit index are fresh and empty; startup neither performs nor masks cleanup
of a prior live slot. P7 retains its own existing network admission gate; the P5 bit
is solely the active runtime-lifecycle owner and is neither persistent nor a second
definition truth.

An `Error`, including OOME, instead preserves the existing P5 §34 policy: the same
object propagates after no-intentional-allocation best-effort primitive
terminalization and queue/deferred/index clearing. Known P9 permit/entity gameplay
is invalidated or discarded where that bounded cleanup can do so, but the already
bounded P5 instance/lease graph may remain until `Stopped` or process exit. This A1
does not strengthen Error cleanup into an allocating lease close or catch-and-
continue path.

The owner must remain the exact authenticated caster object registered on the same
server, online, alive, and in the same dimension through hit claim and damage
commit. Before claim the entity requires
`server.getPlayerList().getPlayer(ownerUuid) == authenticatedCasterIdentity`; the
node-1 handoff repeats that identity comparison against both P6's actor and the
loaded exact projectile. Thus a same-UUID replacement object cannot revive the
cast. Logout, death, dimension change, or connection replacement closes the flight.
Slot changes and newer revisions do not revoke it, as fixed in §63.8. All
cleanup is idempotent, bounded by 128 active entries, and may not retain or suppress
a thrown `Throwable`.

### 63.17 Collision classification and inert claimed state

The platform NeoForge projectile-impact hook is evaluated first. A cancelled impact
does not claim, close, publish, damage, or present; bounded flight continues. A
noncancelled block hit, owner/self hit, nonliving entity hit, dead/unloaded/wrong
dimension target, illegal geometry, or invalid identity is terminal: close without
hit and discard, with no node 1. The P9 override does not invoke a block's vanilla
`onProjectileHit` world-mutation path. This slice does not grant block effects.

The first noncancelled loaded `LivingEntity` collision other than the owner captures
the exact finite platform collision position and normalizes the finite nonzero
movement segment actually supplied to that tick's sole platform sweep, after any
final 64-block range clamp. That normalized segment is the only hit direction
source. It is never the target-center vector, the post-sweep drag/gravity velocity,
or an inert/zero velocity. It is encoded using the same Q15 range and
`StrictMath.rint` ties-to-even rule as §63.7; an all-zero/nonfinite result is
invalid. The
immutable entity-created candidate and P5-created execution data are exact:

```java
record ProjectileHitCandidateV0(
        UUID projectileId,
        UUID targetId,
        ResourceLocation dimension,
        double hitX,
        double hitY,
        double hitZ,
        int directionXQ15,
        int directionYQ15,
        int directionZQ15) {}

record ProjectileHitExecutionDataV0(
        UUID permitId,
        UUID projectileId,
        SourceFamilyKey sourceFamily,
        int sourceDerivationDepth,
        ResourceLocation dimension,
        UUID targetId,
        double hitX,
        double hitY,
        double hitZ,
        int directionXQ15,
        int directionYQ15,
        int directionZQ15) implements RuntimeExecutionData {}
```

Both compact constructors are package-private, pure, and enforce nonnull/nonzero
IDs, §63.7's static coordinate domain, and legal nonzero Q15. The P5-created record
also requires the active nonzero permit ID, exact family, and
`sourceDerivationDepth=0`. Its target/dimension/projectile scalars must agree with
the loaded P5 `RuntimeTarget` and entity at claim and again at node-1 commit. The
candidate never contains a permit ID, source family, reference, token, EventId, or
depth.

The entity latch and P5 permit claim form two independent one-shot checks. If P5
accepts, the entity enters `CLAIMED_PENDING_DAMAGE`: it becomes inert, sets velocity
to zero, disables gravity, rejects all later collision callbacks, and remains loaded
only until the queued node 1 reaches any terminal. It is not discarded immediately.
This is an explicit correction to RO1's proposed immediate-discard wording: a later
queued damage commit must resolve the exact same projectile for
`indirectMagic(projectile, caster)`. Keeping the inert entity is the narrow way to
make those two RO1 recommendations coherent. It never sweeps again and cannot claim
a second target.

If P5 refuses the claim, the entity closes and discards immediately. If the inert
entity unloads or is removed before node 1 commits, damage fails closed and P5
terminal cleanup closes the permit. On every non-Error node-1 outcome—match failure,
guard rejection, target invalidation, commit false, commit true, queue cancellation,
or `RuntimeException`—a non-throwing finally-style owner cleanup discards the entity
and closes the permit without masking the original outcome. On `Error`, the same
object propagates after only the no-intentional-allocation best effort in §63.16;
known entity/permit gameplay is invalidated where possible, while bounded P5
instance/lease retention until `Stopped` remains legal.

### 63.18 Real damage and exactly-once meaning

Node 1 inherits the root `PlayerOrigin`; P6's actor is the original authenticated
caster. It may target only the exact loaded living target captured by the accepted
hit, on the same server and dimension, still alive, and not the caster. The commit
also resolves the exact loaded `gramarye:starter_projectile` UUID and requires its
package-visible caster witness to match the exact P6 actor. P5—not the entity or
handoff—revalidates the indexed CLAIMED_PENDING_DAMAGE permit/current-child binding
at the pre-dispatch and three guard checkpoints fixed in §63.12. Failure of any
revalidation returns or propagates the applicable closed rejection without a
`hurt` call; there is no entity/service/late-Opened capability getter or
latest-entity fallback.

Canonical magnitude must divide evenly by 1000. Exactly 4000 abstract units becomes
the finite float `4.0F`; invalid remainder, overflow, nonfinite conversion, or value
outside existing P6 bounds rejects rather than rounds or clamps. The sole call is:

```text
target.hurt(serverLevel.damageSources().indirectMagic(projectile, caster), 4.0F)
```

The platform's ordinary damage event, PvP, team/friendly-fire, spawn-protection,
shield, invulnerability-frame, reduction, and absorption decisions are not bypassed.
`hurt == false` means `NOT_APPLIED`, no applied fact, and no HIT. `hurt == true`
means `APPLIED` and exactly one HIT fact even when absorption makes raw health delta
zero. The unperturbed acceptance case separately proves an unarmored target with no
absorption loses exactly 4.0 health points. There is no retry, second damage source,
custom `DamageType`, durable crash exactly-once claim, or compensation after an
uncertain/accepted world mutation.

### 63.19 Mana, cooldown, and recast policy

Node 0 cost is exactly 0; node 1 cost is exactly 0; skill cooldown is exactly 0
ticks. Cost 0 literally performs no ManaTransactionService call and constructs no
account mutation, receipt, escrow, debit, refund, or cross-tick value. Node 0 and
node 1 are independent P6 invocations; no receipt or account object crosses the
projectile lifetime.

The fresh default balance of zero can therefore execute the canonical slice. A
future noncanonical positive-cost action continues to follow existing P6 debit and
same-call compensation rules, but it is not this P9 product. A successful spawn that
later misses or fails damage is never refunded. Presentation failure never changes
mana or retries gameplay. Existing P7 sequence/token-bucket controls plus the P9
1/16/128 active caps are the complete P9 recast bound; no regeneration, funding,
cooldown Store, login grant, or economy rule is introduced.

### 63.20 P8 applied-fact mapping and presentation isolation

Only P6 applied truth reaches P8 through the existing call-scoped
`P8AppliedFactHandoff`:

- successful node-0 spawn (`addFreshEntity == true`) maps the exact
  `gramarye:active_cast` event to one `CAST_RELEASE` offer;
- successful node-1 damage (`hurt == true`) maps the exact
  `gramarye:effect_hit` event to one real `HIT` offer;
- every `NOT_APPLIED`, reject, cancellation, false platform result, or precommit
  failure maps to no CAST_RELEASE/HIT offer.

The historical controlled P8 HIT source remains intact and is not evidence of P9
damage. Reserved P8 `PROJECTILE_SPAWN` is not used; standard entity tracking and the
client-only renderer display the projectile without a duplicate presentation truth.

CAST_RELEASE position/direction are copied from the node-0 frozen
`CastGeometryExecutionDataV0`. HIT position/direction are copied from the accepted
hit snapshot in `ProjectileHitExecutionDataV0`, and recipient/target identities are
the exact resolved server target. P8 must not re-read the actor, target, entity
position, or look after queue delay. Each offer still captures one immutable §62
catalog snapshot, then follows all existing profile, generation, recipient, budget,
packet, sequencing, degradation, and client lifecycle rules.

Missing/disabled profiles, budget drop, degradation, absent recipients, local
submission without delivery acknowledgement, client rendering failure, and an
observer `RuntimeException` cannot change already finalized spawn, damage, or mana
truth and cannot create a gameplay retry. The existing observer boundary catches
that `RuntimeException`, records its fixed bounded diagnostic, and drops
presentation while ordinary child/lease/cleanup progression continues. `Error` is
not caught: it cannot roll back an already finalized spawn or damage or fabricate a
retry, but the same object propagates into the existing P5 fault path and may
terminate future hit/damage progression; bounded instance/lease retention follows
§63.16 and existing P5 §34 until `Stopped`.

The following single table is authoritative for P9. “Inherited” means P9 consumes
